17:32: God Almighty says, And We sent Lot or its meaning is And remember Lot when he said to his people and Lot is the son of Haran bin Azar and he is the nephew of Abraham the friend of God, peace be upon them, and he had believed with Abraham, peace be upon him, and migrated with him to the land of Ash-Sham, so God sent him to the people of Sodom and the surrounding villages, calling them to God Almighty and commanding them to do good and forbidding them from what they were committing of sins, prohibitions and obscenities that they had invented and no one from the children of Adam or others had preceded them in, which is intercourse with males without females, and this is something that the children of Adam were not familiar with nor familiar with nor did it cross their minds, until the people of Sodom did it, may God's curses be upon them. Amr ibn Dinar said about his statement, No one in the worlds has preceded you with it, he said: No male has copulated with another male until the people of Lot. Al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik, the Umayyad Caliph who built the Great Mosque of Damascus, said: If God Almighty had not told us the story of the people of Lot, I would not have thought that a male would mount another male. That is why Lot, peace be upon him, said to them, Do you commit such immorality as no one in the worlds has preceded you with? Indeed, you approach men with desire instead of women. That is, you have turned away from women and what your Lord created for you from them to men. This is extravagance and ignorance on your part because he put the thing in the wrong place. That is why he said to them in the other verse, These are my daughters, if you are to do so. So he directed them to their women, but they apologized to him by saying that they did not desire them. “They said, ‘Indeed, you know that we have no right to your daughters, and indeed, you know what we want. ’” That is, you know that we have no interest in women or desire, and indeed, you know what we want from your guests. The commentators mentioned that the men had become satisfied with each other, and their women had also become satisfied with each other. They also dispensed with each other. God Almighty says, forbidding His servants from adultery, from approaching it, and from mixing with its causes and motives: “And do not come near adultery. Indeed, it is ever an immorality” meaning a great sin and an evil way meaning an evil path and course. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun narrated to us, Salim bin Aamer narrated to us on the authority of Abu Umamah, “A young man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to commit adultery. The people turned to him and rebuked him, and said: Stop, stop. He said: Come closer. So he came close to him, and he said: Sit down. So he sat down. He said: Would you like it for your mother? He said: No, by God, may God make me your ransom. He said: Nor do people like it for their mothers. He said: Would you like it for your daughter? He said: No, by God, O Messenger of God, may God make me your ransom. He said: Nor do people like it for their daughters. He said: Would you like it for your sister? He said: No, by God, may God make me your ransom. He said: Nor do people like it for their sisters. He said: Would you like it for your aunt? He said: No, by God, O Messenger of God, may God make me your ransom. He said: Nor do people like it for their aunts. He said: Would you like it for your maternal aunt? He said: No, by God, O Messenger of God, may God make me your ransom. He said: Nor do people like it for their maternal aunts. He said: Then he put his hand on him and said: O God, forgive his sin, purify his heart, and protect his private parts. He said: After that, the young man did not pay attention to anything. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya said: Ammar bin Nasr told us, Baqiyah told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Maryam, on the authority of Al-Haitham bin Malik Al-Ta’i, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is no sin after polytheism greater in the sight of God than a drop of sperm that a man places in a womb that is not permissible for him.”
17:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Isra, which is Meccan Imam, Hafiz, and Master Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Bukhari said: Adam bin Abi Iyas told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Abdur-Rahman bin Yazid, who heard Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, say about Bani Israel, Al-Kahf, and Maryam 19:They are among the first to be freed, and they are from my lineage. And Imam Ahmad said: Abdur-Rahman told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Marwan Abu Lubaba, who heard Aisha say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would fast until we would say he did not want to break his fast, and he would break his fast until we would say he did not want to fast, and he would recite Bani Israel and Az-Zumar every night.” In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty glorifies Himself and magnifies His status, for His ability to do what no one else can do. There is no god but Him and no Lord but Him. Who took His servant by night meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from al-Masjid al-Haram meaning the mosque of Mecca to al-Masjid al-Aqsa which is Jerusalem in Ilya, the source of the prophets since Abraham, peace be upon him. For this reason, they all gathered for Him there, and He led them in prayer in their neighborhood and home. This indicates that He is the greatest Imam and the foremost leader, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him and them all. And the Almighty’s saying: Whose surroundings We have blessed meaning the crops and fruits that We might show him meaning Muhammad of Our signs meaning the great things. As God Almighty said: He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord. We will mention from that what the Sunnah has reported from the hadiths about him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God Almighty’s saying: Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. That is, He hears the words of His servants, their believers and their disbelievers, their truth-tellers and their deniers, and He sees them, so He gives each of them what he deserves in this world and the hereafter. Imam Abu Abdullah Al-Bukhari said: Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah told me, Sulayman - he is the son of Bilal - told us on the authority of Sharik bin Abdullah who said: “I heard Anas bin Malik say on the night of the Isra’ of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the mosque of the Kaaba: Three men came to him before revelation came to him while he was sleeping in the Sacred Mosque. The first of them said: Which one is he? The middle one said: He is the best of them. The last of them said: Take the best of them. That night happened and he did not see them until they came to him another night in what his heart sees and his eye sleeps but his heart does not sleep - and that is how the prophets sleep, their eyes do not sleep - and they did not speak to him until they carried him and placed him at the well of Zamzam. Gabriel took charge of him from among them and Gabriel split open the space between his throat and his loins until he finished with his chest and his stomach. He washed him with Zamzam water with his hand until his stomach was cleansed. Then he was brought a golden basin in which there was a golden bowl filled with faith and wisdom and he filled his chest and his veins with it - meaning the veins.” Then he closed it and ascended with him to the lowest heaven, and knocked on one of its doors. The people of heaven called out to him: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad is with me. They said: Has he been sent to him? He said: Yes. They said: Then welcome to him and hello. The people of heaven rejoice at his arrival. The people of heaven do not know what God intends for him on earth until He informs them. Then he found Adam in the lowest heaven, and Gabriel said to him: This is your father Adam, greet him. So he greeted him and Adam responded to him and said: Welcome and hello to my son, what an excellent son you are. Then he was in the lowest heaven with two rivers flowing. He said: What are these two rivers, O Gabriel? He said: These are the Nile and the Euphrates, their source. Then he went with him into the heaven and saw another river with a palace of pearls and emeralds. He struck it with his hand and saw that it was the most fragrant musk. He said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is Al-Kawthar which your Lord has hidden for you. Then he ascended with him to the second heaven and the angels said to him the same as the first angels had said to him: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: Welcome to him, then he ascended with him to the third heaven and they said to him the same as the first and second, then he ascended with him to the fourth heaven and they said to him the same, then he ascended with him to the fifth heaven and they said to him the same, then he ascended with him to the sixth heaven and they said to him the same, then he ascended with him to the seventh heaven and they said to him the same, each heaven has prophets whom he named and I remembered from them Idris in the second and Aaron in the fourth and another in the fifth whose name I did not remember, and Abraham in the sixth and Moses in the seventh with the preference of the speech of God Almighty, then Moses said: O Lord, I did not think that anyone would be raised above me, then he ascended with him above that with what no one knows except God Almighty, until he came to the Lote Tree of the Limit, and the Almighty, the Lord of Majesty, approached and came close, until he was two bow lengths away from him or nearer, then God revealed to him among what He revealed fifty prayers upon your nation every day and night, then he descended with him until he reached Moses and Moses detained him and said: O Muhammad, what did your Lord enjoin upon you? He said: I was entrusted with fifty prayers every day and night. He said: Your nation cannot do that, so go back and let your Lord make it easier for you and for them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to Gabriel as if he was consulting him about that, and Gabriel indicated that yes, if you wish. So he went with him to the Almighty, the Most High, and said while he was in his place: O Lord, lighten it for us, for my nation cannot do this. So He reduced ten prayers from him, then he returned to Moses and held him back. Moses kept returning him to his Lord until it became five prayers. Then Moses held him back at the fifth and said: O Muhammad, by God, the Children of Israel tried to seduce my people with something less than this, but they became weak and abandoned it. Your nation is weaker in bodies, hearts, bodies, sight, and hearing. So go back and let your Lord lighten it for you. All this while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to Gabriel to advise him, and Gabriel did not dislike that, so He lifted him up at the fifth and said: O Lord, my nation is weak in bodies, hearts, hearing, sight, and bodies, so lighten it for us. The Almighty, the Most High, said: O Muhammad. He said: At your service and at your pleasure. He said: Verily, My word will not be changed, as I have enjoined upon you in the Mother of the Book. So every good deed is worth ten like it, so they are fifty in the Mother of the Book, and they are five for you. So he returned to Moses and said: How did you do? He said: He made it easy for us. He gave us for every good deed ten like it. Moses said: By God, I tried to seduce the Children of Israel with something less than that, but they abandoned it. So return to your Lord, and He may make it easy for you as well. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Moses, by God, I feel shy before my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, about what I have differed with. He said: Then descend in the name of God. He said: And he woke up while he was in the Sacred Mosque. This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it in the Book of Monotheism, and he narrated it in the description of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Uways, on the authority of his brother Abu Bakr Abdul Hamid, on the authority of Sulayman bin Bilal. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Harun bin Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Sulayman, who said: So he added and subtracted, and brought forward and delayed. It is as Muslim said, for Sharik bin Abdullah bin Abi Namir was confused in this hadith and his memory was bad and he did not control it, as will be explained, God willing, in the other hadiths. Some of them consider this a dream, in preparation for what happened after that, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said in the hadith of Sharik: An addition that he alone transmitted, according to the view of those who claim that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw God Almighty, meaning His statement, Then He drew near, the Compeller, the Lord of Majesty, and He came nearer * and was two bow lengths away or even nearer. He said: The statement of Aisha, Ibn Masoud, and Abu Hurairah in interpreting these verses as meaning that he saw Gabriel is more correct. What Al-Bayhaqi may God have mercy on him said in this matter is the truth, for Abu Dharr said: O Messenger of God, have you seen your Lord? He said: Light, how can I see Him? And in another narration: I saw a light. Narrated by Muslim. And his statement: Then he drew near and came closer refers to Gabriel, peace be upon him, as is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, and on the authority of Ibn Masoud. It is also in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurairah. And no one among the Companions is known to have disagreed with them in interpreting this verse in this way. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Thabit al-Banani told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was brought al-Buraq, which is a white animal larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, placing its hoof where it reaches its end. I mounted it and it took me until I reached the Holy House. I tied the animal to the ring where the prophets are tied, then I entered and prayed two rak’ahs in it. Then I came out and Gabriel came to me with a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk. I chose the milk, and Gabriel said: You have chosen the fitrah. He said: Then I was taken up to the lowest heaven, and Gabriel asked for the opening. It was said to him: Who are you? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to? He said: He has been sent to. So it was opened for us and there I was Adam, who welcomed me and prayed for my well-being. Then we were taken up to the second heaven, and Gabriel asked for the opening. It was said to him: Who are you? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to? He said: He has been sent to.” Then he opened for us and there I was my cousins, John and Jesus, they welcomed me and prayed for my well-being. Then he ascended with me to the third heaven. Gabriel asked for the door to be opened and it was said: Who are you? He said: Gabriel. It was asked: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was asked: Has he been sent for? He said: Has he been sent for? Then it was opened for us and there I was Joseph, peace be upon him, and he had been given half of his beauty. He welcomed me and prayed for my well-being. Then he ascended with us to the fourth heaven. Gabriel asked for the door to be opened and it was said: Who are you? He said: Gabriel. It was asked: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was asked: Has he been sent for? He said: Has he been sent for? Then it was opened for us and there I was Idris. He welcomed me and prayed for my well-being. Then God the Almighty says: {And We raised him to a high station}. Then he ascended with us to the fifth heaven. Gabriel asked for the door to be opened and it was said: Who are you? Gabriel said. It was asked: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was asked: Has he been sent for? He said: Has he been sent for? Then it was opened for us and there I was Aaron. He welcomed me and prayed for my well-being. Then he ascended with us to the sixth heaven. Gabriel asked for the door to be opened and it was said: Who are you? Gabriel said: It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to him? He said: He has been sent to him. So the gate was opened for us and there I was with Moses, peace be upon him. He welcomed me and prayed for my well-being. Then he ascended with us to the seventh heaven. Gabriel asked for the gate to be opened. It was said: Who are you? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to him? He said: He has been sent to him. So the gate was opened for us and there I was with Abraham, peace be upon him, leaning against the Frequented House, and there seventy thousand angels enter it every day and they do not return to it. Then he took me to the Lote Tree of the Limit and there its leaves were like the ears of elephants and its fruit was like large jars. But when what covered it from the command of God covered it, it changed, and none of God’s creation can describe its beauty. He said: Then God revealed to me what He revealed, and He imposed upon me fifty prayers every day and night. Then I went down until I reached Moses. He said: What did your Lord impose upon your nation? I said: Fifty prayers every day and night. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it for your nation, for your nation cannot bear that, and I have tested the Children of Israel and experienced them. He said: So I went back to my Lord and said: O Lord, lighten it for my nation. So He removed five from me. Then I went down until I reached Moses. He said: What did you do? I said, He has reduced five from me. He said, Your nation cannot bear that, so go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce it for your nation. He said, “I kept going back and forth between my Lord and Moses, and He reduced five by five from me until He said, ‘O Muhammad, there are five prayers every day and night, and for every prayer ten, so that is fifty prayers. Whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, a good deed will be recorded for him, and if he knows it, ten will be recorded for him. Whoever intends to do a bad deed but does not know it, it will not be recorded for him, and if he does it, one bad deed will be recorded for him. ’ So I went down until I reached Moses and informed him, and he said, “Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce it for your nation, for your nation cannot bear that.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I have gone back to my Lord until I felt ashamed. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Shaiban ibn Farukh on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah with this chain of transmission, and it is more authentic than the chain of transmission of Sharik. Al-Bayhaqi said: In this context there is evidence that the Mi'raj was on the night of the Night Journey, peace and blessings be upon him, from Mecca to the Holy House in Jerusalem, and what he said is the truth about which there is no doubt or uncertainty. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, “That the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was brought al-Buraq on the night of the Night Journey, saddled and bridled, for him to ride, but he found it difficult, so Gabriel said to him: What makes you do this? By God, no one more honorable to God than him has ever ridden you?” He said: Then sweat heavily. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ishaq ibn Mansur, on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, and he said it is strange, and we do not know it except from his hadith. Ahmad also said: Abu Al-Mughira told us, Safwan told us, Rashid bin Saeed and Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubair told me on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When I was taken up to my Lord, the Almighty, I passed by people who had nails of copper with which they scratched their faces and chests. I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are the ones who eat the flesh of people and slander them.” Abu Dawud included it on the authority of Safwan bin Amr, and from another chain of transmission that does not include Anas, so God knows best. He also said: Waki’ told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the night of my ascension, I passed by Moses, peace be upon him, standing and praying in his grave.” Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah from Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi and Thabit al-Bunani, both from Anas. Al-Nasa’i said: This is more authentic than the narration of Sulayman from Thabit from Anas. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Wahb ibn Baqiyyah told us, Khalid told us from al-Taymi from Anas who said: Some of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) told me that on the night of the Isra’, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed by Moses while he was praying in his grave. Abu Ya’la said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Arara told us, Mu’tamir told us from his father who said: I heard Anas that on the night of the Isra’, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed by Moses while he was praying in his grave. Anas said: He mentioned that he was carried on al-Buraq and tied up the beast or he said the horse. Abu Bakr said: Describe it to me. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is like this and that. He said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, had seen it. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Amr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Salamah bin Shabib told us, Saeed bin Mansour told us, Al-Harith bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Joni, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: While I was sleeping, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came and poked me between my shoulders. I went to a tree in which there were birds nesting. He sat in one of them and I sat in the other. It rose and ascended until it filled the two horizons. I turned my eyes and if I wanted to touch the sky, I could. I turned to Gabriel as if he were a soft blanket, and I recognized the superiority of his knowledge of God over me. A door from the doors of heaven was opened for me and I saw the greatest light. And before the veil, pearls and rubies fluttered, and what God willed to be revealed was revealed to me.” Then he said: We do not know that anyone narrated this hadith except Anas, and we do not know that anyone narrated it from Abu Imran Al-Joni except Al-Harith bin Ubaid, and he was a famous man from the people of Basra. Al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Dala’il on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Qadi on the authority of Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaim on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Husayn, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Mansur, and he mentioned it with his chain of transmission likewise, then he said, and someone else said in this hadith at the end of it, And before me, or he said before the veil, the pearls and rubies fluttered. Then he said, “This is how al-Harith ibn Ubayd narrated it, and Hammad ibn Salamah narrated it on the authority of Abu Imran al-Jawni on the authority of Muhammad ibn Umair ibn Uttarid, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in a group of his companions when Gabriel came to him and poked him in the back, so he went with him to the tree in which was something like a bird’s nest. He sat in one of them and Gabriel sat in the other, so it grew with us until it reached the horizon, and if I extended my hand to the sky I would reach it, so it was lowered by a cause and the light descended, and Gabriel fell unconscious as if he were a parasite, so I knew the superiority of my fear of Him over my fear, so a prophet was revealed to me: A king or a prophet, a servant, and to Paradise you are not, so he gestured to me.” Gabriel, while he was lying down, said: I said: No, but a prophet and a servant. I said: And if this is true, it requires that it occurred on a different night than the Night Journey, because the Holy House or the ascension to heaven was not mentioned in it, so it occurred on a different night than what we are in. And God knows best. Al-Bazzar also said: Amr bin Isa told us, Abu Bahr told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Anas that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. And this is strange. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Yunus told us, `Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, Ya`qub ibn `Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Hashim ibn `Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: “When Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with al-Buraq, it seemed as if it had moved its tail. Gabriel said to it, ‘Slow down, O al-Buraq, for by God, no one like it has ridden you.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked and saw an old woman on the side of the road. He said, ‘What is this, O Gabriel?’ He said, ‘Go, O Muhammad.’ He said, ‘So he walked as long as God willed him to walk. Then something called him away from the road, so he said, ‘Come, O Muhammad.’ Gabriel said to him, ‘Go, O Muhammad.’ He walked as long as God willed him to walk. He said, ‘A group of God’s creation met him and said, ‘Peace be upon you O First, peace be upon you O Last, peace be upon you, O Gatherer.’ Gabriel said to him, ‘Return the greeting, O Muhammad.’ He returned the greeting. Then he met him a second time and said to him the same as the first time, then a third time likewise, until he reached the Holy House in Jerusalem. He offered him wine, water, and milk, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took them.” And Gabriel said to him: You have hit the mark, and if you had drunk water you and your nation would have drowned, and if you had drunk wine you and your nation would have been lost. Then Adam was sent to him, and the prophets after him, peace be upon them, and the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, led them in prayer that night. Then Gabriel said to him: As for the old woman whom you saw on the side of the road, there is nothing left of this world except what remained of the life of that old woman. As for the one who wanted you to lean towards him, that is the enemy of God, Satan, who wanted you to lean towards him. As for those who greeted you, they are Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, peace be upon them. And this is how Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dalil Al-Nubuwwah from the hadith of Ibn Wahb. And in some of its wording there is something strange and odd. Another way On the authority of Anas bin Malik, and it contains a very strange and strange narration. In the Sunan of al-Nasa’i and al-Mujtaba, and I did not see it in al-Kabeer, he said: Amr bin Hisham told us, Mukhallad, he is the son of al-Husayn, told us on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz, Yazid bin Abi Malik told us, Anas bin Malik told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was brought a beast larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, its stride reaching the end of its eye, so I rode it and Gabriel, peace be upon him, was with me. I set off and he said, ‘Dismount and pray,’ so I prayed. He said, ‘Do you know where you prayed?’ I prayed in Taiba, and the immigrants went to it. Then he said, ‘Dismount and pray,’ so I prayed. He said, ‘Do you know where you prayed?’ I prayed at Mount Sinai, where God spoke to Moses. Then he said, ‘Dismount and pray,’ so I prayed. He said, ‘Do you know where you prayed?’ I prayed in Bethlehem, where Jesus, peace be upon him, was born. Then I entered Jerusalem and gathered the prophets, peace be upon them, for me, so Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought me forward until I led them in prayer. Then he ascended with me to the lowest heaven, and in it was Adam, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me to the second heaven, and in it were the two sons of the maternal uncle, Jesus.” And John, peace be upon them, then he ascended with me to the third heaven and there was Joseph, peace be upon him, then he ascended with me to the fourth heaven and there was Aaron, peace be upon him, then he ascended with me to the fifth heaven and there was Idris, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me to the sixth heaven, and in it was Moses, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me to the seventh heaven, and in it was Abraham, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me above seven heavens and I came to Sidrat al-Muntaha, and a mist covered me, so I fell down in prostration, and it was said to me, On the day I created the heavens and the earth, I imposed upon you and your nation fifty prayers, so perform them you and your nation. So I returned with that until he ordered Moses, peace be upon him, and he said, What did your Lord impose upon your nation? I said, Fifty prayers. He said, You will not be able to perform them, neither you nor your nation, so go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce them. So I returned to my Lord, and He reduced them for me by ten. Then I came to Moses, and he ordered me to go back, so I went back, and He reduced them for me by ten. Then I was returned to five prayers. He said, Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce them, for He imposed two prayers on the Children of Israel, but they did not perform them. So I returned to my Lord, the Almighty, and asked Him to reduce them, and He said, On the day I created the heavens and the earth, I imposed upon you and your nation fifty prayers, so five for fifty, so perform them you and your nation. He said, So I knew that it was from God, the Almighty. And the matter became clear to me, so I returned to Moses, peace be upon him, and he said, Go back. So I knew that it was from God Almighty, the Almighty, the Majestic, and it was clear - meaning, it was inevitable - so I did not go back.” Another path Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Khalid bin Yazid bin Abi Malik told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: “When the night of the Isra’ of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Jerusalem was, Gabriel came to him with a beast bigger than a donkey and smaller than a mule. Gabriel carried him on it, its hoof ending where its edge ended. When he reached Jerusalem and reached the place called the Gate of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, he came to the stone that was there, and Gabriel poked it with his finger and pierced it, then tied it up and climbed up. When they were level in the courtyard of the mosque, Gabriel said, O Muhammad, have you asked your Lord to show you the houris? He said, Yes. He said, So go to those women and greet them while they were sitting to the left of the rock. He said: So I went to them and greeted them and they returned my greeting, so I said, Who are you? They said: We are the best and most beautiful women of a righteous people who were pure and were not known. They stayed and did not move, and they remained immortal and were not…” They die, he said, then I left and it was not long before many people gathered, then a muezzin called the prayer and the prayer was established, he said so we stood in rows waiting for someone to lead us, then Gabriel, peace be upon him, took my hand and made me come forward and I led them in prayer, and when I left Gabriel said: O Muhammad, do you know who prayed behind you? He said - I said - No - he said every prophet whom God Almighty sent prayed behind you. He said: Then Gabriel took me by the hand and ascended with me to the heaven. When we reached the door, he asked to be let in. They said: Who are you? He said: I am Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to him? He said: Yes. They opened it for him and said: Welcome to you and to those with you. He said: When he was on its back, there was Adam in it. Gabriel said to me: O Muhammad, will you not greet your father Adam? He said: I said: Yes. So I went to him and greeted him and he responded and said: Welcome to my righteous son and righteous prophet. He said: Then he ascended with me to the second heaven and asked to be let in. They said: Who are you? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to him? He said: Yes. They opened it for him and he said: Welcome to you and to those with you. There was Jesus and his cousin John, peace be upon them. He said: Then he ascended with me to the third heaven and asked to be let in. They said: Who are you? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to him? He said, Yes. So they opened for him and said, Welcome to you and to those with you. And therein was Joseph, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me to the fourth heaven and asked to be admitted. They said, Who are you? He said, Gabriel. They said, And who is with you? He said, Muhammad. They said, Has he been sent to him? He said, Yes. So they opened for him and said, Welcome to you and to those with you. And therein was Idris, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me to the fifth heaven and Gabriel asked to be admitted. They said, Who are you? He said, And who is with you? He said, Muhammad. They said, Has he been sent to him? He said, Yes. So they opened for him and said, Welcome to you and to those with you. And therein was Aaron, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me to the sixth heaven, and Gabriel asked for the door to be opened. They said, Who are you? Gabriel said, And who is with you? He said, Muhammad. They said, Has he been sent to you? He said, Yes. They opened it and said, Welcome to you and to those with you. And there was Moses, peace be upon him, in it. Then he ascended with me to the seventh heaven, and Gabriel asked for the door to be opened. They said, Who are you? Gabriel said, And who is with you? He said, Muhammad. They said, Has he been sent to you? He said, Yes. They opened it for him and said, Welcome to you and to those with you. And there was Abraham, peace be upon him, in it. Gabriel said, O Muhammad, will you not greet your father Abraham? I said, Yes. So I went to him and greeted him, and he returned my greeting and said, Welcome to my righteous son and righteous prophet. Then he took me on the seventh heaven until he reached a river with tents of pearls, rubies, and emeralds, and on it was a green bird, the softest bird I have ever seen. I said, O Gabriel, this bird is soft. He said, O Muhammad, I eat it softer than it. Then he said, O Muhammad, do you know what river this is? I said, No. He said, This is the Kauthar that God has given you. And in it were vessels of gold and silver, flowing over stones of rubies and emeralds, its water whiter than milk. He said, "So I took a vessel of gold from its vessel, scooped up some of that water and drank it. It was sweeter than honey and had a stronger scent than musk." Then he took me until I reached the tree, and a cloud covered me in which were all colors, and Gabriel rejected me, and I fell down prostrating to God Almighty, and God said to me: O Muhammad, on the day I created the heavens and the earth, I made fifty prayers obligatory upon you and your nation, so perform them, you and your nation. - He said - Then the cloud cleared from me, and Gabriel took my hand, and I quickly turned away. I came to Abraham, but he did not say anything. Then I came to Moses, and he said: What did you do, O Muhammad? I said: My Lord made fifty prayers obligatory upon me and my nation. He said: You will not be able to do it, nor will your nation, so go back to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it for you. So I quickly went back until I reached the tree, and the cloud covered me and Gabriel rejected me. I fell down in prostration and said: My Lord, You have enjoined upon me and my nation fifty prayers, and neither I nor my nation will be able to do them, so lighten it for us. He said: I have reduced ten for you. He said: Then the cloud cleared and Gabriel took my hand. He said: "I quickly turned away until I came to Abraham, but he did not say anything to me. Then I came to Moses, who said: "What have you done, O Muhammad?" I said: "My Lord has reduced ten for me." He said: "Then forty prayers, neither you nor your nation will be able to do them. Go back to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it for you." He mentioned the hadith in the same way, up to five prayers, and five is fifty. Then Moses ordered him to go back and ask Him to lighten it, and he said: "I am shy before the Almighty." He said: Then he descended and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel: “Why did I not come to the people of heaven without them welcoming me and smiling at me except for one man, so I greeted him and he returned my greeting and welcomed me and did not smile at me. He said: O Muhammad, that is Malik, the keeper of Hell, he has not laughed since he was created, and if he had laughed at anyone he would have laughed at you.” He said: Then he rode away and was leaving. While he was on some of the road, a camel of the Quraysh passed by carrying food, among them was a camel with two buckets, a black bucket and a white bucket. When it came level with the camel, it was startled by it and turned around and that camel fell down and broke. Then he went on in the morning and told what had happened. When the polytheists heard what he said, they came to Abu Bakr and said: O Abu Bakr, do you want to know about your companion? He said that he came on this night a month’s journey and returned on the same night, so Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: If he said that, then he has spoken the truth, and we believe him in what is further than this, so we believe him based on the report from heaven. So the polytheists said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, What is the sign of what you say? He said: I passed by a camel of the Quraysh while it was in such and such a place, and the camels were frightened of us and turned around, and among them was a camel with two saddlebags, a black saddlebag and a white saddlebag, and it fell down and was broken. When the camel arrived, they asked them and they told them the story as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had told them, and from that Abu Bakr was named the truthful. They asked him and said: Were Moses and Jesus among those who came with you? He said: Yes. They said: Describe them to us. He said: As for Moses, he is a dark-skinned man as if he were from the men of Azd Oman, and as for Jesus, he is a man of medium build, with a reddish complexion, as if pearls were dripping from his hair. This is a context in which there are strange and amazing things. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammam told us: I heard Qatada narrating on the authority of Anas bin Malik that Malik bin Sa’sa’ah told him that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told them about the night he was taken on the Night Journey. He said: “While I was lying in al-Hateem - and Qatada may have said in al-Hijr - a man came to me and began to say to his companion, ‘The middle one among the three. ’ He said: ‘So he came to me and - I heard Qatada say - split - between this and this. ’ Qatada said: ‘So I said to al-Jarud, who was beside me: What does he mean? ’ He said: ‘From the opening of his throat to his hair. ’ And I heard him say: ‘From his hairline to his hair. ’ He said: ‘So he extracted my heart. ’ He said: ‘So I was brought a golden basin filled with faith and wisdom. ’ My heart was washed, then stuffed, then returned. ’ Then I was brought a beast, smaller than a mule and larger than a donkey, white. ’ Al-Jarud said: ‘Is it al-Buraq, O Abu Hamza? ’ He said: ‘Yes, its stride falls at its furthest point. ’ He said: ‘So I carried it and Gabriel, peace be upon him, took me until he brought me. ’” To the lowest heaven, so he asked for permission. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to him? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, and what a good coming he has been. He said: It was opened for us. When I reached the end, there was Adam, peace be upon him. He said: This is your father Adam, so greet him. I greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he ascended until he reached the second heaven and asked for permission. It was said: Who is this? Gabriel said: It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to him? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, and what a good coming he has been. He said: It was opened for us. When I reached the end, there was Jesus and John, and they were the sons of the maternal aunt. He said: These are John and Jesus, so greet them. I greeted them and they returned the greeting. Then they said: Welcome to the righteous brother and righteous prophet. Then he ascended until he reached the third heaven and asked for permission. It was said: Who is this? Gabriel said: It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to him? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, and what a good arrival he has come. He said: So it was opened for us. When I was finished, there was Joseph, peace be upon him. He said: This is Joseph. I greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he ascended until he reached the fourth heaven and asked for permission. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Or has he been sent to? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, and what a good arrival he has come. He said: So it was opened for us. When I was finished, there was Idris, peace be upon him. He said: This is Idris. I greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he ascended until he reached the fifth heaven and asked for permission. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Or has he been sent to? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, and what a good arrival he has come. So it was opened for us. When I reached it, there was Aaron, peace be upon him. He said: This is Aaron, so greet him. I greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he said: Welcome to the righteous brother and righteous prophet. He said: Then he ascended until he reached the sixth heaven and asked for permission. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Or has he been sent to? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, and what a good arrival he has come. So it was opened for us. When I reached it, there was Moses, peace be upon him. He said: This is Moses, so greet him. I greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he said: Welcome to the righteous brother and righteous prophet. He said: When I passed him, he cried. It was said to him: What makes you cry? He said: I cry because a boy was sent after me who will enter Paradise from his nation more than will enter it from my nation. He said: Then he ascended until he reached the seventh heaven and asked for permission. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Or has he been sent to him? He said, "Yes. It was said, Welcome to him, and what a good arrival he has come to." Then it was opened for us, and when I had finished, there was Abraham, peace be upon him. He said, "This is Abraham, so greet him." So I greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he said, "Welcome to the righteous brother and righteous prophet. He said, Then I was raised to the Lote Tree of the Limit, and its fruit was like the jars of Hajar, and its leaves were like the ears of elephants. He said, This is the Lote Tree of the Limit. He said, "And there were four rivers: two hidden rivers and two apparent rivers." I said, What is this, O Gabriel? He said, As for the hidden ones, they are two rivers in Paradise, and as for the apparent ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates. He said, Then I was raised to the Frequented House. Qatada said: Al-Hasan narrated to us on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he saw the Frequented House, which seventy thousand enter every day and then they do not return to it. Then he returned to the hadith of Anas, who said: “Then I was brought a vessel of wine, a vessel of milk, and a vessel of honey. He said: So I took the milk. He said: This is the nature upon which you and your nation are. He said: Then prayer was imposed upon me, fifty prayers every day. He said: So I descended until I came to Moses, and he said: What has your Lord imposed upon your nation? He said: I said: Fifty prayers every day. He said: Your nation cannot do fifty prayers, and I have experienced the people before you, and I have treated the Children of Israel with the utmost severity. So go back to your Lord and ask Him to make it easier for your nation. He said: So I went back and He reduced ten from me. He said: So I went back to Moses and he said: What have you been commanded? I said: Forty prayers every day. He said: Your nation cannot do forty prayers every day, and I have experienced the people before you and I have treated the Children of Israel with the utmost severity. So go back to your Lord and ask Him to make it easier for your nation.” He said: So I went back and He made ten more. I went back to Moses and he said: What have you been commanded to do? I said: I have been commanded to do thirty prayers. He said: Your nation cannot do thirty prayers each day. I have experienced the people before you and have dealt with the Children of Israel in the most severe way. So go back to your Lord and ask Him to make it easier for your nation. He said: So I went back and He made ten more. I went back to Moses and he said: What have you been commanded to do? I said: I have been commanded to do twenty prayers each day. He said: Your nation cannot do twenty prayers each day. I have experienced the people before you and have dealt with the Children of Israel in the most severe way. So go back to Moses and he said: What have you been commanded to do? I said, I have been commanded to perform ten prayers every day. He said, “Your nation cannot do ten prayers every day. I have experienced the people before you and dealt with the Children of Israel in the most severe manner. So go back to your Lord and ask Him to make it easier for your nation.” He said, So I went back and was commanded to perform five prayers every day. I went back to Moses and he said, What have you been commanded to do? He said, I have been commanded to perform five prayers every day. He said, “Your nation cannot do five prayers every day. I have experienced the people before you and dealt with the Children of Israel in the most severe manner. So go back to your Lord and ask Him to make it easier for your nation.” He said, I have asked my Lord until I felt ashamed, but I am satisfied and submit. So I carried out the task and a caller called out, I have fulfilled my obligation and made it easier for My servants. They both included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Qatadah in a similar manner. Al-Bukhari said: Yahya bin Bakir narrated to us, Al-Layth narrated to us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: Abu Dharr used to narrate that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The ceiling of my house was opened while I was in Mecca, and Gabriel came down and opened my chest, then washed it with Zamzam water. Then he brought a golden basin full of wisdom and faith, and poured it into my chest. Then he took my hand and ascended with me to the lowest heaven. When I reached the heaven, Gabriel said to the keeper of the heaven: Open. He said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. He said: Is there anyone with you? He said: Yes, with me is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Send for him? He said: Yes. When he opened, we ascended to the lowest heaven and there was a man sitting with black women on his right and black women on his left. If he looked to his right, he laughed and if he looked to his left, he cried. He said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous son. I said to Gabriel: Who is this? He said: This is Adam, and these black women on his right and on his left are the names of his children. The people on the right are the people of Paradise.” Anas said: “He mentioned that he found in the heavens Adam, Idris, Moses, Jesus, and Abraham, but he did not confirm their abodes except that he mentioned that he found Adam in the lowest heaven and Abraham in the sixth. Anas said: “When Gabriel and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by Idris, he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous brother. I said: Who is this? He said: Idris. Then I passed by Moses, and he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous brother. I said: Who is this? He said: This is Moses. Then I passed by Jesus, and he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous brother. I said: Who is this? He said: This is Jesus. Then I passed by Abraham, and he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous son. I said: Who is this?” He said: This is Ibrahim. Al-Zuhri said: Ibn Hazm informed me that Ibn Abbas and Abu Habbah Al-Ansari used to say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then he ascended with me until I reached a level where I could hear the scratching of the pens. Ibn Hazm and Anas bin Malik said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God enjoined fifty prayers upon my nation, so I returned with that until I passed by Moses, peace be upon him, and he said: What did God enjoin upon your nation? I said: He enjoined fifty prayers. Moses said: Then return to your Lord, for your nation cannot bear that. So I returned and He reduced half of it. I returned to Moses and I said: He reduced half of it. He said: Go back to your Lord, for your nation cannot bear that. So I returned and He reduced half of it. I returned to him and he said: Go back to your Lord, for your nation cannot bear that. I returned to him and he said: They are five and they are fifty. My word does not change. I returned to Moses and he said: Go back to your Lord. I said: I am ashamed before my Lord. Then he took me until he reached the Lote Tree of the Limit, and it was covered with colors I do not know what they are. Then I was brought into Paradise, and there were sides of pearls in it, and its soil was musk.” This is the wording of Al-Bukhari in the Book of Prayer, and he narrated it in the mention of the Children of Israel, in the Hajj, and in the hadiths of the prophets. From other chains of transmission on the authority of Yunus, and Muslim narrated it in his Sahih in the Book of Faith on his authority on the authority of Harmalah on the authority of Ibn Wahb on the authority of Yunus, similarly. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, who said: I said to Abu Dharr: If I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I would ask him. He said: What did you ask him? He said: I would ask him: Did he see his Lord? He said: I asked him, and he said: I saw Him as a light. How can I see Him? This is how it was narrated by Imam Ahmad. Muslim included it in his Sahih on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ‘Did you see your Lord?’ He said: ‘Light. How can I see Him.’” And on the authority of Muhammad bin Bashar, on the authority of Muadh bin Hisham: My father told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, who said: I said to Abu Dharr: If I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I would ask him. He said: What did you ask him about? He said: I would ask him: Did you see your Lord? Abu Dharr said: I asked, and he said: I saw a light. Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Muhammad Al-Masini told us, Anas bin Ayyad told us, Yunus bin Yazid told us, Ibn Shihab said: Anas bin Malik said: Abi bin Kaab used to narrate that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The ceiling of my house was opened while I was in Mecca, so Gabriel came down and opened my chest, then washed it with Zamzam water, then he brought a golden basin full of wisdom and faith, and poured it into my chest, then closed it, then he took my hand and ascended with me to the heavens. When he reached the lowest heaven, there was a man with black faces on his right and black faces on his left. When he looked to his right, he smiled, and when he looked to his left, he cried. He said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous son. I said to Gabriel: Who is this? He said: This is Adam, and these black faces on his right and left are the souls of his children. The people of his right are the people of Paradise, and the black faces on his left are the people of Hell. When he looked to his right, he laughed, and when he looked to his left, he said: Anas said: “He said: ‘He said: “He mentioned that he found Adam, Idris, Moses, Abraham, and Jesus in the heavens, but he did not confirm to me how their dwellings were, except that he mentioned that he found Adam, peace be upon him, in the lowest heaven, and Abraham in the sixth heaven. Anas said: ‘When Gabriel, peace be upon him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by Idris, he said: “Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous brother.” I said: Who is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is Idris. He said: “Then I passed by Moses, and he said: “Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous brother.” I said: Who is this? He said: Moses. Then I passed by Jesus, and he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous brother. I said: Who is this? He said: This is Jesus, son of Mary. He said: “Then I passed by Abraham, and he said: “Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous son.” I said: Who is this? He said: This is Abraham. Ibn Shihab said: Ibn Hazm told me that Ibn Abbas and Abu Habbah Al-Ansari used to say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then he ascended with me until I reached a level where I could hear the scratching of the pens.” Ibn Hazm and Anas bin Malik said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has imposed fifty prayers on my nation. He said: So I returned with that until I passed by Moses, and Moses said: What has your Lord imposed on your nation? I said: He imposed fifty prayers on them. Moses said to me: Go back to your Lord, for your nation cannot bear that. He said: So I went back to my Lord, and He reduced half of it. I went back to Moses and told him. He said: Go back to your Lord, for your nation cannot bear that. I went back and he said: They are five and they are fifty. My word does not change. He said: So I went back to Moses, and he said: Go back to your Lord. I said: I am ashamed before my Lord. He said: Then he took me until he came to the Lote Tree of the Limit. He said: It was covered with colors I do not know what they were. He said: Then I entered Paradise, and there were in it pearls and its soil was musk.” This is how Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated it in his father’s Musnad, and it is not in any of the six books. It was previously mentioned in the two Sahihs on the authority of Yunus on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Dharr, with a similar context, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Mutawakkil and Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told us, and the wording is his. They said: Abu Numailah told us, Al-Zubayr bin Junadah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Buraydah, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the night of my ascension came - he said - Gabriel came to the rock in the Holy House - he said - and put his finger in it and pierced it and tied Al-Buraq to it.” Then Al-Bazzar said: We do not know that it was narrated on the authority of Al-Zubayr bin Junadah except by Abu Numailah, and we do not know this hadith except on the authority of Buraydah. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the interpretation of his collection on the authority of Ya’qub bin Ibrahim Al-Dawraqi with it, and he said it is strange. Imam Ahmad said: Yaqub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Salih, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Salamah said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah narrating that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When the Quraysh denied me when I was taken on the Night Journey to Jerusalem, I stood in the Hijr and God showed me Jerusalem, so I began to tell them about its signs while I was looking at it. They included it in the two Sahihs through various chains of transmission on the authority of al-Zuhri with it. Al-Bayhaqi said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qadi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, al-Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duri told us, Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told us, my father told us, on the authority of Salih ibn Kaysan, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: I heard Saeed ibn al-Musayyab say: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached Jerusalem, he met Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, and two cups were brought to him: a cup of milk and a cup of wine. He looked at them, then took the cup of milk, and Gabriel said: You have found the truth, you have been guided to the natural disposition. If you had taken the wine, your nation would have been idle. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to Mecca and was informed that he had been taken on the Night Journey, and many people who had prayed with him were tempted.” Ibn Shihab said: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman said: So he prepared himself, or something similar, some people from Quraysh went to Abu Bakr and said: What do you think about your companion who claims that he came to Jerusalem and then returned to Mecca in one night? Abu Bakr said: Or did he say that? They said: Yes. He said: Then I bear witness that if he said that, he has spoken the truth. They said: So do you believe him if he comes to Ash-Sham in one night and then returns to Mecca before morning? He said: Yes, I believe him with more than that. I believe him with report from heaven. Abu Salamah said: That is why Abu Bakr As-Siddiq was named. Abu Salamah said: Then I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah may God be pleased with them both narrating that he heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: When the Quraysh denied me when I was taken on the Night Journey to Jerusalem, I stood in the Hijr and God showed me Jerusalem. I began to tell them about its signs while I was looking at it. Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr told us, Sulayman told us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish, who said: I came upon Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him, while he was talking about the night of the Isra’ Night Journey of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was saying: So they set off until they came to Jerusalem, but they did not enter it. I said: Rather, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered it that night and prayed in it. He said: What is your name, O Bald One? I know your face, but I do not know your name. I said: I am Zur ibn Hubaish. He said: How do you know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed in it that night? He said: I said: The Qur’an informs me of that. He said: So whoever recites the Qur’an, let him recite. I said: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa. He said: O Bald One, do you find that he prayed in it? I said: No. He said: By God, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not pray in it that night. If he had prayed in it, a prayer would have been prescribed for you in it just as a prayer in the Ancient House was prescribed for you. By God, they did not leave Al-Buraq until the gates of heaven were opened for them and they saw Paradise and Hell and the promise of the Hereafter together. Then they returned to their original state. He said: Then he laughed until I saw his molars. He said: And they tell him that he tied it up so that it could not escape from him, and that the Knower of the Unseen and the Seen made it subservient to him. I said: O servant of God, what is the beast of Al-Buraq? He said: A tall white beast, its stride is as far as the eye can see. Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi narrated it on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Asim on his authority. At-Tirmidhi and An-Nasa’i narrated it in their Tafsir on the authority of Asim, who is Ibn Abi An-Najud, on his authority. At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan. What Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him said and what others have confirmed from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about tying the beast to the ring, and about praying in Bayt Al-Maqdis, from what has come before and what will come, takes precedence over his statement. And God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said in the book of Evidences of Prophethood: Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Yaqoub told us, Abu Bakr Yahya bin Abi Talib told us, Abdul Wahhab bin Ata told us, Abu Muhammad Rashid Al-Hammani told us on the authority of Abu Harun Al-Abdi, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that his companions said to him: O Messenger of God, tell us about the night in which you were taken on the Night Journey. He said: God Almighty said: Glory be to Him who took His servant on a night journey Al-Masjid Al-Haram, the verse: He said: So tell them. He said: While I was sleeping in the evening in the Sacred Mosque, someone came to me and woke me up. I woke up and did not see anything. Then I saw a shadow, so I followed it with my eyes until I left the Sacred Mosque. Then I saw a beast that was more similar to these beasts of yours, these mules of yours, except that it had twitching ears. It was called Al-Buraq, and the prophets before me used to ride it. Its hoof would land as far as its sight could reach, so I rode it. While I was I was walking on it when a caller called me from my right: O Muhammad, look at me, I ask you, O Muhammad, look at me, I ask you, O Muhammad, look at me, I ask you. But I did not answer him and did not stand on it. While I was walking on it, a caller called me from my left: O Muhammad, look at me, I ask you. But I did not answer him and did not stand on it. While I was walking, I saw a woman with her arms uncovered and wearing every adornment that God had created. She said: O Muhammad, look at me, I ask you. But I did not turn to her and did not stand on it until I came to the Holy House, and I tied my mount to the ring to which the prophets used to tie them. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to me with two vessels: one of wine and the other of milk. I drank the milk and refused the wine. Gabriel said: You have chosen the natural disposition. If you had taken the wine, your nation would have been led astray. I said: God is Great, God is Great. Gabriel said: What do you see on your face? He said: So I said, while I was walking, a caller called me on my right: O Muhammad, wait for me, I am asking you, but I did not answer him or stand up for him. He said, That is the caller of the Jews. If you had answered him or stood up for him, your nation would have become Jews. He said: While I was walking, a caller called me on my left, saying: O Muhammad, wait for me, I am asking you, but I did not turn around or stand up for him. He said: That is the caller of the Christians. If you had answered him, your nation would have become Christians. He said: While I was walking, I saw a woman with her arms uncovered, wearing every adornment that God had created, saying: O Muhammad, wait for me, I am asking you, but I did not answer her or stand up for her. He said: That is the world. If you had answered her or stood up for her, your nation would have chosen the world over the Hereafter. He said: Then Gabriel and I entered the Holy House, and each of us prayed two rak'ahs. Then I came to the Mi'raj ascension by which the souls of the sons of Adam used to ascend. The creation has never seen a better ascension than this. Have you not seen a dead person when he squints his eyes ascending to the heavens? He squints his eyes ascending to the heavens out of amazement at the Mi'raj. He said: So Gabriel and I ascended, and there I saw an angel called Ismail, who is the master of the lowest heaven, and before him are seventy thousand angels, with each angel having a hundred thousand soldiers. He said: God the Almighty said: And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. Gabriel then opened the door of heaven. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to him? He said: Yes, and behold, I saw Adam as he was on the day God created him in His image, and behold, the souls of his believing descendants were presented to him, and he said: A good soul and a good soul, place them in the highest place. Then the souls of his wicked descendants were presented to him, and he said: A bad soul and a bad soul, place them in Sijjin. So I went on for a while and behold, I saw a hut on which there was dissected flesh, no one would approach it, and behold, I saw another hut on which there was flesh that had rotted and was rotting, and there were people eating from it. I said: O Gabriel, who are these? He said: These are from your nation who do what is forbidden and leave what is permissible. He said: Then I went on for a while and behold, I saw people whose lips were like the lips of camels. He said: Their mouths were opened and they took a sip of that hot coal, then something came out from their lower parts. I heard them crying out to God, the Almighty, so I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are from your nation. Those who devour the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming into their bellies fire, and they will burn in a Blaze. He said: Then I went on for a while, and there I saw women clinging to their breasts, and I heard them crying out to God Almighty. I said: O Gabriel, who are these women? He said: These are the adulterers of your nation. He said: Then I went on for a while, and there I saw people whose bellies were like houses. Whenever one of them got up, he would fall down and say: O God, do not establish the Hour. He said: They are on the path of the people of Pharaoh. He said: Then a traveler would come and trample them. He said: I heard them crying out to God. I said: O Gabriel, who are these? He said: These are from your nation. Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. He said: Then I went on for a while, and there I saw people whose flesh was being cut from their sides and they were feeding it to him, and it was said to him: Eat as you used to eat from the flesh of your brother. I said: O Gabriel, who are these? He said: These are the slanderers and backbiters of your nation. He said: Then we ascended to the second heaven, and there I saw a man who was the most beautiful of what God Almighty had created, and he excelled people in beauty, like the moon on the night of the full moon over all the other planets. I said: O Gabriel, who is this? He said: This is your brother Joseph, and with him are some of his people. So I greeted him and he greeted me back. Then we ascended to the third heaven, and it was opened, and there I saw Yahya and Jesus, peace be upon them, and with them were some of their people, so I greeted them and they greeted me. Then we ascended to the fourth heaven, and there I saw Idris, whom God had raised to a high place, so I greeted him and he greeted me. He said: Then we ascended to the fifth heaven, and there I saw Aaron, half of whose beard was white and half of it was black, his beard almost reaching his navel because of its length. I said: O Gabriel, who is this? He said: This is the beloved one among his people, this is Aaron bin Imran, and with him are some of his people. So I greeted him and he greeted me. Then I ascended to the sixth heaven, and there I saw Moses, son of Imran, a dark-skinned man with much hair. If he had two shirts on, his hair would have come through the shirt. He said: People claim that I am more honored in the sight of God than this one, but this one is more honored in the sight of God than I. He said: I said, O Gabriel, who is this? He said: This is your brother Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him, and with him are some of his people. So I greeted him and he greeted me. Then I ascended to the seventh heaven, and behold, I saw our father, Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, leaning his back against the Frequented House like the best of men. I said: O Gabriel, who is this? He said: This is your father, Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, peace be upon him, and with him are some of his people. So I greeted him and he greeted me. And behold, I saw my nation in two halves: one half had white garments like paper, and the other half had garments of sore eyes. He said: So I entered the Frequented House, and those who had white garments entered with me, and those who had black garments prevented me, and they were in good condition. So I and those with me prayed in the Frequented House, then I and those with me went out. He said: And the Frequented House, in which seventy thousand angels pray every day and do not return to it until the Day of Resurrection. He said: Then I was taken up to the Lote Tree of the Limit, and behold, every leaf of it almost covered this nation, and behold, in it was a flowing spring called Salsabil, from which two rivers gushed forth one of them Al-Kawthar and the other is called the River of Mercy, so I washed myself in it and He forgave me my past and future sins. He said: I was raised to Paradise and a girl met me. I said: Who do you belong to, O girl? She said: Zaid bin Haritha. And behold, there were rivers of water that had not become stagnant, and rivers of milk whose taste had not changed, and rivers of wine that was delicious to those who drink, and rivers of pure honey. And behold, its spears were like buckets, large, and behold, its birds were as if they were your camels. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God the Most High has prepared for His righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of man. He said: Then the Fire was shown to me, and in it was the wrath, rebuke and vengeance of God. If stones and iron were thrown into it, it would eat it. Then it was closed to me. Then I was raised to the Lote Tree of the Limit, and it covered me, and between me and it was a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. He said, And an angel from among the angels descended upon each leaf of it. He said, “And fifty prayers were enjoined upon me, and He said, ‘For every good deed ten, so if you intend to do a good deed but do not do it, a good deed will be written down for you, and if you do it, ten will be written down for you. And if you intend to do a bad deed but do not do it, nothing will be written down for you, but if you do it, one bad deed will be written down for you.” Then I returned to Moses and he said: What did your Lord command you? I said: Fifty prayers. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it for your nation, for your nation cannot bear that, and when it cannot bear it, it disbelieves. So I returned to my Lord and said: O Lord, lighten it for my nation, for it is the weakest of nations. So He reduced it to ten and made it forty. I kept differing between Moses and my Lord. Every time I came to him, he said to me the same thing, until I returned to him. He said to me: What have you been commanded? I said: I have been commanded to perform ten prayers. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it for your nation. Then He called to me: I have completed my obligation and lightened it for My servants and given them for every good deed ten times the like thereof. Then I returned to Moses and he said: What have you been commanded to do? I said: Five prayers. He said: Go back to your Lord, for nothing tires Him, and ask Him to lighten the burden for your nation. I said: I have returned to my Lord until I felt shy. Then he went to Mecca in the morning telling them of the wonders: I came to Jerusalem last night and was taken up to heaven, and I saw such and such. Abu Jahl, meaning Ibn Hisham, said: Are you not amazed at what Muhammad said? He claims that he came to Jerusalem last night, then he became among us and one of us was riding his mount, ascending for a month and stopping for a month, so this is a journey of two months in one night. He said: So I told them about a camel of the Quraysh, when I was on my ascent, I saw it in such and such a place, and that it had fled, and when I returned I found it at the pass, and he told them about each man and his camel such and such, and his belongings such and such, so Abu Jahl said: He will tell us things, so a man from among them said: I am the most knowledgeable person about Jerusalem, and how it was built and arranged, and how close it is to the mountain, so if Muhammad is truthful then I will tell you, and if he is lying then I will tell you, so that polytheist came and said: O Muhammad, I am the most knowledgeable person about Jerusalem, so tell me: How is it built, and how is it arranged, and how close it is to the mountain? He said: Then the Holy House was raised to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his seat, and he looked at it as one of us looks at his house. He said: Its construction is such and such, its appearance is such and such, and its proximity to the mountain is such and such. The other said: You have spoken the truth. So he returned to them and said: Muhammad spoke the truth in what he said, or something similar to this statement. And Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir narrated it in full on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Abd al-`A`la, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Thawr, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of Abu Harun al-`Abdi, and on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Yahya, on the authority of `Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of Abu Harun al-`Abdi, with the same chain of transmission. And he also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Ruh ibn al-Qasim told me on the authority of Abu Harun, with a chain of transmission similar to the one mentioned above. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ahmad ibn `Abdah, on the authority of Abu `Abd al-Samad `Abd al-`Aziz ibn `Abd al-Samad, on the authority of Abu Harun al-`Abdi, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, and he mentioned it in a long, beautiful, elegant chain of transmission, better than what others have narrated, despite its strangeness and what is strange in it. Then Al-Bayhaqi also mentioned it from the narration of Nuh bin Qais Al-Hadani, Hisham and Muammar on the authority of Abu Harun Al-Abdi, whose name is Ammarah bin Juwayn, and he is considered weak by the Imams. We only cited his hadith here because it contains corroborating evidence from others, and because Al-Bayhaqi narrated: Imam Abu Uthman Ismail bin Abdul Rahman informed us, Abu Naim Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Bazzar informed us, Abu Hamid bin Bilal informed us, Abu Al-Azhar informed us, Yazid bin Abi Hakim informed us, he said: “I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a dream. I said: O Messenger of God, a man from your nation called Sufyan Al-Thawri is fine. The Messenger of God said: There is nothing wrong with him.” He told us on the authority of Abu Harun Al-Abdi on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, on the night of your Night Journey, “I said: I saw in the sky, so I told him the hadith and he said to me: Yes. I said to him: O Messenger of God, some people from your nation tell strange things about you during the Night Journey? He said to me: That is the hadith of storytellers.” Imam Abu Ismail Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Tirmidhi said: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Al-Ala bin Al-Dahhak Al-Zubaidi told us: Amr bin Al-Harith told us: Abdullah bin Salem Al-Ash'ari told us: Muhammad bin Al-Waleed bin Aamer Al-Zubaidi told us: Al-Waleed bin Abdul Rahman told us: Jubayr bin Nafeer told us: Shaddad bin Aws said: "We said: O Messenger of God, how was your Night Journey?" He said: I prayed the Isha prayer with my companions in Mecca, wearing the Isha prayer, then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to me with a white animal, or he said: white, bigger than a donkey and smaller than a mule. He said: Ride. I found it difficult to separate it by its ear. Then he made me ride it, and it set off with us, falling with its hoof wherever it ended, until we reached a land of palm trees. He made me dismount and said: Pray. So I prayed, then I rode. He said: Do you know where you prayed? I said: God knows best. He said: I prayed in Yathrib. I prayed in Tayyibah. Then it set off, falling with us, its hoof landing where its edge reached, then we reached a land. He said, Get down. Then he said, Pray. So I prayed, then we mounted. He said, Do you know where you prayed? I said, God knows best. He said, I prayed in Madyan near the tree of Moses. Then it set off, falling with us, its hoof landing where its edge reached, then we reached a land where palaces appeared to us. He said, Get down. So I got down. He said, Pray. So I prayed, then we mounted. He said, Do you know where you prayed? I said, God knows best. He said, I prayed in Bethlehem where Jesus Christ, son of Mary, was born.
