Then he set off with me until we entered the city from its Yemeni gate. He came to the direction of the mosque and tied his mount to it. We entered the mosque from a gate where the sun and moon incline. I prayed in the mosque wherever God willed. I was overcome by thirst more than anything else. I was brought two vessels, one containing milk and the other containing honey. He sent them both to me, so I made them evenly distributed between them. Then God guided me, so I took the milk and drank until it struck my forehead. In front of me was an old man reclining on his resting place. He said, Your companion has taken the natural disposition, and indeed he is being guided. Then he took me until we came to the valley in which the city was located. Then Hell appeared as if it were hills. I said, O Messenger of God, how did you find it? He said: I found it like a hot fever. Then he turned with me and we passed a camel of the Quraysh in such and such a place. They had lost a camel of theirs and so-and-so had gathered it. I greeted them and some of them said: This is the voice of Muhammad. Then I came to my companions before dawn in Mecca and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, came to me and said: O Messenger of God, where were you last night? I looked for you in your places. He said: I knew that I came from Jerusalem last night. He said: O Messenger of God, it is a month’s journey, so describe it to me. He said: A path was opened for me as if I was reaching it. He did not ask me about anything except that I informed him of it. Abu Bakr said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. The polytheists said: Look at Ibn Abi Kabshah, he claims that he came to Jerusalem last night. He said: One of the signs that I am telling you is that I passed a camel of yours in such and such a place and they had lost a camel of theirs and so-and-so had gathered it. They will continue their journey and will descend at such and such and then at such and such and they will come to you on such and such a day, preceded by a red camel with black hair on it and two black cloaks. When that day came, the people looked out while it was close to noon until the caravan approached, preceded by that camel which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had described. This is how Al-Bayhaqi narrated it through two chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Ismail Al-Tirmidhi with it. Then he said after completing it: This is a sound chain of transmission. He narrated it in parts from the hadiths of others, and we will mention from that, God willing, what we have in attendance. Then he cited many hadiths about the Night Journey as evidence for this hadith. This hadith was narrated in full on the authority of Shaddad bin Aws by Imam Abu Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Hatim in his interpretation on the authority of his father on the authority of Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Al-Ala Al-Zubaidi with it. There is no doubt that this hadith, I mean the hadith narrated on the authority of Shaddad bin Aws, contains things, some of which are sound as Al-Bayhaqi mentioned, and some of which are rejected, such as praying in Bethlehem, and the question of the friend about the description of Jerusalem and other things, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Uthman bin Muhammad told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Abbas told us: “On the night of the Isra’ Night Journey of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he entered Paradise and heard a noise in one corner of it, so he said: ‘O Gabriel, what is this? ’ He said: ‘This is Bilal the muezzin. ’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he came to the people, ‘Bilal has succeeded. I saw such and such in him. ’ Moses, peace be upon him, met him and welcomed him. He said: ‘Welcome to the unlettered Prophet. ’ He said: ‘He was a tall, dark-skinned man, with straight hair that reached his ears or above them. ’ He said: ‘Who is this, O Gabriel? ’ He said: ‘This is Moses. ’ He went on and was met by a venerable, awe-inspiring old man, who welcomed him and greeted him, and they all greeted him. ’ He said: ‘Who is this, O Gabriel? ’ He said: ‘This is your father, Abraham. ’ He looked into the Fire and saw people eating carrion. ’ He said: ‘Who are these, O Gabriel? ’ He said: ‘These are the ones who eat the flesh of people. ’ He saw a very red and blue man. He said: ‘Who is this, O Gabriel? ’ He said: ‘This is the one who hamstrung the she-camel. ’ He said: ‘He is the one who hamstrung the she-camel. ’ He said: ‘He is the one who hamstrung the she-camel. ’” When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to the Al-Aqsa Mosque, he stood up to pray and found all the prophets praying with him. When he turned away, two cups were brought, one on the right and the other on the left. In one of them was milk and in the other was honey. He took the milk and drank from it, and the one who had the cup said: You have attained the natural disposition. The chain of transmission is sound, but they did not include it. Another way - Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Thabit Abu Zaid told us, Hilal told us, Ikrimah told me on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on a night journey to Jerusalem, then he came that night and told them about his journey and the sign of Jerusalem and their camel. The people said: We do not believe Muhammad in what he says, so they turned back as infidels, so God struck their necks with Abu Jahl, and Abu Jahl said: Muhammad is frightening us with the tree of Zaqqum, bring dates and butter, so they choked, and the Antichrist saw in his image a vision with the eyes, not a vision in a dream, and Jesus, Moses, and Abraham, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the Antichrist, so he said: I saw him in a dream, a white-skinned, straight-eyed man, one of his eyes standing out like a shining star, and the hair of his head was like the branches of a tree, and I saw Jesus, peace be upon him, white, with curly hair, sharp eyesight, and a well-built body, and I saw Moses, peace be upon him, dark-skinned, with much hair, and a strong body, and I looked at Abraham, peace be upon him, and I did not see a single one. From him, I looked at him from me until he was as if he was your companion. Gabriel said: Greet Malik, so I greeted him. Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Abu Zaid Thabit on the authority of Hilal, who is Ibn Khabab, with it, and it is a sound chain of transmission. Another way Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Bakr Al-Shafi’i informed us, Ishaq bin Al-Hasan informed us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad informed us, Shaiban informed us on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, who said: The cousin of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, informed us, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘On the night of my Night Journey, I saw Moses bin Imran, a tall, curly-haired man, as if he were from the men of Shanu’ah. I saw Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, with a medium build, reddish and white, with a smooth head. I saw Malik, the keeper of Hell, and the Antichrist in signs that God showed him. ’ He said: ‘So do not be in doubt about meeting him. ’ So Qatada interpreted it as meaning that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had met Moses, peace be upon him. ‘And We made him a guidance for the Children of Israel. ’ He said: God made Moses a guidance for the Children of Israel. Muslim narrated it in Sahih on the authority of Abd bin Hamid on the authority of Yunus bin Muhammad, on the authority of Shaiban, and they both included it on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of… Qatada in brief. Another path Al-Bayhaqi said: Ali bin Ahmad bin Abdun informed us, Ahmad bin Ubaid Al-Saffar informed us, Dubays Al-Mu’addil informed us, Affan informed us, Hammad bin Salamah informed us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When I was taken on the Night Journey, a pleasant scent passed by me, so I said: What is this scent? They said: The hairdresser of Pharaoh’s daughter and her children. The comb fell from her hand, so she said: In the name of God. Pharaoh’s daughter said: My father. She said: My Lord, your Lord, and the Lord of your father. She said: Do you have a lord other than my father? She said: Yes, my Lord, your Lord, and the Lord of your father is God. He said: So he called her and said: Do you have a lord other than me? She said: Yes, my Lord, and your Lord is God, the Almighty and Majestic. He said: So he ordered a copper pot to be heated, then he ordered her to be thrown into it. She said: I have a need of you. He said: What is it? She said: Gather my bones and the bones of my children in one place. He said: That is for you because of the right you have over us. He said: So he ordered them to be thrown into it. One by one, until he reached the age of an infant among them, and he said: O mother, sit down and do not be lazy, for you are on the truth. He said: And four spoke in the cradle while they were young: this one, and the witness of Joseph, and the companion of Guraij, and Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. The chain of transmission is not bad, and they did not include it. Another way Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and Ruh ibn al-Mu`in told us: Awf told us on the authority of Zurarah ibn Awfa on the authority of Ibn `Abbas who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the night of my Isra’ Night Journey came, I was in Mecca and was terrified and knew that the people would deny me, so he sat isolated and sad. Then the enemy of God, Abu Jahl, passed by him, so he came and sat next to him and said to him as if mockingly: ‘Did something happen?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘And what was it?’ He said: ‘I was taken on a Night Journey last night.’ He said: ‘To where?’ He said: ‘To the Holy House.’ He said: ‘Then you are now among us in the morning?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘He did not think he should belie him for fear that he would deny the hadith if he called his people to it. So he said: ‘Do you think that if I called your people, would you tell them what you told me?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘O people of Banu Ka`b ibn Lu`ay.’ He said: ‘So the gatherings dispersed to him and they came and sat next to him.’ He said: ‘Tell your people what you told me.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: I was taken on a night journey last night. They said: Where to? He said: To Jerusalem. They said: Then you became among us? He said: Yes. He said: Some clapped and some put their hands on their heads in amazement at the lie. They said: Can you describe the mosque to us? Among them were those who had traveled to that country and seen the mosque. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: I kept describing until some of the description became unclear to me. He said: The mosque was brought to me while I was looking at it until it was placed near the house of Aqil or Uqayl, so he described it while I was looking at it. He said: And along with this there was a description that I did not remember. The people said: As for the description, by God, he hit the nail on the head. An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Awf ibn Abi Jamilah, who is the Bedouin, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of An-Nadr ibn Shumayl and Hudhahah from Awf, who is the son of Abi Jamilah the Bedouin, one of the trustworthy imams. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ya’qub told us, Al-Sari bin Khuzaymah told us, Yusuf bin Bahlol told us, Abdullah bin Numayr told us, on the authority of Malik bin Mughul, on the authority of Al-Zubayr bin Adi, on the authority of Talha bin Masraf, on the authority of Marra Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree of the Limit, which is in the sixth heaven. What he ascends ends at it until he is taken from it, and what he descends from above it ends at it until he is taken. “When that which covers the Lote Tree covers it,” he said: It was covered by a bed of gold. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given the five daily prayers and the last verses of Surat Al-Baqarah, and the major sins were forgiven for whoever does not associate anything with God. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr and Zuhayr ibn Harb, both on the authority of Abdullah ibn Numayr, and then al-Bayhaqi said: This which Abdullah ibn Mas`ud mentioned is part of the hadith of the Mi`raj. Anas ibn Malik narrated it on the authority of Malik ibn Sa`sa`ah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then on the authority of Abu Dharr on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he narrated it once without mentioning them, then al-Bayhaqi cited the three hadiths as mentioned above. I said: It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud in a more detailed manner than this, and there is something strange in it, and that is in what al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated in his famous section: Marwan ibn Mu`awiyah narrated to us on the authority of Qatadah ibn Abdullah al-Nahmi, Abu Dhibyan al-Junbi narrated to us, saying: We were sitting with Abu Ubaydah ibn Abdullah, meaning Ibn Mas`ud, and Muhammad ibn Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, and they were sitting, and Muhammad ibn Sa`d said to Abu Ubaydah: Tell us on the authority of your father on the night of the Isra’ with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Ubaydah said: No, rather you tell us on the authority of Your father, Muhammad said: If you had asked me before I asked you, I would have done so. Abu Ubaidah began to narrate, meaning on the authority of his father, as he was asked. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to me with a mount larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule. He carried me on it, then he set off, tumbling with us. Whenever he ascended a hill, his legs were straight, like his hands, and whenever he descended, his hands were straight with his legs, until we passed by a tall man from the tribe of Adam, as if he were from the men of Azd Shanu’ah. He raised his voice, saying, I have honored and favored him. He said: So we pushed him towards him and greeted him, and he returned the greeting. He said: Who is this with you, O Gabriel? He said: This is Ahmad. He said: Welcome to the unlettered Arab prophet who conveyed the message of his Lord and advised his nation. He said: Then we pushed on, and I said: Who is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is Moses, son of Imran. He said: I said: Who is he blaming? He said: He is blaming his Lord for you. I said: And he raises his voice to his Lord? He said: Indeed, God knows his sharpness. He said: Then we pushed on until we passed by a tree whose fruit was like a saddle, and under it was an old man and his family. He said: Then Gabriel said to me: Go to your father Ibrahim. So we pushed him towards us and greeted him and he returned the greeting. Ibrahim said: Who is this with you, Gabriel? He said: This is your son Ahmad. He said: Welcome to the unlettered prophet who delivered the message of his Lord and advised his nation. O my son, you will meet your Lord tonight, and your nation is the last and weakest of nations. So if you can have your need or most of it met by your nation, then do so. He said: Then we pushed on until we reached the Al-Aqsa Mosque, so I got off and tied the animal in the ring at the door of the mosque where the prophets used to be tied, then I entered the mosque and recognized the prophets among those standing, kneeling and prostrating. He said: Then I was brought two cups of honey and milk, so I took the milk and drank, then Gabriel, peace be upon him, struck my shoulder and said: You have found the natural disposition, by the Lord of Muhammad. He said: Then the prayer was established and I led them in prayer, then we turned away and came back. It is a strange chain of transmission, and they did not include it. It includes the strangeness of the prophets asking him, peace be upon him, first, then asking him about them after he turned away. What is well-known in the Sahihs, as mentioned above, is that Gabriel informed him of them first so that he could greet them with a greeting of knowledge. It also includes that he met the prophets, peace be upon them, before entering the Al-Aqsa Mosque, and what is correct is that he met them in the heavens, then he descended to the Holy House a second time and they were with him. He prayed with them there, then he rode Al-Buraq and returned to Mecca, and God knows best. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Jabalah bin Suhaim, on the authority of Muathir bin Afazah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said: On the night of my Night Journey, I met Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, peace be upon them, and they discussed the matter of the Hour. He said: They referred their matter to Abraham, peace be upon him, and he said: I have no knowledge of it. They referred their matter to Moses, and he said: I have no knowledge of it. They referred their matter to Jesus, and he said: I have not revealed it to anyone except God Almighty. And among what my Lord has entrusted to me is that the Antichrist will emerge. He said: I will have two sticks with me, and when he sees me he will melt like lead melts. He said: God will destroy him when he sees me, until the rock and the tree will say: O Muslim, there is an unbeliever beneath me, so come and kill him. He said: God will destroy them, then the people will return to their lands and homelands. He said: At that time, Gog and Magog will emerge, and they will swarm from every hill and tread upon their lands, and they will not come upon anything except that they will destroy it, and they will not pass by water.” Except that they drink it. He said: Then the people will return to me and complain about them, so I will call upon God against them and He will destroy them and cause them to die until the earth runs with the stench of their stench, meaning it stinks. He said: Then God will send down rain and sweep away their bodies until He throws them into the sea. So what my Lord has entrusted me with is that if that is the case, the Hour will be like a pregnant woman who has just given birth, and her family will not know when she will surprise them with her birth, at night or during the day. Narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, narrated by Abd Al-Rahman bin Quraz, the brother of Abdullah bin Quraz Al-Thamali. Saeed bin Mansour said: Maskeen Maymun bin Mu’adhdhin of Al-Ramlah Mosque told us, Urwah bin Ruwaim told me on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Quraz that on the night of the Night Journey, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken from Al-Masjid Al-Haram to Al-Masjid Al-Aqsa, between Zamzam and Al-Maqam, Gabriel was on his right and Michael was on his left. They flew with him until he reached the highest heavens. When he returned, he said: I heard glorification in the highest heavens, along with much glorification. The highest heavens glorify the One of Majesty, fearful of the One of Exaltation for what is high. Glory be to the Most High, the Most High, glory be to Him and He is Most High. We mention here the hadith when God the Almighty says in this Surah, The seven heavens glorify Him verse. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad bin Aamer told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ubaid bin Adam, Abu Maryam, and Abu Shuaib, that Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was in Jabiyah, and he mentioned the conquest of Jerusalem. He said: Abu Salamah said: Abu Sinan told me, on the authority of Ubaid bin Adam, who said: I heard Umar bin Al-Khattab say to Ka’b: Where do you think I should pray? He said: If you take it from me, you will pray behind the rock, and all of Jerusalem will be in your hands. Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: You have imitated the Jews, but I will pray where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed. So he advanced towards the qiblah and prayed, then he came and spread out his cloak and swept the trash with his cloak, and the people swept it. He did not venerate the rock with the reverence that would make him pray behind it while it was in front of him, as Ka’b Al-Ahbar had indicated, and he was from a people who venerated it to the point that they made it their qiblah. But God bestowed Islam upon him, so he was guided to the truth. For this reason, when he indicated that, the Commander of the Faithful Omar said to him: You have imitated the Jews and did not humiliate it as the Christians humiliated it, who had made it a garbage dump because it was the qiblah of the Jews. Rather, he removed the harm from it and swept the trash from it with his cloak. This is similar to what came in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Marthad Al-Ghanawi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not sit on graves and do not pray towards them.
17:2: Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said in his interpretation of Surat Subhan: Ali bin Sahl told us, Hajjaj told us, Abu Jaafar Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah Al-Riyahi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah or someone else, Abu Jaafar doubted, in the words of God the Almighty, Glory be to Him who took His servant by night the verse, he said: “Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with Michael, and Gabriel said to Michael: Bring me a basin of Zamzam water so that I may purify his heart and expand his chest. He said: So he split open his stomach and washed it three times, and Michael came to him with three basins of Zamzam water, and expanded his chest and removed whatever rancor was in it, and filled it with knowledge, patience, faith, certainty, and Islam, and sealed between his shoulders with the seal of prophethood, then he brought him a horse and carried him on it with every step of it as far as his sight could reach or the furthest part of it.” His sight, he said: So he walked and Gabriel, peace be upon them, walked with him. He said: He came upon a people who plant in one day and harvest in the next day. Whenever they harvest, it returns to how it was. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Gabriel, what is this? He said: These are the ones who strive in the way of God. Their good deeds will be multiplied seven hundredfold, and whatever they spend, He will replace it, and He is the Best of providers. Then he came upon a people whose heads were being crushed against rocks. Whenever they were crushed, they returned to how they were, and nothing of that would stop for them. He said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are those whose heads are too heavy to pray the obligatory prayers. Then he came upon a people with patches on their fronts and patches on their backs. They graze as camels and cattle graze, and they eat the thorny thorn, the zaqqum, and the stones of Hell. He said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are the ones who do not pay the zakat of their wealth, and God has not wronged them in the least, and God is not unjust to His servants. Then he came upon a people who had before them cooked meat in a pot and raw meat in a bad pot, so they began to eat from the bad raw meat and leave the good cooked meat. He said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: This man from your nation has a lawful, good wife, so he goes to a bad woman and spends the night with her until morning, and the woman leaves her lawful, good husband and goes to a bad man and spends the night with him until morning. He said: Then he came upon a piece of wood on the road, and no garment passes by it without tearing it or anything else without tearing it. He said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is like the people of your nation who sit on the road and cut it off. Then he recited: And do not sit on every path, threatening and turning away 3:10. He said: Then he came upon a man who had gathered a huge bundle that he could not carry and he was adding more to it. He said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This man from your nation has people’s trusts on him and he is not able to fulfill them, and he wants to carry them. Then he came upon a people whose tongues and lips were being cut off with iron shears. Every time they were cut off, they returned to the way they were, and they did not stop doing so. He said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: These are the preachers of discord. Then he came upon a small hole from which a huge bull was emerging. The bull wanted to go back from where it came out but could not. He said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This man speaks a great word, then regrets it and is not able to take it back. Then he came to a valley and found a pleasant, cool wind and the scent of musk and heard a voice, so he said: O Gabriel, what is this pleasant, cool wind, and what is this musk, and what is this voice? He said: This is the voice of Paradise saying: O Lord, bring me what You promised me, for my rooms have become many, and my brocade, and my silk and my satin, and my pearls and my coral, and my silver and my gold, and my cups and my plates and my pitchers and my goblets, and my honey and my water and my milk and my wine, so bring me what You promised me. So He said: For You is every Muslim man and woman, and every believer man and woman, and whoever believes in Me and My messengers and does righteousness and does not associate anything with Me, and does not take rivals besides Me, and whoever fears Me is safe, and whoever asks Me - I will give to him, and whoever lends Me - I will repay him, and whoever relies on Me - I will suffice him. Indeed, I am God, there is no god but Me. I do not break My promise, and the believers have succeeded. Blessed be God, the Best of Creators. It said: I am satisfied. He said: Then he came to a valley and heard an unpleasant sound and found a foul odor, so he said: What is this, O Gabriel, and what is this sound? He said: This is the sound of Hell saying: O Lord, bring me what You promised me, for my chains, shackles, blazing fire, scalding water, filth, and torment have increased, and my bottom has become distant and my heat has become intense, so bring me what You promised me. It said: For You is every polytheist, male and female, and disbeliever, male and female, and every wicked man and female, and every tyrant who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning. It said: I am satisfied. He said: Then he walked until he came to Jerusalem, and he got down and tied his horse to the rock, then he entered and prayed with the angels. When he finished the prayer, they said: O Gabriel, who is this with you? He said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, he is a brother and a successor. What a good brother, what a good successor, and what a good coming he has come. He said: Then he met the spirits of the prophets and they praised their Lord. Abraham, peace be upon him, said: Praise be to God who took me as a friend, and gave me a great kingdom, and made me a devout nation that follows me, and saved me from the fire and made it cool and peaceful for me. Then Moses, peace be upon him, praised his Lord and said: Praise be to God who spoke to me directly, and caused the destruction of the people of Pharaoh and the salvation of the Children of Israel to be at my hands, and made from my nation a people who guide with the truth and do justice by it. Then David, peace be upon him, praised his Lord and said: Praise be to God who made for me a great kingdom, and taught me the Psalms, and softened iron for me, and subjected the mountains to me to glorify God and the birds, and gave me wisdom and the ability to make clear statements. Then Solomon, peace be upon him, praised his Lord, saying: Praise be to God, who has subjected the winds to me and subjected the devils to me to make for me whatever I wish of shrines, statues, basins like basins, and fixed cauldrons. He taught me the language of birds, and gave me from all things a bounty, and subjected to me the soldiers of devils, humans, and birds, and preferred me over many of His believing servants, and gave me a great kingdom such as no one after me will have, and made my kingdom good, without account. Then Jesus, peace be upon him, praised his Lord, the Almighty, and said: Praise be to God, who made me His word, and made my likeness like that of Adam, whom He created from dust, then said to him, Be, and he was. He taught me the Book and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel, and made me create from clay like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by God’s permission. He made me heal the blind and the leper and bring the dead to life by God’s permission. He raised me up and purified me, and protected me and my mother from the accursed Satan, so Satan had no way against us. He said: Then Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, praised his Lord, the Almighty, and said: All of you have praised your Lord, and I praise my Lord. He said: Praise be to God, who sent me as a mercy to the worlds and as a bringer of good tidings and a warner to all mankind, and sent down to me the Criterion in which is clarification of everything, and made my nation the best nation brought forth for mankind, and made my nation a middle nation, and made my nation the first and they the last, and expanded my chest for me and removed my burden, and raised my reputation for me, and made me the opener and the seal. Then Abraham, peace be upon him, said: With this Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, has excelled you. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said: The seal of prophecy is the opening of intercession on the Day of Resurrection. Then three vessels were brought to him with their mouths covered. One of them contained water, and it was said to him: Drink. So he drank a little from it. Then another vessel was given to him containing milk, and it was said to him: Drink. So he drank from it until he was satisfied. Then another vessel was given to him containing wine, and it was said to him: Drink. So he said: I do not want it, I have been satisfied. So Gabriel said to him: It will be forbidden to your nation, and if you drink from it, only a few of your nation will follow you. He said: Then he ascended with him to the heaven and asked for it to be opened. It was said: Who is this, O Gabriel? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, what a brother and a successor! What an excellent brother, what an excellent successor, and what an excellent arrival he has been. So it was opened for them, and he entered and there was a man who was perfect in his creation, nothing missing from his creation, as is missing from the creation of people. On his right was a door from which a good smell emanated, and on his left was a door from which a bad smell emanated. When he looked at the door on his right, he laughed and was delighted, and when he looked at the door on his left, he cried and was sad. So I said: O Gabriel, who is this old man who was perfect in his creation, nothing missing from his creation, and what are these two doors? He said: This is your father Adam, and this door on his right is the door of Paradise. When he looks at those of his descendants who will enter Paradise, he laughs and is glad. And the door on his left is the door of Hell. When he looks at those of his descendants who will enter it, he will cry and be sad. Then Gabriel ascended with him to the second heaven and asked to be admitted. It was said: Who is this with you? He said: Muhammad, the Messenger of God. They said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, he is a brother and a successor. What a good brother, what a good successor, and what a good visitor he has come. He said: So he entered and saw two young men. He said: O Gabriel, who are these two young men? He said: This is Jesus, son of Mary, and John, son of Zachariah, the sons of the maternal aunt, peace be upon them. He said: So he ascended with him to the third heaven, and asked to be admitted. They said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, what a brother and a successor! What an excellent brother, what an excellent successor, and what an excellent arrival he has come. He said: So he entered, and behold, he was a man who had excelled himself over the people in beauty, just as the moon on the night of the full moon is excelled over all the other stars. He said: Who is this, O Gabriel, who has excelled himself over the people in beauty? He said: This is your brother Joseph, peace be upon him. He said: Then he ascended with him to the fourth heaven, and he asked to be admitted. They said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, what a brother and a successor! What a good brother, what a good successor, and what a good coming he has been. He said: So he entered, and there was a man. He said: Who is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is Idris, peace be upon him. May God raise him to a high station. He said: So he ascended with him to the fifth heaven, and asked to be admitted. They said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, what a brother and a successor! What a good brother, what a good successor, and what a good visitor he has been. He said: So he entered, and there he saw a man sitting with people around him telling stories to him. He said: Who is this, O Gabriel, and who are these around him? He said: This is Aaron the beloved, and these are the Children of Israel. He said: Then he ascended with him to the sixth heaven, and he asked for permission. They said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, what a brother and a successor! What an excellent brother, what an excellent successor, and what an excellent arrival he has come. He said: So he entered, and there was a man sitting, so he passed him and the man wept. He said: O Gabriel, who is this? He said: Moses. He said: Why is he weeping? He said: The Children of Israel claim that I am the most honored of the children of Adam in the sight of God, the Almighty, and this is a man from the children of Adam who has succeeded me in this world and I am in the next. If he were himself, I would not care, but with every prophet is his nation. He said: Then he ascended with him to the seventh heaven, and asked for it to be opened. They said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, what a brother and a successor! What a good brother, what a good successor, and what a good visitor he has been. He said: So he entered, and there he saw a disheveled man sitting on a chair at the gate of Paradise, and with him were sitting people with white faces like paper, and people with different colors. Those who had different colors stood up, entered a river and washed in it, and came out with some of their colors gone. Then they entered another river and washed in it, and came out with some of their colors gone. Then they entered another river and washed themselves in it, and came out with their colors cleared and became like the colors of their companions. They came and sat with their companions, and he said: O Gabriel, who is this ruddy-haired one? Then who are these with white faces and who have something in their colors? What are these rivers that they entered and came out with their colors clear? He said: This is your father Abraham, the first of those with ruddy faces on the face of the earth. As for these with white faces, they are people who did not mix their faith with injustice. As for these with something in their colors, they are people who mixed good deeds with bad ones, then they repented and God accepted their repentance. As for the rivers, the first is the mercy of God, the second is the blessing of God, and the third is that their Lord gave them to drink a pure drink. He said: Then he reached the lote tree, and it was said to him: This lote tree, everyone from your nation will reach it according to your way. And behold, it is a tree from whose root flows rivers of water that is not stagnant, and rivers of milk whose taste never changes, and rivers of wine that is delicious to those who drink, and rivers of pure honey. It is a tree in whose shade a rider can travel for seventy years without crossing it, and its leaves cover the entire nation. He said: Then the light of the Creator, the Almighty and Majestic, covered it, and the angels covered it like crows when they land on the tree, out of love for the Lord, the Blessed and Exalted. They said: Then God spoke to him and said to him: Ask. He said: You took Abraham as a friend and gave him a great kingdom, and You spoke to Moses directly and gave David a great kingdom and softened iron for him, and You subjected the mountains to him, and You gave Solomon a kingdom and subjected the jinn, mankind and devils to him, and You subjected the winds to him and gave him a kingdom that no one after him would have, and You taught Jesus the Torah and the Gospel and made him heal the blind. And the leper and He brings the dead back to life by Your permission, and I protected him and his mother from Satan the accursed, so Satan had no way over them, so the Lord Almighty said to him: And I have taken you as a friend - and it is written in the Torah: Beloved of the Most Gracious - and I have sent you to all people as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and I have expanded your breast for you, and removed from you your burden, and raised your fame, so that I do not mention you except that you are mentioned with me, and I have made your nation the best nation brought forth for mankind, and I have made your nation a middle nation, and I have made your nation the first and they are the last, and I have made it not permissible for your nation to speak to them until they testify that you are My servant and Messenger, and I have made from your nation people whose hearts are their Gospels, and I have made you the first of the prophets to be created and the last of them to be sent, and the first of them to be judged, and I have given you seven of the oft-repeated verses that were not given to any prophet before you, and I have given you the final verses of Surat Al-Baqarah from a treasure beneath the Throne that I have not given to any prophet before you, and I have given you Al-Kawthar, and I have given you eight shares: Islam, migration, jihad, prayer, and charity. And fasting Ramadan, and enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and I have made you a conqueror and a sealer. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My Lord has favored me with six things: He has given me the openings of speech and its endings, and the comprehensive hadiths. He has sent me to all people as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. He has cast terror into the hearts of my enemies from a distance of a month’s journey. He has made spoils of war lawful for me, as they were not lawful for anyone before me. He has made the entire earth pure and a place of prostration for me. He said: And fifty prayers have been made obligatory for me. When he returned to Moses, he said: What have you been commanded, O Muhammad? He said: Fifty prayers. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce it, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and you have encountered hardship from the Children of Israel. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to his Lord and asked Him to reduce it, so He reduced it by ten. Then he returned to Moses and said to him: How much have you been commanded? He said: Forty. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce it, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and you have encountered hardship from the Children of Israel. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to his Lord and asked Him to reduce it, so He reduced it by ten. Then he returned to Moses and said: How much have you been commanded? He said: I have been commanded with thirty. Moses said to him: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce it, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and you have encountered hardship from the Children of Israel. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to his Lord and asked Him to reduce it, so He reduced it by ten. Then he returned to Moses and said to him: How much have you been commanded? He said: Twenty. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce it, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and you have suffered hardship from the Children of Israel. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went back to his Lord, the Almighty, and asked Him to reduce it, so He reduced it by ten. Then he went back to Moses, peace be upon him, and said to him: How much have you been commanded? He said: Ten. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce it, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and you have suffered hardship from the Children of Israel. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went back to his Lord, the Almighty, and asked Him to reduce it, so He reduced it by five. Then he went back to Moses, peace be upon him, and said to him: How much have you been commanded? He said: Five. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to make it easier, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and I have encountered hardship from the Children of Israel. He said: I have returned to my Lord until I felt ashamed, but I will not return to Him. It was said: As you have patiently prayed five prayers, they will suffice for you as fifty prayers, for every good deed is rewarded tenfold. He said: So Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was completely pleased. He said: And Moses, peace be upon him, was the most severe of them to him when he passed by him and the best of them to him when he returned to him. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ubayd God on the authority of Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah or someone else. Abu Ja`far was uncertain on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he mentioned it with its meaning. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi narrated it on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Malini, on the authority of Ibn `Adi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sakuni al-Balasi in Ramla. `Ali ibn Sahl told us, so he mentioned the same as what Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority. Al-Bayhaqi mentioned that al-Hakim Abu `Abdullah narrated it on the authority of Isma`il ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl ibn Muhammad al-Sha`rani on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hamza al-Zubayri, on the authority of Hatim ibn Isma`il. `Isa ibn Mahan, meaning Abu Ja`far al-Razi, told me on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr told us: Yunus ibn Bakir told us: Isa ibn Abdullah al-Tamimi told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas al-Bakri, on the authority of Abu al-A’liyyah or someone else, Isa was not sure, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said regarding the words of God Almighty: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram, so he mentioned the hadith in its entirety, similar to what we have cited. I said, and Abu Ja’far al-Razi said: It includes al-Hafiz Abu Zur’ah al-Razi: He makes many mistakes in the hadith, and others have also weakened him, and some have authenticated him, and it appears that he had a poor memory, so what he narrated alone should be looked into. This hadith has some strange and extremely strange wording, and it contains something from the hadith of a dream narrated by Samurah ibn Jundub in the long dream narrated by al-Bukhari, and it seems that it is a collection of various hadiths or a dream or another story other than the Night Journey, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, that Ma’mar informed us from al-Zuhri, that Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab informed me from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When I was taken on the Night Journey, I met Moses, peace be upon him - and I described him, and there was a man whom I thought was him. He said: His head was twitching, as if he was from the men of Shanu’ah. He said: And I met Jesus - and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, described him. He said: He was of medium build, red, as if he had just come out of a bathhouse. He said: And I met Abraham, and I resembled his son to him. He said: And I was brought two vessels, one of which contained milk and the other wine. It was said to me: Take whichever one you want. So I took the milk and drank it. It was said to me: You have been guided to the fitrah - or you have attained the fitrah. If you had taken wine, your nation would have gone astray.” And they narrated it from another chain of transmission from al-Zuhri with a similar wording. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Al-Hujayn ibn Al-Muthanna, on the authority of Abdul Aziz ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Al-Fadl Al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw myself in Al-Hijr and the Quraysh were asking me about my Night Journey. They asked me about things from the Holy House that I did not confirm, so I was distressed in a way I had never been distressed before. Then God raised him up to me so that I could look at him. They did not ask me about anything except that I informed them about it. I saw myself in a group of prophets, and Moses was standing praying. He was a curly-haired man as if he were one of the men of Shanu’ah. Jesus, son of Mary, was standing praying, and the person closest to him in resemblance was Urwah ibn Mas’ud Al-Thaqafi. And Abraham was standing praying, and the person closest to him in resemblance was your companion - meaning himself - and the time for prayer came, so I led them in prayer. When I finished, someone said: O Muhammad, this is Malik, the keeper of Hell. So he turned to him and he greeted me first.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hajjaj bin Munhal told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu al-Salt, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw on the night of my ascension when I reached the seventh heaven, and I looked up and saw thunder, lightning, and lightning bolts. He said: And I came upon a people whose stomachs were like houses, and in them were snakes that could be seen from outside their stomachs, so I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are the ones who consume usury. When I descended to the lowest heaven, I looked below me and saw a thunderstorm, smoke, and voices, so I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are the devils hovering over the eyes of the children of Adam, and they do not contemplate the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and were it not for that, they would have seen wonders.” Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Hasan and Affan, both on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah on his authority. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Hammad on his authority. Al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah, meaning al-Hakim, told us, Abdullah bin Zaid bin Ya’qub al-Daqqaq al-Hamadani told us, Ibrahim bin al-Husayn al-Hamadani told us, Abu Muhammad, he is Ismail bin Musa al-Fazari told us, Umar bin Sa’d al-Nadri from Bani Nasr bin Ma’in told us, Abdul Aziz, Laith bin Abi Salim, Salman al-A’mash and Ata’ bin al-Sa’ib told me, some of them adding to the hadith some of them, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, Abdullah bin Abbas and Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar on the authority of someone who told him on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Salim bin Muslim al-Uqaili on the authority of Amer al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud and Juwaybir al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sleeping in the house of Umm Hani’ and he had prayed the last ‘Isha’ prayer. Abu Abdullah al-Hakim said: This sheikh told us, and he mentioned the hadith, so I wrote the text from a copy that I heard from him, and he mentioned a long hadith in which he mentioned the number of stairs and angels and other things that are not denied in the power of God if the narration is authentic. Al-Bayhaqi said, as we mentioned before, in the hadith of Abu Harun al-Abdi proving the Isra and Mi'raj, it is sufficient, and success is from God. I said, and this hadith was transmitted by more than one of the followers and imams of the commentators, may God have mercy on them all. Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Makram bin Ahmad Al-Qadi informed me, Ibrahim bin Al-Haitham Al-Baldi informed me, Muhammad bin Katheer Al-San’ani informed me, Muammar bin Rashid informed us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey to the Al-Aqsa Mosque, he began to tell people about that in the morning. Some of those who had believed in him and confirmed him turned back and went to Abu Bakr about that and said: Do you have any information about your companion? He claims that he was taken on the Night Journey to Jerusalem last night. He said: Did he say that? They said: Yes. He said: If he said that, then he has spoken the truth. They said: Do you believe him that he went to Jerusalem last night and came back before morning? He said: Yes. I believe him in what is further than that. I believe him in report from heaven in the morning or evening. That is why Abu Bakr was called Al-Siddiq.” Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn al-Sa’ib al-Kalbi told me on the authority of Abu Salih Bazan on the authority of Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib regarding the Night Journey of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she used to say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not taken on the Night Journey except that he was in my house sleeping with me that night. He prayed the last ‘Isha’ prayer, then slept and we slept. When it was just before dawn, we woke up with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when he prayed the morning prayer and we prayed with him, he said: O Umm Hani’, I prayed the last ‘Isha’ prayer with you as you saw in this valley, then I came to Jerusalem and prayed in it, then I prayed the morning prayer with you now as you see.” Al-Kalbi is abandoned once and is omitted, but Abu Ya’la narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Ansari on the authority of Damrah ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Amr al-Shaibani on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Umm Hani’ with a more detailed chain of transmission than this, so let it be written here. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abd al-A’la ibn Abi al-Masawir on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Umm Hani’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spent the night there. The night he was taken on the Night Journey in my house, I missed him during the night, and I could not sleep for fear that some of the Quraysh might have attacked him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to me and took me by the hand and led me out. At the door was a beast smaller than a mule and larger than a donkey. He carried me on it and then set off until he brought me to the Holy House. He showed me Abraham, peace be upon him, whose creation resembled mine and whose creation resembled his. He showed me Moses, Adam, tall and with straight hair. I likened him to the men of Azd Shanu’ah. He showed me Jesus, son of Mary, stocky, white, tinged with redness. I likened him to Urwah ibn Mas’ud al-Thaqafi. He showed me the Antichrist, whose right eye was anointed. I likened him to Qatan ibn Abd al-Uzza.” He said: “I wanted to go out to the Quraysh and tell them what I had seen, so I took hold of his garment and said: ‘I remind you of God. You go to your people and they deny you and reject your words, so I fear that they will attack you. ’ She said: ‘He struck his garment from my hand and then went out to them. He came to them while they were sitting and told them what he had told me. Then Jubayr ibn Mut’im stood up and said: O Muhammad, if you had the status you have, you would not have spoken what you spoke while you were among us. A man from the people said: O Muhammad, did you pass by our camels in such and such a place? He said: Yes, by God, I found that they had lost one of their camels and are searching for it. He said: Did you pass by so-and-so’s camels? He said: Yes, I found them in such and such a place and their red she-camel had broken down, and they had a bowl of water with them so I drank what was in it. They said: Tell us how many of them are there, and who are the shepherds? He said: I was busy counting them and slept, and the camels were brought to him, so he counted them and learned what shepherds were among them. Then he went to Quraysh and said to them: You asked me about the camels of Banu So-and-so, and they are such and such, and among them are so-and-so and so-and-so the shepherds. You asked me about the camels of Banu So-and-so, and they are such and such, and among them are the shepherds Ibn Abi Quhafah and so-and-so and so-and-so, and they will meet you in the morning at the pass. He said: So they sat at the pass waiting for the truthful one of them in what he said, so they faced the camels and asked them: Have you lost any of your camels? They said: Yes. So they asked the other, Did you ever break a red camel? They said: Yes. They said: Did you have a bowl? Abu Bakr said: By God, I placed it down, and no one drank it or poured it on the ground. So Abu Bakr believed him and had faith in him, and he was called the Truthful One that day. Chapter If we are able to compile all these hadiths, their authentic, good and weak, we will obtain the content of what they agreed upon regarding the Prophet’s Night Journey (peace be upon him) from Mecca to Jerusalem, and that it was a single time, even if the narrators’ expressions differed in conveying it, or some of them added to it or omitted from it, because error is permissible for anyone other than the prophets (peace be upon them). Whoever among the people makes every narration that contradicts the other one time separately, and establishes multiple Night Journeys, has gone far and strange, and fled to no escape, and did not obtain his goal. Some of the later scholars have stated that he (peace be upon him) was taken on a Night Journey once from Mecca to Jerusalem only, and once from Mecca to heaven only, and once to Jerusalem and from there to heaven, and he was happy with this path, and that he had obtained something that would free him from the problems, and this is very far-fetched, and this was not transmitted from any of the predecessors, and if this multiplicity had been repeated, the Prophet (peace be upon him) would have informed his nation about it, and people would have transmitted it in multiplicity and repetition. Musa bin Uqbah Al-Zuhri said: The Night Journey was one year before the Hijra, and Urwah said the same. Al-Suddi said: “Sixteen months. The truth is that he, peace be upon him, was taken on a night journey while awake, not asleep, from Mecca to the Holy House, riding Al-Buraq. When he reached the door of the mosque, he tied the beast to the door and entered it. He prayed two rak’ahs of greeting the mosque facing its qibla. Then he came to the Mi’raj, which is like a ladder with steps that one ascends. He ascended on it to the lowest heaven, then to the rest of the seven heavens. He was met by those closest to him in each heaven, and he greeted the prophets in the heavens according to their stations and degrees, until he passed by Moses, the one who spoke to God, in the sixth, and Abraham, the friend of God, in the seventh. Then he passed their stations, may God bless him and grant him peace, and upon them and upon all the prophets, until he reached a level where he heard the creaking of the pens, that is, the pens of destiny regarding what is to come. He saw the Lote Tree of the Limit, and it was covered by the command of God Almighty with a great magnificence of a bed of gold and various colors, and the angels covered it. He saw Gabriel there in his form, and he had six hundred wings. He saw a green flap that filled the horizon. He saw the Frequented House, and Abraham, the friend of God, the builder.” The Kaaba on earth was his back, because it was the heavenly Kaaba, and seventy thousand angels entered it every day to worship in it, and then they did not return to it until the Day of Resurrection. He saw Paradise and Hell, and God imposed fifty prayers upon him there, then reduced them to five, out of His mercy and kindness to His servants. In this there is great concern for the honor and greatness of prayer. Then he descended to Jerusalem and the prophets descended with him and he prayed with them there when the time for prayer came, and it is possible that it was the dawn of that day, and some people claim that he led them in heaven, and what the narrations agree upon is that he was in Jerusalem, but in some of them it is that it was his first entry into it. And it appears that it was after his return to it because when he passed by them in their homes he began to ask Gabriel about them one by one, and he informed him about them, and this is appropriate, because he was first sought by the upper side to impose upon him and his nation what God Almighty willed, then when he finished what was wanted for him, he and his brothers from the prophets met with him and then he showed his honor and superiority over them by his precedence in the imamate, and that was from Gabriel’s indication to him in that. Then he left Jerusalem, rode Al-Buraq and returned to Mecca at dawn. And God Almighty knows best. As for the presentation of vessels of milk and honey, or milk and wine, or milk and water, or all of them, it has been reported that he was in Jerusalem, and it has been reported that he was in heaven. It is possible that it was here and there, because it is like hospitality for the newcomer. And God knows best. Then the people differed: Was the Isra’ with his body, peace be upon him, and his soul, or with his soul only? According to two opinions, the majority of scholars are of the opinion that he was taken on a night journey with his body and soul while awake, not in a dream, and they do not deny that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had seen a dream before that and then saw it after waking up, because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not see a vision except that it came like the break of dawn, and the evidence for this is the saying of God the Almighty: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed. So glorification is only for great matters, so if it were a dream, there would be nothing great in it, and it would not have been considered great, and the infidels of Quraysh would not have rushed to deny it, and a group of those who had converted to Islam would not have apostatized. Also, the servant is a combination of the soul and the body, and God the Almighty said: He took His servant on a night journey and God the Almighty said: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except a trial for the people. Ibn Abbas said: It is a vision of the eye that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw on the night of his night journey, and the cursed tree is the tree of Zaqqum, narrated by al-Bukhari, and God the Almighty said: The sight did not swerve, nor did it turn aside. He became overwhelmed, and sight is one of the instruments of the self, not the soul. Also, it is attributed to Al-Buraq, which is a white, shiny creature with a luster. This only applies to the body, not the soul, because it does not need a vehicle to ride on in its movement. And God knows best. Others said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on a night journey in spirit, not in body. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said in the Seerah: Yaqub bin Utbah bin Al-Mughirah bin Al-Akhns told me that when Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan was asked about the night journey of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would say: It was a true vision from God. Some of the family of Abu Bakr told me that Aisha used to say: The body of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not lost, but his soul was taken on a night journey. Ibn Ishaq said: He did not deny that from her saying, because Al-Hasan said that this verse was revealed: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people and because God said in the report about Abraham: Indeed, I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you, so see what you think. He said: Then he continued on with that, and I knew that revelation comes to the prophets from God while they are awake and asleep. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: My eyes sleep but my heart is awake. And God knows best, which of these had come to him and what he saw from God in it, in whatever state he was in, whether he was asleep or awake, all of that is true and correct. End of the words of Ibn Ishaq. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir followed him in his interpretation with refutation, denial and denunciation, that this is contrary to the apparent context of the Qur’an, and he mentioned some of the evidence for his refutation of what was mentioned above, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Naim Al-Isfahani narrated in his book, Dala’il Al-Nubuwwah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Umar Al-Waqidi: Malik bin Abi Al-Rijal told me, on the authority of Amr bin Abdullah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Dihya bin Khalifa to Caesar, and mentioned his arrival and his arrival to him. The context is a great indication of the abundance of Heraclius’s intelligence. Then he summoned the merchants of Ash-Sham, and Abu Sufyan Sakhr bin Harb and his companions were brought to him. He asked them about those famous issues that were narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, as will be explained. Abu Sufyan tried hard to belittle him and make him seem small in his eyes. He said in this context on the authority of Abu Sufyan: By God, nothing prevented me from saying something about him that would make him lose his respect except that I hate to tell a lie in his presence that he would take from me and not believe me in anything. He said: Until I remembered his statement on the night of his Night Journey. He said: So I said, O King, shall I not tell you something that you will know has been lied? He said: What is it? He said: I said that he claims to us that he left our land, the land of the sanctuary, in one night and came to your mosque, this mosque of yours, the mosque of Ilya, and returned to us that night before morning. He said: And the road of Ilya is at the head of Caesar, so the road of Ilya said: I knew that night, he said: Caesar looked at him and said: How do you know this? He said: I did not sleep a night until I closed the doors of the mosque, and when that night came, I closed all the doors except one door that overcame me, so I called upon my workers and all those who were present to help him, so I dealt with him, but he overcame us and we were unable to move him as if we were climbing a mountain with him, so I called the stonemasons to him, and they looked at him and said: This door was fallen on by the chandeliers and the buildings, and we cannot move it until morning and we see from where it came. He said: So I returned and left the two doors open. When morning came, I went to it, and the stone in the corner of the mosque was perforated, and there was a trace of a tethered animal in it. He said: I said to my companions, This door was not closed tonight except for a prophet, and he prayed tonight in our mosque, and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Benefit Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Khattab Omar bin Dihya said in his book Al-Tanweer fi Mawlid Al-Siraj Al-Munir and he mentioned the Hadith of Al-Isra’ from the path of Anas and spoke about it well and benefited, then he said: The narrations in the Hadith of Al-Isra’ have been transmitted in succession from Omar bin Al-Khattab, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Abu Dharr, Malik bin Sa’sa’ah, Abu Hurairah, Abu Saeed, Ibn Abbas, Shaddad bin Aws, Ubayy bin Ka’b, Abd Al-Rahman bin Qurt, Abu Hubbah, Abu Laila Al-Ansariyyin, Abdullah bin Amr, Jabir, Hudhayfah, Buraydah, Abu Ayoub, Abu Umamah, Samurah bin Jundub, Abu Al-Hamra’, Suhaib Al-Rumi, Umm Hani’, Aisha, and Asma’, the daughters of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them all, some of them narrated it in full, and some of them abbreviated it to what was found in the Musnads, even if the narration of some of them did not meet the conditions of authenticity, so the Hadith of Al-Isra’ was agreed upon by the Muslims, and the heretics and atheists turned away from it. They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God will perfect His light, even if… The infidels hated it. When God Almighty mentioned that He took His servant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Night Journey, He followed it up with the mention of Moses, His servant and Messenger, and His interlocutor as well. God Almighty often links the mention of Moses and Muhammad, may God bless them and grant them peace, with the mention of the Torah and the Qur’an. This is why He said after mentioning the Night Journey, And We gave Moses the Scripture, meaning the Torah, and made it, meaning the Scripture, a guide, meaning a guide, for the Children of Israel, that you take not, meaning so that you do not take besides Me a protector, meaning a guardian, nor a helper, nor a deity other than Me, because God Almighty revealed to every prophet He sent that they should worship Him alone, with no partner for Him. Then he said: The descendants of those We carried with Noah. The meaning is: O descendants of those We carried with Noah. This is an exhortation and a reminder of the favor, meaning: O descendants of those We saved and carried with Noah in the ship, resemble your father. Indeed, he was a grateful servant. So remember My favor upon you by sending you Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It has been reported in the hadith and in the tradition from the predecessors that Noah, peace be upon him, used to thank God for his food, drink, clothing, and all his affairs. For this reason, he was called a grateful servant. Al-Tabarani said: Ali bin Abdul Aziz told me, Abu Naim told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abdullah bin Sinan, on the authority of Saad bin Masoud Al-Thaqafi, who said: Noah was called a grateful servant because whenever he ate or drank, he would thank God. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Usamah told us, Zakariya bin Abi Zaida told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Burdah, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God is pleased with the servant who eats a meal or drinks a drink and praises God for it. This is how Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Abu Usamah. Malik said on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam: He used to praise God in every situation. Al-Bukhari mentioned here the hadith of Abu Zur’ah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection - in its entirety and in it - and they will come to Noah and say: O Noah, you are the first of the messengers to the people of the earth, and God has named you a grateful servant, so intercede for us with your Lord.” And he mentioned the hadith in its entirety.
