17:11: God Almighty tells us about man’s haste and his occasional supplication for evil upon himself, his children, or his wealth, i.e., death, destruction, damnation, and the like. If his Lord had answered him, he would have been destroyed by his supplication, as God Almighty said, And if God were to hasten evil for the people, the verse. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah interpreted it this way. It was mentioned earlier in the hadith, Do not supplicate against yourselves or your wealth, lest you happen to encounter a time when God answers. Rather, what drives the son of Adam to do this is his anxiety and haste. For this reason, God Almighty said, And man is ever hasty. Salman al-Farsi and Ibn Abbas mentioned here the story of Adam, peace be upon him, when he intended to stand up before the soul reached his feet. This was because the breath came to him from his head, and when it reached his brain, he sneezed and said, Praise be to God. God Almighty said, May your Lord have mercy on you, O Adam. When it reached his eyes, he opened them. When it reached his limbs and body, he began to look at it and admire it. He wanted to get up before it reached his feet, but he could not. He said: O Lord, hurry before nightfall. 11- And man invokes evil. Here, what is meant by man is the species, as this supplication occurs from some of its individuals, which is a man’s supplication against himself and his children when he is annoyed with something he does not like to be answered. His supplication for good means like his supplication to his Lord for good for himself and his family, such as asking for well-being, provision, and the like. If God answered his supplication for evil against himself, he would perish, but He did not answer it out of His favor and mercy. Similar to that is And if God were to hasten evil for people as they hasten good, which has been mentioned previously. It has been said that what is meant by man here who says this statement is the disbeliever who supplicates for evil for himself, which is hastening the punishment. He supplicates for good, like the saying of someone: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. It was said that he calls for what is forbidden as he calls for what is permissible, and the waw was deleted from and man calls for in the script of the Qur’an because it is not pronounced with the silent lam after it, like his saying: We will call the guards “and God will erase falsehood” and God will give to the believers and the like, and man is ever hasty meaning he is naturally hasty, and from his haste he asks for evil as he asks for good, and it was said that it refers to Adam, peace be upon him, when he arose before the soul was completed in him, and what is appropriate to the context is the first. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, {And We decreed for the Children of Israel}, that he said: We informed them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, that he said: We informed them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, that he said: We informed them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, that he said: We decreed for the Children of Israel: We decided upon them. Ibn Asakir narrated in his history on the authority of Ali, regarding His statement, {You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice}, that he said: The first time was the killing of Zakariya, and the second time was the killing of John. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, regarding the verse, that he said: The first corruption was the killing of Zakariya, then God sent against them the king of the Nabataeans, then the Children of Israel prepared and attacked the Nabataeans and defeated them, so this is what His statement, {And We gave you back the upper hand over them}. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: God sent against them the first time Goliath, and the second time He sent against them Nebuchadnezzar, so they returned, so God gave power over them to the believers. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, {And they roamed}, that he said: They walked. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him that he said: Destruction means annihilation. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement, Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you, that he said: The mercy that He promised them was sending Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdur-Razzaq Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement, And if you return, We will return, that he said: So they returned, and God Almighty sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them, and they pay the jizyah willingly while they were humiliated. Note that the narrations differ regarding the specification of what happened to them in the two cases, and regarding the person God gave authority over them, and regarding the manner of vengeance against them, but this is not of much benefit. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers, that he said: A prison. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him. He said: The meaning of a prison is that God made their abode in it. Abd al-Razzaq Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding his statement, a mat, that he said: a mattress and a cradle. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement, Indeed, this Qur’an guides to that which is most upright, that he said: to that which is most correct. Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he used to recite often, Indeed, this Qur’an guides to that which is most upright and gives good tidings, with the emphasis. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And man invokes evil as he invokes good, meaning that man says, O God, curse him and be angry with him. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement, And man is ever hasty, that he said: impatient, with no patience in times of ease or hardship. Ibn Abi Shaybah Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Salman al-Farisi that he said: The first thing that God created of Adam was his head. He watched while it was being created, and his feet remained. Then, after the afternoon, he said, O Lord, hasten before nightfall. That is why God said, And man is ever hasty.
17:12: God Almighty bestows His great blessings upon His creation, among them His distinction between night and day so that they may rest at night and spread out during the day for livelihoods, crafts, work and travel, and so that they may know the number of days, gatherings, months and years, and know the passing of the appointed terms for debts, worship, transactions, rents and other things. For this reason, He said: That you may seek bounty from your Lord meaning in your livelihoods, travels and the like, and that you may know the number of years and the account because if all of time were one system and an equal method, none of that would be known, as God Almighty said: “Say, ‘Have you considered: if God made the night continuous for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God could bring you light? Then will you not hear?’ Say, ‘Have you considered: if God made the day continuous for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God could bring you a night in which to rest? Then will you not see?’ And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty and that you may attain knowledge.” And God the Almighty said: “Blessed is He who has placed constellations in the heaven and placed therein a lamp and an illuminating moon. And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires to be grateful.” And God the Almighty said: And to Him belongs the alternation of the night and the day. And He said: “He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night. And He has subjected the sun and the moon. Each runs for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.” And God the Almighty said: “He who splits the dawn and makes the night for rest and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.” And God the Almighty said: “And a sign for them is the night. We strip thereof the day, and at once they are in darkness. And the sun runs to its resting place. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.” Then God the Almighty made a sign for the night, that is, a mark by which it is known, which is darkness and the appearance of the moon in it, and a sign for the day, which is light and the rising of the luminous sun in it. He distinguished between the light of the moon and the brightness of the sun so that one may be known from the other, as God the Almighty said: “It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and account. God did not create that except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know. Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day and what God has created in the heavens and the earth Signs for a people who fear God. God Almighty said: “They ask you about the new moons. Say, ‘They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj.’” Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Abdullah ibn Kathir regarding the statement of God, {So We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible}, he said: The darkness of the night and the curtain of the day. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid: The sun is a sign of the day and the moon is a sign of the night. {So We erased the sign of the night}, he said: The blackness in the moon, and God created it that way. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: The moon used to shine as the sun shines, and the moon is a sign of the night, and the sun is a sign of the day, so We erased the sign of the night, the blackness in the moon. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir narrated through multiple good chains of narration that Ibn al-Kawwa` asked the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, saying: O Commander of the Faithful, what is this spot on the moon? He said: Woe to you, do you not read the Quran? He said: So We erased the sign of the night, and this is its erasure. Qatada said about His statement: So We erased the sign of the night, we used to say that the erasure of the sign of the night was the blackness of the moon in it, and We made the sign of the day visible, that is, luminous, and the creation of the sun is more luminous than the moon and greater. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We made the night and the day two signs, meaning night and day, that is how God Almighty created them.
17:13: God Almighty says after mentioning time and the deeds that occur in it of the children of Adam: And We have fastened to the neck of every man his bird. His bird is what flew away from him of his deeds, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others said, of good and evil, and he is bound by it and is rewarded for it, “So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.” And God Almighty said: “On the right and on the left he is seated. Not a word does he utter but there is an observer by him, ever present.” And He said: “And indeed, over you are keepers, * Noble and recording. * They know what you do.” And He said: You will only be recompensed for what you used to do. And He said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. The point is that the deeds of the son of Adam are recorded for him, whether little or much, and are recorded for him night and day, morning and evening. Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The bird of every person is around his neck. Ibn Lahi’ah said: He means the bad omen. This statement by Ibn Lahi’ah in interpreting this hadith is very strange, and God knows best. And His statement: And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find wide open. That is, We will gather all of his deeds in a book which he will be given on the Day of Resurrection, either in his right hand if he is blessed, or in his left if he is miserable. Wide open, that is, open, so that he and others will read in it all of his deeds from the beginning of his life to the end. "On that Day, man will be informed of what he sent forth and what he left behind. Rather, man is a witness against himself, even if he puts forth his excuses." For this reason, God the Almighty said: "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant." That is, you have not been wronged, and nothing has been written against you except what you did, because you remembered everything that you did, and no one forgets anything that he did. Everyone reads his record, whether he is a writer or an illiterate. And His statement: We fastened his bird to his neck only mentioned the neck because it is an organ among the organs that has no equal in the body, and whoever is bound by something in it has no escape from it, as the poet said. Go with it, go with it, I'll put a dove's collar around it Qatada said on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There is no contagion and no bad omen, and we have bound every person’s bad omen to his neck. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it. Imam Abd ibn Hamid narrated it in his Musnad in a continuous chain of transmission, and he said: Al-Hasan ibn Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The bad omen of every servant is to his neck. Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Yazid told me that Abu al-Khair told him that he heard Uqbah bin Amir, may God be pleased with him, narrating on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is no deed of a day but that it is sealed for it. So when a believer falls ill, the angels say: O our Lord, Your servant so-and-so has been detained. Then the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, says: Seal him with a deed like his until he recovers or dies.” Its chain of transmission is good and strong, and they did not include it in their collections. Muammar said on the authority of Qatada: And We have fastened his deeds to his neck meaning his deeds. And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection meaning: We will bring out that deed. A book which he will find spread wide. Muammar said: Al-Hasan Al-Basri recited: On the right and on the left, seated. O son of Adam, your record has been spread out for you, and two noble angels have been assigned to you, one on your right and the other on your left. As for the one on your right, he will record your good deeds, and as for the one on your left, he will record your bad deeds. So do whatever you wish, less or more, until when you die, your record will be folded and placed around your neck with you in your grave, until you bring out on the Day of Resurrection a book which you will find spread wide. Read your record, the verse, for God has done justice who made you the judge of yourself. This is one of the best words of Al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him.

O son of Adam, your record has been spread out for you, and two noble angels have been assigned to you, one on your right and the other on your left. 17:15: The Almighty informs that whoever is guided and follows the truth, and follows the path of prophethood, then the good outcome of that is for himself, and whoever goes astray that is from the truth, and deviates from the path of guidance, then he only reaps the consequences for himself, and the consequences of that will only come back to him, then He said: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another meaning no one shall bear the sin of another, and no bearer of burdens shall reap except for himself, as the Almighty said: And if a heavily laden soul calls to bear it, nothing of it shall be borne and there is no contradiction between this and His statement: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens in addition to their burdens and His statement: And of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge for the callers bear the sin of their misguidance in themselves, and another sin because of what they misled those whom they misled without diminishing the burdens of those, and He does not bear anything from them, and this is from the justice of God and His mercy towards His servants, and likewise His statement, the Almighty: And We never punish until We have sent a Messenger informing about His justice, the Most High, and that He does not punish anyone except after the proof has been established against him by sending a messenger to him, as in His saying, the Most High: “Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, ‘Did there not come to you a warner? ’ They will say, ‘Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied and said, ‘God has not sent down anything. You are not but in great error. ’” And likewise His saying, “And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened and its keepers will say to them, ‘Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours? ’ They will say, ‘Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers. ’” And the Most High said, “And they will cry out therein, ‘Our Lord, take us out; we will do righteousness other than what we used to do. Did We not grant you life long enough for whoever would remember therein to remember? And a warner has come to you, so taste [it], for there is no helper for the wrongdoers. ’” And other verses indicating that God, the Most High, does not admit anyone into Hell except after sending a messenger to him. Hence, a group of scholars have criticized the word that came with an emphatic letter in Sahih al-Bukhari when He, the Most High, said, Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good. Abdullah bin Saad told us, Yaqoub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Salih bin Kaysan, on the authority of Al-Araj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Paradise and Hell have argued. Then he mentioned the hadith until he said: As for Paradise, God does not wrong any of His creation, and He creates for Hell a creation and they are thrown into it, and it says, ‘Is there more?’ three times. Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith. This only came about Paradise, because it is the abode of bounty. As for Hell, it is the abode of justice, and no one enters it except after he has been excused and the proof has been established against him. A group of hadith masters spoke about this wording and said: Perhaps it was turned against the narrator, based on what they included in the two Sahihs. The wording is from al-Bukhari from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Hammam on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Paradise and Hell have argued. Then he mentioned the hadith until he said: “As for Hell, it will not be filled until he places his foot in it, and it will say: ‘Enough, enough.’ Then it will be filled and some parts will withdraw into others. And God does not wrong anyone of His creation. As for Paradise, God will create new creations for it.” There remains here an issue that the Imams, may God have mercy on them, have differed about in the past and present, which is the children who died while they were young and their fathers were infidels: What is their ruling? And the same applies to the insane, the deaf, the senile old man, and the one who died during the interval and the call did not reach him? There are hadiths about them that I will mention to you with the help and guidance of God, then we will mention a summary section of the Imams’ words on that, and God is the source of help. The first hadith is on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Sari’. Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Muadh bin Hisham told us, my father told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf bin Qais, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Sari’ that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Four people will argue on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:a deaf man who hears nothing, an insane man, an old man, and a man who died during a period of stagnation. As for the deaf man, he will say: ‘O Lord, Islam came and I did not hear anything.’ As for the insane man, he will say: ‘O Lord, Islam came and the children were pelting me with dung.’ As for the old man, he will say: ‘O Lord, Islam came and I did not understand anything.’ As for the one who died during a period of stagnation, he will say: ‘O Lord, no messenger of yours came to me.’ Then he will take their covenants to obey him, and he will send to them to enter the Fire. By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if they were to enter it, it would be cool and safe for them.” And with the chain of transmission on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Abu Rafi’ on the authority of Abu Hurairah, similarly, except that he said at the end of it: Whoever enters it, it will be cool and safe for him, and whoever does not enter it will be dragged to it. And this is how Ishaq bin Rahawayh narrated it on the authority of Muadh bin Hisham, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in the Book of Belief from the hadith of Ahmad bin Ishaq on the authority of Ali bin Abdullah Al-Madani with it, and he said: This is a sound chain of transmission. And this is how Hammad bin Salamah narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Zaid on the authority of Abu Rafi’ on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Four, each of whom provides proof for God, and he mentioned something similar. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Hammam on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and he mentioned it as a continuation of the verse. Then Abu Hurair said: So recite, if you wish, And We never punish until We have sent a messenger. And this is how Muammar narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Tawus on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah as a continuation of the verse. The second hadith On the authority of Anas bin Malik, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Al-Rabi’ told us on the authority of Yazid bin Abaan, who said: We said to Anas: O Abu Hamza, what do you say about the children of the polytheists? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “They did not have any bad deeds for which they would be punished, so they would be among the people of Hellfire, and they did not have any good deeds for which they would be rewarded, so they would be among the people of Paradise.” The third hadith also on the authority of Anas. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Abu Khaithama told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Laith on the authority of Abdul-Warith, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Four will be brought on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:the newborn, the insane, the one who died during the interval, and the old, decrepit man. Each of them will speak with his proof.” Then the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, will say: A neck of Hell will emerge, and He will say to them: I used to send to My servants messengers from among themselves, and I am the Messenger of Myself to you. Enter this. He said: Then the one for whom misery was decreed will say: O Lord, how can we enter it when we used to flee from it? He said: And the one for whom happiness was decreed will go on and rush into it quickly. He said: Then God, the Most High, will say: You are the most vehement in denying and disobeying My messengers. So these will enter Paradise and those will enter Hell. And this is how Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Yusuf bin Musa on the authority of Jarir bin Abdul-Hamid with his chain of transmission similarly. Hadith 4 On the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, may God be pleased with him. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili also said in his Musnad: Qasim bin Abi Shaybah told us, Abdullah, meaning Ibn Dawud, told us, on the authority of Umar bin Dhir, on the authority of Yazid bin Umayya, on the authority of Al-Bara’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the children of the Muslims, and he said: They are with their fathers. And he was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: They are with their fathers. So it was said: O Messenger of God, what do they do? He said: God knows best about them. And it was narrated by Umar bin Dhir, on the authority of Yazid bin Umayya, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Bara’, on the authority of Aisha, and he mentioned it. The fifth hadith on the authority of Thawban. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Amr bin Abdul Khaliq Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari told us, Rayhan bin Saeed told us, Ibad bin Mansour told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu Asma, on the authority of Thawban that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, emphasized the importance of questioning. He said, “When the Day of Resurrection comes, the ignorant will come carrying their burdens on their backs, and their Lord will question them, saying, ‘Our Lord, you did not send us a messenger, and no command from you came to us. If you had sent us a messenger, we would have been the most obedient of your servants.’ Their Lord will say to them, ‘Have you seen that if I command you to do something, will you obey me?’ They will say, ‘Yes.’ So He will order them to go to Hell and enter it. They will set out, and when they come close to it, they will find it raging and sighing, so they will return to their Lord, and they will say, ‘Our Lord, take us out or save us from it.’ He will say to them, ‘Did you not claim that if I commanded you to do something, you would obey me?’ So He will take their covenants and say, ‘Go to it.’” So enter it. They set out until, when they see it, they are afraid of it and return and say: Our Lord, we are afraid of it and we cannot enter it. He says: Enter it in awe. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If they had entered it the first time, it would have been cool and safe for them. Then Al-Bazzar said: The text of this hadith is not known except from this source. It was not narrated from Ayoub except by Ibad, and from Ibad except by Rayhan bin Saeed. I said: Ibn Hayyan mentioned him among his trustworthy ones, and Yahya bin Ma’in and Al-Nasa’i said: There is nothing wrong with him, but Abu Dawud did not approve of him, and Abu Hatim said: He is a sheikh who is not bad. His hadith is written down but it is not used as evidence. The sixth hadith On the authority of Abu Saeed Saad bin Malik bin Sinan Al-Khudri. Imam Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Dhahali said: Saeed bin Sulaiman narrated to us on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The one who perishes during the interval, the insane, and the newborn, the one who perishes during the interval will say: No book came to me, and the insane will say: O Lord, You have not given me a mind with which to understand good or evil, and the newborn will say: O Lord, I did not attain the mind, so a fire will be raised for them and it will be said to them: Return it, he said: So the one who was happy in the knowledge of God if he had attained the action will return it, and the one who was miserable in the knowledge of God if he had attained the action will be held back from it, and he will say: You disobeyed Me, so how would it be if My messengers had come to you?!” And thus Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Omar bin Hayaj Al-Kufi on the authority of Ubaid God bin Musa on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq on his authority. Then he said: It is not known from the hadith of Abu Saeed except through his chain of transmission on the authority of Atiyah on his authority. And he said at the end of it: “Then God says: You disobeyed Me, so how about My messengers in the unseen?” The seventh hadith On the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, Hisham ibn Ammar and Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak al-Suri said: Amr ibn Waqid narrated to us on the authority of Yunus ibn Halbas on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal on the authority of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “On the Day of Resurrection, the one who was transformed in his intellect, the one who perished during the interval, and the one who perished as a child will be brought. The transformed one will say: O Lord, if You had given me intellect, the one to whom You had given intellect would not have been happier than me.” And he mentioned something similar about the one who perished during the interval and the child. “The Lord, the Almighty, will say: I command you to do something and you obey me? They will say: Yes. He will say: Go and enter the Fire. He said: Even if they entered it, it would not have harmed them. Then grippers will come out upon them and they will think that it has destroyed everything God has created, so they will quickly return. Then He will command them a second time, and they will return in the same manner. The Lord, the Almighty, will say: Before I created you, I knew what you would do, and based on My knowledge I created you, and to My knowledge you will return. I will gather them.” Then the fire will take them. Hadith 8 On the authority of Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Every child is born in a state of fitrah pure natural disposition, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian, just as an animal gives birth whole. Do you see any among them with their ears cut off?” In another narration, they said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of one who dies young? He said: God knows best what they would have done. Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Thabit told us, on the authority of Ata bin Qurrah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Damrah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), as far as I know - Musa was uncertain - he said: “The children of the Muslims will be in Paradise, and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) will be responsible for them.” In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Iyad bin Himar, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), on the authority of God the Almighty, that He said: Indeed, I created My servants as monotheists, and in another narration: Muslims. Hadith 9 On the authority of Samurah, may God be pleased with him. It was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Barqani in his book Al-Mustakhraj ‘ala Al-Bukhari from the hadith of Awf Al-A’rabi. On the authority of Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi, on the authority of Samurah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Every newborn is born in a state of fitrah pure disposition. The people called out to him: O Messenger of God, what about the children of the polytheists? He said: And the children of the polytheists. At-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Ahmad told us, Uqbah bin Makram Ad-Dhabi told us, on the authority of ‘Isa bin Shu’aib, on the authority of ‘Ibad bin Mansur, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Samurah, who said: “We asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the children of the polytheists, and he said: ‘They are the servants of the people of Paradise.’” The tenth hadith On the authority of Hasna’s uncle, Ahmad said: Ruh told us, Aouf told us on the authority of Hasna’ bint Mu’awiyah, from Bani Sareem, who said: My uncle told me: I said: O Messenger of God, who will be in Paradise? The Prophet said: In Paradise, the martyr will be in Paradise, the one who was born will be in Paradise, and the one who was buried alive will be in Paradise. Some scholars stopped at them for this hadith, and some of them were certain that they will be in Paradise, based on the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub in Sahih al-Bukhari, that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said in the context of that dream when he passed by that old man under the tree and there were children around him, and Gabriel said to him: This is Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and these are the children of the Muslims and the children of the polytheists. They said: O Messenger of God, and the children of the polytheists? He said: Yes, and the children of polytheists. Some of them were certain that they would go to Hell, based on the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): They will be with their fathers. Some of them went to the fact that they will be tested on the Day of Resurrection in the plains, so whoever obeys will enter Paradise and God will reveal to them their previous happiness, and whoever disobeys will enter Hell as a humiliated person and God's knowledge of them will be revealed due to their previous misery. This statement combines all the evidence, and the previous hadiths that support each other have clearly stated it. This statement is what Sheikh Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ismail al-Ash'ari narrated from the people of the Sunnah and the community, and it is what Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi supported in his book al-I'tiqad, as well as other scholars, hadith masters, and critics. Sheikh Abu Omar ibn Abdul-Barr al-Namri mentioned it after the previous hadiths about testing, then he said: The hadiths of this chapter are not strong and do not constitute evidence, and the people of knowledge deny them, because the Hereafter is a place of reward and not a place of work or trial, so how can they be charged with entering Hell, and that is not within the capacity of the creatures, and God does not charge a soul except with what it can bear? The answer to what he said is that the hadiths of this chapter include those that are authentic, as many of the imams of the scholars have stated, and those that are good, and those that are weak, which are strengthened by the authentic and the good. If the hadiths of a single chapter are connected and support each other in this manner, they provide evidence for the one who examines them. As for his saying that the Hereafter is the abode of reward, there is no doubt that it is the abode of reward, and it does not contradict the obligation in its courtyards before entering Paradise or Hell, as Sheikh Abu al-Hasan al-Ash’ari narrated from the school of thought of the people of the Sunnah and the Community regarding the testing of children, and God Almighty said: The Day the shin will be laid bare and they will be called to prostrate Al-An’am 2:17. It has been proven in Sahih and other books that the believers will prostrate to God on the Day of Resurrection, and that the hypocrite will not be able to do so, and his back will return to being like a single plate, one plate, and whenever he wants to prostrate, he will fall on his back. In Sahih Al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, regarding the man who will be the last of the people of Hell to leave it, God takes his covenants and pledges that he will not ask for anything other than what he has, and this is repeated many times, and God the Most High says: O son of Adam, how treacherous you are! Then He gives him permission to enter Paradise. As for his saying: How can God order them to enter Hell when that is not within their capacity? This does not prevent the authenticity of the hadith, for God will command the servants on the Day of Resurrection to cross the Sirat, which is a bridge over Hell, sharper than a sword and finer than a hair, and the believers will cross it according to their deeds like lightning and like the wind and like the best horses and riders, and among them are those who run, those who walk, those who crawl, and those who are scratched on their faces in the Fire. What has been reported about those people is not greater than this, rather this is more severe and greater. The Sunnah also proves that the Antichrist will have Paradise and Hell with him. The Lawgiver has commanded the believers who will see him to drink from what he sees as fire, for it will be cool and peaceful for him. This is similar to that. Also, God Almighty commanded the Children of Israel to kill themselves, so they killed each other until they killed, as it was said, seventy thousand in one morning. A man would kill his father and his brother, while they were in the blindness of a cloud that God sent upon them. This is a punishment for them for their worship of the calf. This is also very difficult for the souls, and it does not fall short of what was mentioned in the aforementioned hadith. And God knows best. Chapter If this is established, then people have differed regarding the children of polytheists, with statements one of which is that they are in Paradise. They have cited as evidence the hadith of Samurah that he, peace be upon him, saw with Abraham, peace be upon him, the children of Muslims and the children of polytheists, and what was mentioned in the narration of Ahmad on the authority of Hasna on the authority of her uncle that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: And the child is in Paradise. This is a correct argument, but the hadiths of testing are more specific than that. So whoever God knows will obey, He will place his soul in the Barzakh with Abraham and the children of Muslims who died in accordance with the fitrah, and whoever He knows will not answer, his matter is up to God Almighty on the Day of Resurrection and he will be in the Fire, as indicated by the hadiths of testing, and as Al-Ash’ari transmitted from the people of the Sunnah. Then those who say that they are in Paradise, some of them made them independent in it, and some of them made them servants to them, as came in the hadith of Ali bin Zaid on the authority of Anas according to Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi, and it is weak, and God knows best. The second statement is that they are with their fathers in Hell. And he provided evidence for this with what Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated on the authority of Abu al-Mughira, who narrated to us on the authority of Utbah ibn Damrah ibn Habib, who narrated to me on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Qais, the freed slave of Ghutayf, who came to Aisha and asked her about the children of the infidels, and he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They follow their fathers. I said: O Messenger of God, without deeds? He said: God knows best what they used to do.” Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Harb on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Ilahani, who heard Abdullah ibn Abi Qais, who heard Aisha say: “I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the children of the believers. He said: They are with their fathers. I said: What about the children of the polytheists? He said: They are with their fathers. I said: Without deeds? He said: God knows best what they used to do.” Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Wakee’ on the authority of Abu Uqayl Yahya ibn al-Mutawakkil, who is rejected, on the authority of his freed slave Bahiyyah on the authority of Aisha that she mentioned the children of the polytheists to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: If you wish, I will hear you compete with them in the Fire. Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad narrated: Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Fadil bin Ghazwan, on the authority of Muhammad bin Uthman, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: “Khadijah asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about two of her sons who died in the pre-Islamic era, and he said: They are in Hellfire. He said: When he saw the hatred on her face, he said to her: If you saw where they were, you would hate them. He said: And my sons are from you? He said: The believers and their children are in Paradise, and the polytheists and their children are in Hellfire - then he recited: ‘And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring. ’” This is a strange hadith, because in its chain of transmission is Muhammad bin Uthman, whose status is unknown, and his sheikh Zadan did not meet Ali, and God knows best. Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Ibn Abi Zaidah on the authority of his father on the authority of Al-Sha’bi who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The one who gives birth to a girl and the one who is buried alive are in Hell.’ Then Al-Sha’bi said: ‘Alqamah told me about it on the authority of Abu Wa’il on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. A group of people narrated it on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind on the authority of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Alqamah on the authority of Salamah ibn Qays Al-Ashja’i who said: ‘My brother and I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we said: “Our mother died in the pre-Islamic era, and she used to welcome guests and maintain family ties. She buried our sister alive in the pre-Islamic era who had not yet reached puberty.” He said: ‘The one who gives birth to a girl and the one who is buried alive is in Hell unless the one who gives birth to a girl reaches Islam and becomes Muslim.’’ This is a good chain of transmission. The third opinion is to stop at them. They relied on the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): God knows best what they used to do. It is in the two Sahihs from the hadeeth of Ja’far ibn Abi Iyas from Sa’eed ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: God knows best what they used to do. It is also in the two Sahihs from the hadeeth of al-Zuhri from Ata’ ibn Yazid, and from Abu Salamah from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: God knows best what they used to do. Some of them made them among the people of al-A’raf, and this opinion goes back to the opinion of those who believed that they are among the people of Paradise, because al-A’raf is not a permanent home and the destination of its people is Paradise, as was previously reported in Surat al-A’raf, and God knows best. Chapter And let it be known that this disagreement is specific to the children of polytheists. As for the children of believers, there is no disagreement among the scholars, as Qadi Abu Ya`la ibn al-Farra’ al-Hanbali narrated from Imam Ahmad that he said: There is no disagreement about them being among the people of Paradise. This is what is well-known among the people, and it is what we are certain of, God Almighty willing. As for what Sheikh Abu `Umar ibn `Abd al-Barr mentioned from some scholars that they hesitated about that and that all children are subject to God’s will, Abu `Umar said: A group of scholars of jurisprudence and hadith held this opinion, including Hammad ibn Zayd, Hammad ibn Salamah, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and others. They said: It is similar to what Malik wrote in his Muwatta’ in the chapters on fate, and what he mentioned of hadiths in that regard, and most of his companions held this opinion. There is nothing explicitly stated about Malik in that regard, except that the later ones among his companions held that the children of Muslims are in Paradise and the children of polytheists are specifically subject to God’s will. End of his statement, and it is very strange. Abu `Abdullah al-Qurtubi also mentioned something similar in his book al-Tadhkirah, and God knows best. They also mentioned in this regard the hadith of Aisha bint Talha, on the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was invited to the funeral of a boy from the Ansar, so I said: O Messenger of God, blessed is he, a bird from the birds of Paradise, who did not do evil and did not attain it. He said: Or something else, O Aisha? God created Paradise and created its people while they were in the loins of their fathers. And He created Hell and created its people while they were in the loins of their fathers.” Narrated by Muslim, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah. Since speaking about this issue requires sound and good evidence, and it may be spoken about by someone who has no knowledge of the Lawgiver, a group of scholars disliked speaking about it. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Al-Qasim bin Muhammad bin Abi Bakr Al-Siddiq, Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah, and others. Ibn Hibban included in his Sahih on the authority of Jarir bin Hazim: I heard Abu Raja Al-Attardi, I heard Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, while he was on the pulpit saying: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The affair of this nation will continue to be favorable or close to that as long as they do not speak about parents and destiny.” Ibn Hibban said: He means the children of the polytheists. This is how Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Jarir bin Hazim, then he said: A group narrated it on the authority of Abu Raja on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission ending with him.
17:16: The readers differed in reading his statement We commanded, so the well-known reading is the alleviation, and the commentators differed in its meaning. It was said: Its meaning is that We commanded its affluent people, so they committed an immoral act therein, as in the statement of the Most High: Our command came to them by night or by day, for God does not command immorality. They said: Its meaning is that He subjected them to committing immoral acts, so they deserved punishment. It was also said: Its meaning is that We commanded them to do acts of obedience, so they committed immoral acts, so they deserved punishment. It was narrated by Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Saeed bin Jubayr also said the same. Ibn Jarir said: It is possible that its meaning is that we made them leaders. I said: This only comes according to the reading of those who read We commanded its affluent ones. Ali bin Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement: We commanded its affluent ones, but they disobeyed therein means: We gave authority to its wicked ones, so they disobeyed therein. If they did that, God would destroy them with punishment. This is His statement: And thus have We appointed in every city its greatest criminals Al-Baqarah 2:176. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said the same. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when We desire to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones, but they defiantly disobey therein. He said, We increase their number. This is what Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said. And on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Az-Zuhri: We command its affluent ones means We increase their number. Some of them cited as evidence the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, where he said: Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Abu Nu’aym Al-Adawi told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Badil, on the authority of Iyas bin Zuhair, on the authority of Suwaid bin Hubairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The best wealth of a man is a well-trained mare or a well-tended path. Imam Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam, may God have mercy on him, said in his book Al-Gharib: The well-tended one is the one with many offspring, the path is the well-arranged path of palm trees, and the well-tended one is the pollination. Some of them said: This came in a proportional manner, like his saying, rewarded but not rewarded.
17:17: God the Almighty says, warning the infidels of Quraysh for their denial of His Messenger Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that those who denied the messengers after Noah were destroyed. This indicates that the generations between Adam and Noah were Muslims, as Ibn Abbas said: There were ten generations between Adam and Noah, all of them Muslims. Its meaning is that you, the deniers, are not more honorable to God than them, and you have denied the most honorable of messengers and the most honorable of creation, so your punishment is more deserving and appropriate. And His statement: And sufficient is your Lord as Knower and Seeer of the sins of His servants means that He is All-Knowing of all their deeds: good and bad, nothing is hidden from Him, glory be to Him.
17:18: God Almighty tells us that not everyone who seeks this world and the bliss it contains will obtain it, but rather it will only be obtained by whomever God wills and whatever He wills. This restricts the generality of the other verses, for He said: “We hasten for him therein whatever We will for whomever We will. Then We have made for him Hell” meaning in the Hereafter which he will burn meaning he will enter until it engulfs him from all sides blamed meaning in a state of being blamed for his bad behavior and actions, since he chose the perishable over the eternal rejected banished, excluded, humiliated and disgraced. Imam Ahmad narrated: Hussain told us, Rawid told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Zur’ah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The world is the home of those who have no home, and the wealth of those who have no wealth, and those who have no mind gather for it.’” And his statement: And whoever desires the Hereafter means he desires the Hereafter and what is in it of bliss and joy, and strives for it with the necessary effort means he seeks it through his path, which is following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he is a believer meaning his heart is a believer, meaning he believes in the reward and recompense, their effort is ever appreciated.
17:19: God Almighty tells us that not everyone who seeks this world and the bliss it contains will obtain it, but rather it will only be obtained by whomever God wills and whatever He wills. This restricts the generality of the other verses, for He said: “We hasten for him therein whatever We will for whomever We will. Then We have made for him Hell” meaning in the Hereafter which he will burn meaning he will enter until it engulfs him from all sides blamed meaning in a state of being blamed for his bad behavior and actions, since he chose the perishable over the eternal rejected banished, excluded, humiliated and disgraced. Imam Ahmad narrated: Hussain told us, Rawid told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Zur’ah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The world is the home of those who have no home, and the wealth of those who have no wealth, and those who have no mind gather for it.’” And his statement: And whoever desires the Hereafter means he desires the Hereafter and what is in it of bliss and joy, and strives for it with the necessary effort means he seeks it through his path, which is following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he is a believer meaning his heart is a believer, meaning he believes in the reward and recompense, their effort is ever appreciated.
17:20: God Almighty says: Both meaning each of the two groups who wanted this world and those who wanted the Hereafter, We will provide them with what is in it from the bounty of your Lord meaning He is the Disposer of affairs, the Ruler who does not act unjustly, so He gives each one what he deserves of happiness and misery, so there is no one who can reverse His judgment, nor prevent what He has given, nor change what He wills. For this reason He said And the bounty of your Lord is not forbidden meaning no one can prevent it, nor can anyone reject it. Qatada said: And the gift of your Lord is not restricted, meaning diminished. Al-Hasan and others said: meaning forbidden. Then the Almighty said: See how We have favored some of them over others, meaning in this world. Some of them are rich and some poor, and some are in between, some are handsome and some are ugly, and some die young, and some live to be old and some are in between. And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference, meaning their differences in the Hereafter are greater than in this world. Some of them will be in the lowest levels of Hell and its chains and shackles, and some of them will be in the highest levels and its bliss and joy. Then the people of the lowest levels will differ in what they are in, just as the people of the levels will differ, for Paradise has one hundred levels, and between every two levels is like the distance between the heavens and the earth. In the two Sahihs: The people of the highest ranks will see the people of the highest ranks as you see a distant star in the horizon of the sky. That is why God Almighty said: And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference. And in At-Tabarani, on the authority of Zadan on the authority of Salman, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet: There is no servant who wants to rise a degree in this world and rises, except that God places him in the Hereafter greater than it. Then he recited: And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference.
17:21: God Almighty says: Both meaning each of the two groups who wanted this world and those who wanted the Hereafter, We will provide them with what is in it from the bounty of your Lord meaning He is the Disposer of affairs, the Ruler who does not act unjustly, so He gives each one what he deserves of happiness and misery, so there is no one who can reverse His judgment, nor prevent what He has given, nor change what He wills. For this reason He said And the bounty of your Lord is not forbidden meaning no one can prevent it, nor can anyone reject it. Qatada said: And the gift of your Lord is not restricted, meaning diminished. Al-Hasan and others said: meaning forbidden. Then the Almighty said: See how We have favored some of them over others, meaning in this world. Some of them are rich and some poor, and some are in between, some are handsome and some are ugly, and some die young, and some live to be old and some are in between. And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference, meaning their differences in the Hereafter are greater than in this world. Some of them will be in the lowest levels of Hell and its chains and shackles, and some of them will be in the highest levels and its bliss and joy. Then the people of the lowest levels will differ in what they are in, just as the people of the levels will differ, for Paradise has one hundred levels, and between every two levels is like the distance between the heavens and the earth. In the two Sahihs: The people of the highest ranks will see the people of the highest ranks as you see a distant star in the horizon of the sky. That is why God Almighty said: And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference. And in At-Tabarani, on the authority of Zadan on the authority of Salman, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet: There is no servant who wants to rise a degree in this world and rises, except that God places him in the Hereafter greater than it. Then he recited: And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference.
17:22: God Almighty says, and what is meant are those who are charged with the duty of worship from the nation: Do not, O you who are charged with the duty of worship, make a partner for your Lord, lest you sit blamed, meaning for associating partners with Him, forsaken, because God Almighty does not support you, but rather leaves you to the one you worshipped with, and He does not possess for you harm or benefit, because the One Who possesses harm and benefit is God alone, with no partner for Him. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, Bashir ibn Salman told us, on the authority of Sayyar Abu al-Hakam, on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever is afflicted with poverty and ascribes it to the people, his poverty will not be satisfied, but whoever ascribes it to God, God will send him wealth, either later or immediate wealth. Narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Bashir ibn Salman with it, and al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih Gharib.
17:23: God Almighty says, commanding that He be worshipped alone, with no partner for Him. The word qada’ here means command. Mujahid said, And He decreed means He commanded. This is how Abi bin Ka’b, Ibn Mas’ud, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim read, And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him. This is why He linked His worship with being dutiful to parents, saying, And to parents, good treatment. That is, He commanded that parents be treated well, like His saying in the other verse, “That you be grateful to Me and to your parents. To Me is the final destination.” And His statement, If one or both of them reach old age with you, say not to them a word of disrespect, meaning do not let them hear a bad word, not even a sigh, which is the lowest level of bad speech. And do not scold them, meaning do not do anything bad to them, as Ata’ ibn Rabah said about His statement, And do not scold them, meaning do not shake your hand at them. And when He forbade him from bad speech and bad actions, He ordered him to say and do good, saying, And speak to them a generous word, meaning soft, kind, and good, with politeness, reverence, and respect. And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, meaning be humble to them in your actions. And say, ‘My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small,’ meaning in their old age and upon their death. Ibn Abbas said, Then God revealed, ‘It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists,’ the verse. There are many hadiths about honoring parents, including the hadith narrated by various chains of transmission on the authority of Anas and others, that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended the pulpit, he said: Amen, amen, amen. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Ali bin Zaid told us, Zurarah bin Awfa told us, on the authority of Malik bin Al-Harith, on the authority of a man from among them, that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever takes in an orphan from two Muslim parents, provides him with his food and drink until he no longer needs him, Paradise is guaranteed for him, and whoever frees a Muslim man, his release from the Fire will be rewarded for every limb of his with a limb of his.” Then he said: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Ali bin Zaid, and he mentioned its meaning, except that he said on the authority of a man from his people called Malik or Ibn Malik, and he added, And whoever finds his parents or one of them alive and enters the Fire, God will distance him. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, Ali bin Zaid told us on the authority of Zararah bin Awfa on the authority of Malik bin Amr Al-Qushayri, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever frees a Muslim slave, it is his ransom from the Fire, for every bone of his bones is freed by a bone of his bones. Whoever takes in an orphan from two Muslim parents and provides him with his food and drink until God makes him rich, Paradise is obligatory for him.” Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj and Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us on the authority of Qatadah, I heard Zararah ibn Awfa narrating on the authority of Abi ibn Malik al-Qushayri who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever finds his parents or one of them alive and then enters the Fire after that, may God distance him and crush him. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abu Uwanah told us, Suhayl ibn Abi Salih told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “May his nose be rubbed in the dust, then may... a man who finds one or both of his parents in old age and does not enter Paradise.” It is authentic from this source, and they did not include it except for Muslim from the hadith of Abu Uwanah, Jarir, and Sulayman ibn Bilal on the authority of Suhayl with it. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Rab’i bin Ibrahim told us, Ahmad said, and he was the brother of Ismail bin Aliyah and he was preferred over his brother, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of Sa’id bin Abi Sa’id, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May the nose of a man in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me be rubbed in the dust, and may the nose of a man in whose presence the month of Ramadan comes and passes and he is not forgiven, and may the nose of a man in whose presence his parents reach old age and they do not let him enter Paradise be rubbed in the dust.” Rab’i said: I do not know of anyone except him saying, or one of them. Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj with it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf bin Al-Waleed told us, Ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saad, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, on the authority of Al-Muqaddam bin Ma’dikarib, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God commands you to be kind to your fathers. God commands you to be kind to your mothers. God commands you to be kind to your mothers. God commands you to be kind to your closest relatives.” Ibn Majah included it on the authority of Abdullah bin Ayyash. Another hadith Ahmad said: Yunus told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Salim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man from Banu Yarbu’, who said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I heard him speaking to the people, saying: The upper hand of the giver is your mother and your father, your sister and your brother, then your closest, your closest. Another hadith Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Amr bin Abdul Khaliq Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Ibrahim bin Al-Mustamir Al-Aruqi told us, Amr bin Sufyan told us, Al-Hasan bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of Laith bin Abi Salim, on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad, on the authority of Sulayman bin Buraydah, on the authority of his father, “A man was performing the Tawaf carrying his mother, so he asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you fulfilled her right? He said: No, not even a single sigh,” or something like that. Then Al-Bazzar said: We do not know that it is narrated except from this source. I said: Al-Hasan bin Abi Jaafar is weak, and God knows best.

This is how Abi bin Ka’b, Ibn Mas’ud, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim read, And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him. This is why He linked His worship with being dutiful to parents, saying, And to parents, good treatment. That is, He commanded that parents be treated well, like His saying in the other verse, “That you be grateful to Me and to your parents. To Me is the final destination.” And His statement, If one or both of them reach old age with you, say not to them a word of disrespect, meaning do not let them hear a bad word, not even a sigh, which is the lowest level of bad speech. And do not scold them, meaning do not do anything bad to them, as Ata’ ibn Rabah said about His statement, And do not scold them, meaning do not shake your hand at them. 17:25: Saeed bin Jubair said: He is the man who takes the initiative to his parents, and in his intention and heart that he will not be held accountable for it, and in another narration: He only wants good for that, so he said: Your Lord knows best what is in your souls, if you are righteous. And His statement: For He is ever, to the frequently turning [to God], Forgiving. Qatadah said: For the obedient, the people of prayer, and from Ibn Abbas: Those who glorify God, and in another narration from him: The obedient, the doers of good, and some of them said: They are those who pray between the two evening prayers, and some of them said: They are those who pray the Duha prayer. Shu'bah said from Yahya bin Saeed from Saeed bin Al-Musayyab regarding His statement: For He is ever, to the frequently turning [to God], Forgiving, he said: Those who commit a sin and then repent, and commit a sin and then repent, and Abd Al-Razzaq narrated it likewise from Ath-Thawri and Muammar from Yahya bin Saeed, from Ibn Al-Musayyab in a similar manner, and Al-Layth and Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise from Ibn Al-Musayyab. Ata bin Yasar bin Jubair and Mujahid said: They are those who return to goodness. Mujahid said on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair regarding the verse: He is the one who, when he remembers his sins in the toilet, seeks forgiveness from God for them, and Mujahid agreed with him on that. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muhammad bin Muslim told us on the authority of Amr bin Dinar on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair regarding His statement: For indeed, He is, to the frequently turning [to God], Forgiving. He said: We used to consider the frequently turning [to God] to be the one who remembers and preserves [the sins], who says: O God, forgive me for what I have done in this gathering of mine. Ibn Jarir said: The first opinion is that of those who said: He is the one who repents from sin, who returns from disobedience to obedience from what God dislikes to what He loves and is pleased with. What he said is correct, because the word returning is derived from awwab, which means returning. It is said: So-and-so returned if he returned. God the Almighty said: Indeed, to Us is their return. And in the authentic hadith, it is narrated that when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) returned from a journey, he would say: Returning, repentant, worshipping our Lord, praising Him.
17:26: When God the Almighty mentioned honoring one's parents, He followed it with mentioning kindness to relatives and maintaining kinship ties. In the hadith, Your mother and your father, then your closest, then your closest. In another narration, Then the closest, then the closest. In the hadith, Whoever loves to have his provision expanded and his life extended, let him maintain kinship ties. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abbad ibn Ya’qub told us, Abu Yahya al-Tamimi told us, Fadil ibn Marzouq told us, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: When the verse, And give the near of kin his due, was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Fatimah and gave her Fadak. Then he said: We do not know that anyone narrated it from Fadil ibn Marzouq except Abu Yahya al-Tamimi and Hamid ibn Hammad ibn Abi al-Khawar. This hadith is problematic, even if its chain of transmission is sound, because the verse is Meccan, and Fadak was only conquered with Khaybar in the year seven of the Hijrah. So how can this be reconciled with this? So it is a rejected hadith, and it is most likely that it was fabricated by the Rafidah, and God knows best. We have already discussed the poor and wayfarers in Surat Bara’ah, so there is no need to repeat it here. And His statement, And do not be wasteful, when He commanded spending, He forbade extravagance in it, but rather it should be moderate as He said in the other verse, And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly, the verse, then He said, deterring extravagance and wastefulness, Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, meaning they are similar to them in that. Ibn Masoud said: Extravagance is spending unjustly, and Ibn Abbas said the same. Mujahid said: If a person spent all of his money in the right way, he would not be a wasteful person, but if he spent a mudd unjustly, he would be a wasteful person. Qatada said: Extravagance is spending in disobedience to God, and unjustly and corruptly. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Yazid, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, that he said: “A man from Banu Tamim came to the Messenger of God and said: O Messenger of God, I have a lot of wealth, and I have a family, children, and a city. Tell me how to spend it, and how to act? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Pay zakat from your wealth if you have it, for it is a purification that purifies you, and it connects with your relatives, and it recognizes the rights of the beggar, the neighbor, and the poor. He said: O Messenger of God, give me a little? Give the right of the relative, the poor, and the wayfarer, and do not spend wastefully. He said: It is enough for me, O Messenger of God, if I pay zakat to your messenger, then I have absolved myself of it before God and His Messenger. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, if you pay it to my messenger, then I have absolved myself of it, and you will have its reward, and its sin is upon whoever changes it.” And His statement: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils meaning in their wastefulness, foolishness, abandoning the obedience of God and committing His disobedience. That is why He said: And Satan was ever ungrateful to his Lord meaning ingratitude, because he denied the blessing of God upon him and did not act in obedience to Him, rather he turned to disobeying Him and opposing Him. And His statement: But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord the verse, meaning if your relatives and those We have commanded you to give to ask you and you do not have anything, you turn away from them because of the lack of provision, then speak to them a gentle word meaning promise them with ease and gentleness, if God’s provision comes, then We will provide for you, God willing. This is how His statement: then speak to them a gentle word was interpreted as a promise by Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others.

He said: It is enough for me, O Messenger of God, if I pay zakat to your messenger, then I have absolved myself of it before God and His Messenger. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, if you pay it to my messenger, then I have absolved myself of it, and you will have its reward, and its sin is upon whoever changes it.” And His statement: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils meaning in their wastefulness, foolishness, abandoning the obedience of God and committing His disobedience. That is why He said: And Satan was ever ungrateful to his Lord meaning ingratitude, because he denied the blessing of God upon him and did not act in obedience to Him, rather he turned to disobeying Him and opposing Him. And His statement: But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord the verse, meaning if your relatives and those We have commanded you to give to ask you and you do not have anything, you turn away from them because of the lack of provision, then speak to them a gentle word meaning promise them with ease and gentleness, if God’s provision comes, then We will provide for you, God willing. This is how His statement: then speak to them a gentle word was interpreted as a promise by Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others.
17:29: The Almighty says, commanding moderation in living, blaming miserliness, and forbidding extravagance, And do not make your hand chained to your neck, meaning do not be miserly and withholding, do not give anyone anything, as the Jews said - may God’s curses be upon them - God’s hand is chained, meaning they attributed it to miserliness, the Most High and Most Holy is the Generous Giver. And His saying, And do not extend it completely, meaning do not be extravagant in spending, giving beyond your capacity, and spending more than your income, so that you sit blamed and regretful. This is from the category of twisting and spreading, meaning that if you are miserly, you sit blamed, people blame you and criticize you and do not need you, as Zuhair bin Abi Salma said in the Mu’allaqat: And whoever has wealth and is stingy with it towards his people, he will be independent of them and will be blamed. And when you stretch your hand beyond your capacity, you will sit without anything to spend, and you will be like the hasir, which is the animal that is unable to walk and stops due to weakness and inability, so it is called hasir, and it is taken from fatigue, as He said: Then return your sight - do you see any flaw? Then return your sight a second time - your sight will return to you humbled and exhausted. That is, exhausted from seeing a fault. This is how this verse was interpreted, that what is meant here is miserliness and extravagance: Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Zayd, and others. It was reported in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu al-Zinad on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The example of the miser and the spender is like that of two men wearing iron cloaks from their chests to their collarbones. As for the spender, he does not spend except that it becomes thick or abundant on his skin, covering his fingers and obliterating his traces. As for the miser, he does not want to spend anything except that each link of it sticks to its place, so he expands it but it does not expand.” This is the wording of al-Bukhari in Zakat. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his wife Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, on the authority of her grandmother Asma bint Abi Bakr, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Spend like this and like this and like this, and do not hoard, lest God hoard for you, and do not count, lest God count for you. And in another version: And do not count, lest God count for you. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God said to me: Spend, and I will spend on you.” And in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Abi Mazard, on the authority of Saeed bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no day on which the servants arise except that two angels descend from the heaven, one of them says: O God, give to the one who spends in charity a replacement, and the other says: O God, give to the one who withholds destruction.” Muslim narrated on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of Ismail bin Jaafar on the authority of Al-Ala’ on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him: No wealth is diminished by charity, and God does not increase a servant who spends except in honor, and whoever humbles himself before God, God will raise him. And in the hadith of Abu Katheer on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him: “Beware of miserliness, for it destroyed those who came before you. It commanded them to be miserly, so they were miserly. It commanded them to sever ties of kinship, so they sever ties of kinship. It commanded them to commit immorality, so they committed immorality.” Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Sa’dan bin Nasr on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of his father who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: No man gives charity until he has freed seventy devils from his beard. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Ubaidah Al-Haddad told us, Sakin bin Abdul Aziz told us, Ibrahim Al-Hijri told us on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who is moderate will not be poor. His statement: Indeed, your Lord expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it is informing us that He, the Most High, is the Provider, the Withholder, the Expander, who disposes of His creation as He wills, so He enriches whom He wills and impoverishes whom He wills, because of the wisdom He has in that. For this reason, He said: Indeed, He is All-Knowing and All-Seeing of His servants, meaning He is All-Knowing and All-Seeing of who deserves wealth and who deserves poverty, as came in the hadith: “Some of My servants are not reformed except by poverty, and if I made them rich, I would corrupt their religion. Some of My servants are not reformed except by wealth, and if I made them poor, I would corrupt their religion.” Wealth may be a means of enticement for some people, and poverty may be a punishment, God forbid.
