17:31: This noble verse indicates that God Almighty is more merciful to His servants than a father is to his son, because He forbade killing children as He recommended fathers to inherit children. The people of ignorance did not give inheritance to daughters, but one of them might kill his daughter so that his illness would not increase, so God Almighty forbade that and said, And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, meaning fear that you will become poor in a second situation. For this reason, He presented the concern for their sustenance, saying, We provide for them and for you. And in Al-An’am, And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, meaning poverty, We provide for you and for them. And his saying, Indeed, killing them was a great mistake, meaning a great sin. Some of them read: It was a great mistake, and it has the same meaning. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, I said: O Messenger of God, which sin is the greatest? He said: That you make a rival to God, even though He created you. I said: Then what? He said: That you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you. I said: Then what? He said: That you commit adultery with your neighbor’s wife.
17:33: God Almighty says, forbidding the killing of a soul without a legitimate right, as it was proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The blood of a Muslim man who bears witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God is not permissible to be shed except in one of three cases: a life for a life, a married adulterer, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community.” And in the Sunan: The loss of the world is easier in the sight of God than the killing of a Muslim. And his saying: And whoever is killed unjustly, We have given his heir authority meaning authority over the killer, so he has the choice in it. If he wants to kill him in retaliation, or if he wants to pardon him for blood money, or if he wants to pardon him for free, as the Sunnah has established, then he has the choice. The scholar Ibn Abbas, from the generality of this noble verse, Muawiyah’s authority over the sultanate is that he will rule because he was the heir of Uthman, and he was killed unjustly, may God be pleased with him. Muawiyah was demanding that Ali, may God be pleased with him, hand over his killers so that he could exact retribution from them, because he was an Umayyad. Ali, may God be pleased with him, was asking him to delay the matter until he was able to do so, and Ali was asking Muawiyah to hand over the Levant to him, but Muawiyah refused that, until he handed over the killers to him, and he refused to pledge allegiance to Ali, he and the people of the Levant. Then, with the delay, Muawiyah was able to do so and the matter became his, as Ibn Abbas said and deduced from this noble verse. This is an amazing matter. Al-Tabarani narrated this in his Mu'jam, where he said: Yahya bin Abdul-Baqi told us, Abu Umair bin Al-Nahhas told us, Damrah bin Rabi'ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdab, on the authority of Matar Al-Warraq, on the authority of Zahdam Al-Jarmi, who said: We were in the company of Ibn Abbas, and he said: I am going to tell you a story that is neither secret nor public. When this man's affair meaning Uthman happened, I said to Ali: Stay away, even if you were in a hole, I would search until you were extracted, but he disobeyed me. By God, Mu'awiyah will rule over you, because God says: And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, but let him not exceed limits in [the matter of] taking life (al-Ma'mun 3:17). And the Quraysh will force you to follow the ways of the Persians and the Romans, and the Christians, Jews, and Magians will rule over you. Whoever among you takes what he knows on that day will be saved, and whoever leaves it - and you are leaving it - you will be like a generation of generations that perished among those who perished. And his saying: Let him not exceed limits in [the matter of] taking life, they said: Its meaning is that the heir should not exceed limits in killing the killer by mutilating him or taking revenge. Other than the killer. And his saying: He was victorious means that the guardian is victorious over the killer according to the law and usually according to fate.
17:34: God the Almighty says: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, until he reaches maturity. That is, do not dispose of the orphan's money except for the sake of envy. "And do not consume it extravagantly or hastily, lest they grow up. And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in moderation." It was reported in Sahih Muslim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Dharr: "O Abu Dharr, I see that you are weak, and I love for you what I love for myself: Do not be in charge of two people, and do not take charge of the wealth of an orphan." And His statement, And fulfill the covenant, that is, what you make with people and the contracts that you deal with them, for each covenant and contract will be questioned about its partner. Indeed, the covenant will be questioned about, that is, about it. And His statement: And give full measure when you measure means without defrauding people and do not deprive them of their things. And weigh with an even balance is read with a damma or kasra on the qaf, like qirtas, which is the scale. Mujahid said: It is justice in Roman. And His statement: The straight means that which is free of crookedness, deviation or disorder. That is better means for you in your life and your afterlife. That is why He said and better in outcome meaning better in reward and better in consequence in your afterlife. Saeed said on the authority of Qatadah That is better and better in outcome meaning better in reward and better in consequence. And Ibn Abbas used to say: O group of clients, you have been entrusted with two matters by which people before you were destroyed: this measure and this balance. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say: “No man is able to do something forbidden and then abandons it for no other reason than fear of God, except that God will replace it for him in this worldly life before the hereafter with something better for him than that.”
17:35: God the Almighty says: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, until he reaches maturity. That is, do not dispose of the orphan's money except for the sake of envy. "And do not consume it extravagantly or hastily, lest they grow up. And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in moderation." 17:36: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Do not say. Al-Awfi said: Do not accuse anyone of what you have no knowledge of. Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah said: It means false testimony. Qatada said: Do not say I saw when you did not see, I heard when you did not hear, I knew when you did not know, because God will ask you about all of that. The implication of what they mentioned is that God forbade speaking without knowledge, but rather with conjecture, which is imagination and fantasy, as He said: Avoid much suspicion, for some suspicion is sin. And in the hadith: Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the falsest of speech. And in Sunan Abi Dawud: They claimed that a man's mount is evil. And in another hadith: The most fabricating of lies is for a man to show with his own eyes what he did not see. And in the Sahih: Whoever dreams a dream will be asked on the Day of Resurrection to tie two barley grains together, and he will not do it. And his saying: All of those meaning these attributes of hearing, sight, and the heart he will be questioned about meaning the servant will be asked about them on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be asked about what he did in them. It is correct to use those instead of those, as the poet said: Blame the houses after the house of Al-Lawa and life after those days God Almighty says: The love of this world, its pleasures and its luxuries distracted you from seeking and seeking the Hereafter, and this continued with you until death came to you and you visited the graves and became among its people. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Zakariya bin Yahya al-Waqqad al-Misri told us, Khalid bin Abdul Daim told me, on the authority of Ibn Zayd bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: You are distracted by multiplying [your] desires - from obedience - to the point that you visit the graves - until death comes to you. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: You are distracted by multiplying [your] desires in wealth and children. In Sahih al-Bukhari, in the chapter on asceticism, he said: Abu al-Walid told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b, who said: We used to see this from the Qur’an until the verse: You are distracted by multiplying [your] desires was revealed, meaning, if the son of Adam had a valley full of gold. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, I heard Qatadah narrating, on the authority of Mutraf, meaning Ibn Abdullah bin Ash-Shakheer, on the authority of his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said: You are distracted by multiplying [your] desires. The son of Adam says: “My money, my money. Do you have any of your wealth except what you ate and finished, or wore out, or gave in charity and spent?” It was narrated by Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Shu’bah. Muslim said in his Sahih: Suwaid bin Sa’id told us, Hafs bin Maysarah told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The servant says, ‘My wealth, my wealth.’ But he only gets three things from his wealth: what he ate and finished, what he wore out and gave in charity and acquired. Everything else is lost and he leaves it to the people.” It was narrated only by Muslim. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Humaidi told us, Sufyan told us, Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm told us, he heard Anas bin Malik say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Three things follow a dead person, two of which return and one remains with him: his family, his wealth and his deeds. His family and wealth return and his deeds remain.” Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i also narrated this on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The son of Adam grows old and two things remain in him: greed and hope.” Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Al-Ahnaf bin Qais, whose name was Ad-Dahhak, that he saw a dirham in a man’s hand and said: Whose dirham is this? The man said: Mine. The Prophet said: It is only for you if you spend it in reward or seeking thanks. Then Al-Ahnaf recited, reciting the words of the poet: Money belongs to you if you hold it, but if you spend it, the money belongs to you Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, Salih bin Hayyan narrated to me on the authority of Ibn Buraidah regarding His statement: {Has competition distracted you?} He said: It was revealed about two tribes of the Ansar, Banu Haritha. Banu Al-Harith boasted and multiplied, so one of them said: Among you are the likes of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and so-and-so, and the others said the same. They boasted about the living, then they said: Let’s go to the graves. So one of the two groups began to say: Among you are the likes of so-and-so, pointing to the graves, and the likes of so-and-so, and the others did the same. So God revealed: {Has competition distracted you * Until you visit the graves.} Indeed, in what you have seen there is a lesson and a preoccupation for you. Qatada said: {Has competition distracted you * Until you visit the graves.} They used to say: We are more numerous than Banu so-and-so, and we are more numerous than Banu so-and-so, and they were falling every day until the last of them. By God, they continued like that until they all became people of the graves. The correct meaning of His statement: You visited the graves is that you went to them and were buried in them, as it came. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, it is reported that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon a Bedouin to visit him and said: There is nothing wrong with it, it is a purification, God willing. He said: I said it is a purification, rather it is a fever that boils over an old man, and makes him visit the graves. He said: Then yes. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Muhammad ibn Sa’id al-Asbahani told us, Hakam ibn Salim al-Razi told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qais, on the authority of al-Hajjaj, on the authority of al-Munhal, on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish, on the authority of Ali, who said: We did not cease to doubt the torment of the grave until the verse, Does multiplying [your] efforts distract you * Until you visit the graves? was revealed. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Hakam ibn Salim, and he said: It is strange. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Salamah ibn Dawud al-Ardi told us, Abu al-Malih al-Raqi told us, on the authority of Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: I was sitting with Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz when he recited, Does multiplying [your] efforts distract you * Until you visit the graves? He waited a while, then said: O Maymun, I do not see the graves as anything but a visit, and the visitor has no choice but to return to his home. Abu Muhammad said: It means that he will return to his home, that is, to Paradise or to Hell. Thus, it was mentioned that some of the Bedouins heard a man reciting this verse: Until you visit the graves, so he said: He has been sent today, by the Lord of the Kaaba, meaning that the visitor will move from his place to another. And the saying of God the Almighty: “No indeed, you will surely know. Then no indeed, you will surely know.” Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: This is a warning. Ad-Dahhak said: No indeed, you will surely know means O disbelievers. Then no indeed, you will surely know means O believers. And the saying of God the Almighty: No indeed, if you only knew with certainty means if you knew truly, then multiplying would not have distracted you from seeking the Hereafter until you reached the graves. Then He said: “You will surely see Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.” This is the explanation of the warning that came before, which is His saying: “No indeed, you will surely know. Then no indeed, you will surely know.” He threatens them with this state, which is seeing the people of Hellfire, when it sighs once, every close angel and sent prophet falls on his knees out of awe and majesty and witnessing the horrors, according to what is stated in the transmitted narration about that. And the saying of God the Almighty: Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure means then you will be asked that Day about being grateful for what God has bestowed upon you of health, security, provision, and other things, and how you respond to His blessings by thanking Him and worshipping Him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Zakariya ibn Yahya al-Jazzar al-Muqri told us, Abdullah ibn Isa Abu Khalid al-Jazzar told us, Yunus ibn Ubayd told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out at noon and found Abu Bakr in the mosque. He said: ‘What brought you out at this hour?’ He said: ‘The same one who brought you out, O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.’ Umar ibn al-Khattab came and said: ‘What brought you out, O Ibn al-Khattab?’ He said: ‘The same one who brought you out brought me out.’ Umar sat down and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to talk to them. Then he said: ‘Do you have the strength to go to these palm trees and find food, drink and shade?’ We said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Let us pass by the house of Ibn al-Tayhan Abu al-Haytham al-Ansari.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stepped forward in front of us and greeted us and asked permission three times, and Umm al-Haytham was behind the door, listening to the speech, wanting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to greet her again. When he wanted to leave, Umm al-Haytham came out.” She ran after them and said: O Messenger of God, by God, I heard your greetings, but you wanted to say more of them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Good, then he said: Where is Abu Al-Haytham? I do not see him. She said: O Messenger of God, he is close by, looking for sweet water. Enter, for he will come soon, God willing. So she spread a rug under a tree, and Abu Al-Haytham came and was happy with them, and his eyes were comforted by them. He climbed a palm tree and cut bunches of dates for them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: That is enough, Abu Al-Haytham. He said: O Messenger of God, you will eat of its unripe dates, its ripe dates, and its blackberries. Then he brought them water and they drank from it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is from the blessings that you are asking about. This is strange from this aspect. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me, Al-Walid bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Kaysan, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “While Abu Bakr and Umar were sitting, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them and said: ‘What has made you sit here?’ They said: ‘By Him who sent you with the truth, nothing drove us out of our homes except hunger.’ He said: ‘By Him who sent me with the truth, nothing drove me out except it.’ So they set off until they came to the house of a man from the Ansar. A woman met them and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: ‘Where is so-and-so?’ She said: ‘He went to get us fresh water.’ Their companion came carrying his waterskin and said: ‘Welcome. Nothing has visited the servants better than a Prophet who visited me today.’ So he hung his waterskin on the waterskin of a palm tree and set off and brought them a bunch of dates. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Why didn’t you gather some?’ He said: ‘I would have liked you to be the ones who choose right before your eyes.’ Then he took the knife and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘Beware of milking.’ So he slaughtered a sacrifice for them that day and they ate. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘You will be asked about this.’” On the Day of Resurrection, hunger will drive you out of your homes, and you will not return until you have obtained this. This is from the blessings.” Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Yazid ibn Kaysan with this chain of transmission. Narrated by Abu Ya’la and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Al-Maharibi from Yahya ibn Ubayd God from his father from Abu Hurayrah from Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq with this chain of transmission. The four scholars of Sunan narrated it from the hadith of Abd Al-Malik ibn Umair from Abu Salamah from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, with a similar context and story. Imam Ahmad said: Surayj told us, Hashraj told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Usayb, meaning the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out at night and passed by me and called me, so I went out to him. Then he passed by Abu Bakr and called him, so he went out to him. Then he passed by Umar and called him, so he went out to him. He went until he entered a garden belonging to some of the Ansar and said to the owner of the garden: Feed us some unripe dates. So he brought a bunch of dates and put them down, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions ate. Then he called for cold water and drank it, and said: You will be asked about this on the Day of Resurrection. Umar took the bunch of dates and threw them on the ground until the unripe dates scattered before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he said: O Messenger of God, will we be asked about this on the Day of Resurrection? He said: Yes, except for three things: a rag with which a man wraps his private parts, or a piece of bread with which he satisfies his hunger, or a hole into which he enters to escape the heat and cold.” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, Hammad told us, Ammar told us, I heard… Jabir ibn Abdullah said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Abu Bakr and Umar ate some dates and drank water, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is from the blessings that you are asking about.” An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, from Jabir, and Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad told us, Yazid told us, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Mahmud ibn Ar-Rabi’, who said: When the verse, Has multiplying [your worldly pursuits] distracted you? was revealed, and he recited until he reached, You will surely be asked that Day about pleasures, they said: “O Messenger of God, what pleasures will we ask about? They are the two black ones: water and dates, and our swords are on our necks and the enemy is present, so what pleasure will we ask about?” He said: That will certainly happen. Ahmad said: Abu Amir Abdul Malik bin Amr told us, Abdullah bin Sulaiman told us, Muadh bin Abdullah bin Habib told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his uncle, who said: “We were in a gathering when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us with traces of water on his head. We said: ‘O Messenger of God, we see you in good spirits.’ He said: ‘Yes.’ Then the people began to mention wealth, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There is nothing wrong with wealth for the one who fears God, but health for the one who fears God is better than wealth, and good spirits are a source of comfort.’” Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Khalid bin Mukhallad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Sulaiman. Al-Tirmidhi said: ‘Abd bin Hamid told us, Shababah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Ala’, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Abdul Rahman bin Azrab Al-Ash’ari, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, say: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The first thing that a servant will be asked about - meaning on the Day of Resurrection - regarding comfort is that it will be said to him: Did We not make your body healthy for you and provide you with cold water to drink?’” It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi alone, and Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Al-Walid bin Muslim on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Ala bin Zubayr. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah told us, Musaddad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Yahya ibn Hatib, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr, who said: Az-Zubayr said: “When the verse, ‘Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure,’ was revealed, they said, ‘O Messenger of God, for what pleasure will we be asked about? They are only the two black ones: dates and water.’ He said, ‘That will happen.’” At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah, with it. Ahmad narrated it on his authority, and At-Tirmidhi said, ‘It is hasan.’ Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Az-Zahrani told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Umar Al-Adani, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: When this verse, ‘Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure,’ was revealed, the Companions said, ‘O Messenger of God, what pleasure are we in when we only eat barley bread halfway through our stomachs?’ So God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ‘Say to them, do you not wear sandals and drink cold water? This is from pleasure.’ Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Muhammad bin Sulayman bin Al-Asbahani told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla, I think it was on the authority of Amir, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding his statement: Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure, he said: Security and health. Zayd bin Aslam said: “On the authority of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him: ‘Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure,’ meaning full bellies, cool drinks, shade in dwellings, moderate character, and the pleasure of sleep.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with the chain of transmission mentioned above from him at the beginning of the surah. Sa’id bin Jubayr said: Even about a drink of honey. Mujahid said: About every pleasure of this world. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Among the pleasures is lunch and dinner. Abu Qilabah said: Among the pleasures is eating butter and honey with pure bread. The statement of Mujahid is the most comprehensive of these statements. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then you will be asked on that Day about pleasure. He said: Pleasure is the health of the body, hearing, and sight. God will ask His servants about what they used them for, and He knows that better than they do. This is His Almighty saying, Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart - about all those one will be questioned. It is proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari, Sunan At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Abdullah bin Saeed bin Abi Hind from his father from Ibn Abbas who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘There are two blessings which many people are deceived about: health and free time.’” What this means is that they are negligent in being grateful for these two blessings and do not fulfil their duties. Whoever does not fulfil his duties is deceived. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Al-Qasim bin Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Marwazi told us, Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Shaqiq told us, Abu Hamza told us, from Laith, from Abu Fazarah, from Yazid bin Al-Asamm, from Ibn Abbas who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘A servant will be brought to account for or questioned about on the Day of Resurrection whatever is above the lower garment, the shade of a wall and bread.’” Then he said: We do not know it except through this chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz and Affan told us: Hammad told us, Affan said in his hadith, Ishaq bin Abdullah said, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God the Almighty will say - and Affan said on the Day of Resurrection - O son of Adam, I carried you on horses and camels, and married you to women, and made you rule and lead, so where is the gratitude for that?” It was narrated by him alone from this chain of transmission. At the end of the interpretation of Surat At-Takathur, and praise and thanks be to God.
17:37: God Almighty says, forbidding His servants from being arrogant and swaggering in their gait: And do not walk on the earth exultantly, meaning swaggering and swaying like the tyrants. Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, meaning you will never be cut apart by your walking. Ibn Jarir said this, and he cited as evidence for this the words of Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj: Dark and empty of penetration And his saying: And you will not reach the mountains in height means with your swaying, pride and self-admiration. Rather, the one who does that may be punished with the opposite of what he intended, as it was proven in the Sahih: “While a man was walking among those who came before you, and he was wearing two cloaks, strutting in them, the earth swallowed him up and he will continue to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection.” And likewise, God the Most High informed us about Qarun that he came out to his people in his finery, and that God the Most High swallowed him up and his house. And in the hadith: “Whoever humbles himself for the sake of God, God will raise him up, for he is insignificant in his own eyes and great in the eyes of the people. And whoever is arrogant, God will humiliate him, for he is great in his own eyes and insignificant in the eyes of the people, until he is more hated by them than a dog or a pig.” Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Dunya said in the Book of Indolence and Humility: Ahmad bin Ibrahim bin Katheer told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali, he said: While we were with Al-Hasan, Ibn Al-Ahim passed by him intending to go to Al-Mansur, and he was wearing silk cloaks, some of which were arranged on top of each other, on his legs, and his cloak was parted, and he was walking and strutting, when Al-Hasan looked at him with a glance. He said: Uff, ff, his nose raised, his cheek turned up, looking into his sides. What fool looks into his sides at blessings that are not appreciated or mentioned, not taking God’s command into them, nor fulfilling God’s right in them. By God, if one of them walks by nature, he stutters like a madman in every part of him. It is a blessing, and Satan has a curse on him. Ibn al-Ahim heard him and returned to apologize to him. He said: Do not apologize to me, and repent to your Lord. Have you not heard the words of God Almighty: “And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, and you will never reach the mountains in height.” Al-Bukhtari the pious saw a man from the family of Ali walking in a swaying gait, so he said to him: O man, the One Who honored you with him did not walk like this. He said: So he left it. Ibn Omar saw a man walking in a swaying gait, so he said: The devils have brothers. Khalid bin Ma’dan said: Beware of swaying, for a man’s hand is part of the rest of his body. Both were narrated by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya said: Khalaf bin Hisham Al-Bazzar told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Bahnas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When my nation walks in a swaying gait, and the Persians and Romans serve them, some of them will have power over others. And his saying: All of that is evil and hateful to your Lord. As for the one who reads evil, meaning an indecency, then its meaning to him is all of that which we have forbidden from His saying: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, up to here, then it is an evil for which he will be held accountable and hateful to God, which He does not love or approve of. As for the one who reads evil as an addition, then its meaning to him is all of that which we have mentioned from His saying: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, up to here, then it is evil, meaning its ugliness is hateful to God. This is how Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, interpreted it.

17:39: God Almighty says: This is what we have commanded you to do of good morals, and what we have forbidden you from of bad qualities, from what we have revealed to you, O Muhammad, so that you may command the people with it, And do not make with God another god, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed, meaning your soul will blame you and God and creation will blame you, rejected, meaning banished from all good. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: banished, and what is meant by this address is the nation through the Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, for he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, is infallible.
17:40: The Almighty says, responding to the lying polytheists who claim, upon them be the curses of God: that the angels are the daughters of God, so they made the angels who are the servants of the Most Gracious females, then they claimed that they were the daughters of God, then they worshipped them and made a great mistake in each of the three positions, so the Almighty said, denouncing them, Has your Lord preferred you to sons? meaning, has He singled you out with males, and taken for Himself females from among the angels? meaning, has He chosen for Himself, according to your claim, daughters? Then He intensified the denunciation of them, saying, Indeed, you are saying a terrible thing. meaning, in your claim that God has a son, then He made you His daughters, whom you are reluctant to have and perhaps you killed them by burying them alive, so that is indeed an unfair division. The Almighty said, “And they say, ‘The Most Gracious has taken a son. ’ You have certainly done a terrible thing. ’ The heavens almost burst from it and the earth splits open and the mountains collapse in devastation. ’ That they attribute to the Most Gracious a son. ’ And it is not befitting for the Most Gracious to take a son.” There is none in the heavens and the earth but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them exactly. And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.”
17:41: God Almighty says: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur’an from every [kind of] example. That is, We have presented in it threats so that they may remember what is in it of arguments, clear proofs, and admonitions, and so that they may be deterred from what they are doing of polytheism, injustice, and slander. But it only increases them, that is, the wrongdoers among them, in aversion, that is, from the truth and distance from it.
17:42: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who claim that God has a partner from among His creation, worshipping others besides Him, to bring them closer to Him, if the matter were as they say, and that there were gods with Him who are worshipped to bring them closer to Him and intercede with Him, then those worshipped ones would worship Him and seek closeness to Him and seek a means of approach and closeness to Him, so worship Him alone as those whom you call upon besides Him worship Him, and you have no need for a god who would be an intermediary between you and Him, for He does not love that and is not pleased with it, rather He hates it and rejects it, and He has forbidden that on the tongues of all His messengers and prophets, then He purified and sanctified His noble self and said: Glory be to Him and He is exalted above what they say, meaning these transgressing, unjust polytheists in their claim that there are other gods with Him, with great exaltation, meaning great exaltation, rather He is God, the One, the Eternal Refuge, who did not give birth and was not born, and there is none comparable to Him.
17:43: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who claim that God has a partner from among His creation, worshipping others besides Him, to bring them closer to Him, if the matter were as they say, and that there were gods with Him who are worshipped to bring them closer to Him and intercede with Him, then those worshipped ones would worship Him and seek closeness to Him and seek a means of approach and closeness to Him, so worship Him alone as those whom you call upon besides Him worship Him, and you have no need for a god who would be an intermediary between you and Him, for He does not love that and is not pleased with it, rather He hates it and rejects it, and He has forbidden that on the tongues of all His messengers and prophets, then He purified and sanctified His noble self and said: Glory be to Him and He is exalted above what they say, meaning these transgressing, unjust polytheists in their claim that there are other gods with Him, with great exaltation, meaning great exaltation, rather He is God, the One, the Eternal Refuge, who did not give birth and was not born, and there is none comparable to Him.
17:44: God Almighty says: The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them, that is, the creatures, sanctify Him, glorify Him, venerate Him, and magnify Him above what these polytheists say, and bear witness to His Oneness in His Lordship and Divinity: In everything there is a sign that indicates that He is One. God the Almighty said: The heavens almost burst from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, because they attribute to the Most Gracious a son. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz told us, Saeed ibn Mansur told us, Maskeen ibn Maimun, the muezzin of the Ramla Mosque told us, Urwah ibn Ruwaym told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Qart, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of his Isra’ was taken to the Al-Aqsa Mosque, he was between the Maqam and Zamzam, Gabriel was on his right and Michael was on his left, and they flew until they reached the seven heavens. When he returned, he said: “I heard glorification in the highest heavens, along with much glorification. The highest heavens glorify the One of Majesty, fearing the One of the Most High for what is high. Glory be to the Most High, the Most High, glory be to Him and He is Most High.” And His statement: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise meaning, there is not a thing among the creatures but glorifies God with praise. But you do not understand their glorification meaning, you do not understand their glorification, O people, because it is different from your languages. This is general for animals, inanimate objects, and plants, and this is the more famous of the two opinions, as it was proven in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that he said: We used to hear the glorification of food while it was being eaten. In the hadith of Abu Dharr, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took pebbles in his hand and heard them glorifying God like the humming of bees. The same was true in the hands of Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, may God be pleased with them. It is a well-known hadith in the Musnads. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Zaban told us, on the authority of Sahl ibn Mu’adh, on the authority of Ibn Anas, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he entered upon some people while they were standing on their mounts and camels, and he said to them: Ride them safely and leave them safe, and do not use them as chairs for your conversations in the streets and markets, for many a mount is better than its rider, and remembers God more than he does.” In Sunan An-Nasa'i, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade killing frogs, and said that their croaking is glorification." Qatada said on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubayy on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr that when a man says, There is no god but God, it is the word of sincerity, and God will not accept any action from anyone until he says it. And when he says, Praise be to God, it is the word of gratitude, and no servant has ever thanked God until he says it. And when he says, God is Great, it fills the space between heaven and earth. And when he says, Glory be to God, it is the prayer of all creation, and God has not left any of His creation without making him pray and glorify Him. And when he says, There is no power or strength except with God, He says, My servant has submitted and surrendered. Imam Ahmad said: Wahb bin Jarir told us, my father told us, I heard Al-Saqab bin Zuhair narrating on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam on the authority of Ata bin Yasar on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr who said: “A Bedouin came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wearing a cloak of cloaks edged with brocade, or decorated with brocade, and he said: Your master wants to raise every shepherd who is the son of a shepherd and lower every head who is the son of a head. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up angrily and grabbed the edges of his cloak and pulled him and said: I do not see you wearing the clothes of someone who does not have reason. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and sat down and said: When death approached Noah, peace be upon him, he called his two sons and said: I am telling you my will. I command you to do two things and forbid you from two things. I forbid you from associating partners with God and from arrogance. I command you to say, ‘There is no god but God.’ If the heavens and the earth and everything in them were to say, ‘There is no god but God,’ it would break them or they would break them. I command you to say, ‘Glory be to God and praise be to Him,’ for it is the prayer of everything.” And through it He provides for everything.” Imam Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Sulayman ibn Harb on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd on the authority of Mus`ab ibn Zuhayr, with a longer chain of transmission than this, and he is the only one to narrate it. Ibn Jarir said: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me, Muhammad bin Ya’la told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not tell you of something that Noah commanded his son to do? Noah, peace be upon him, said to his son: O my son, I command you to say: Subhan God, for it is the prayer of creation and the glorification of creation, and with it creation is provided for.” God Almighty said: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise. Its chain of transmission is weak, for Al-Awdi is weak according to the majority. And Ikrimah said about the Almighty’s saying: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, he said: The column glorifies and the tree glorifies - the column - the mast. And some of the predecessors said: The creaking of the door is His glorification and the gurgling of the water is His glorification. God Almighty said: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, and Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Food glorifies, and the verse of prostration in Hajj bears witness to this statement. And others said: Only that which has a soul glorifies, meaning animals and plants. Qatada said about His statement, And there is nothing but glorifies Him with praise, he said: Everything that has a soul glorifies Him, from a tree or something in it. Al-Hasan and Ad-Dahhak said about His statement, And there is nothing but glorifies Him with praise, they said: Everything that has a soul. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Hamid told us, Yahya ibn Wadheeh and Zaid ibn Habbab told us, they said: Jarir Abu Al-Khattab told us, he said: We were with Yazid Al-Raqashi and Al-Hasan were eating, and they brought out a tray, so Yazid Al-Raqashi said: O Abu Saad, does this tray glorify Him? He said: He was once glorifying God - I said: The table is made of wood - so it seems that Al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, went to the fact that when he was alive and had greenery in him, he was glorifying God, but when he was cut and became dry wood, his glorification stopped. This statement may be supported by the hadith of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by two graves and said: “They are being punished, but they are not being punished for anything major. As for one of them, he did not protect himself from urine, and as for the other, he used to spread gossip.” Then he took a fresh palm branch and split it in half, then he stuck one in each grave, then he said: Perhaps it will be lightened for them as long as they do not dry up. They included it in the two Sahihs. Some of the scholars who spoke about this hadith said: He only said as long as they do not dry up because they glorify God as long as there is greenery in them, but when they dry up, their glorification stops, and God knows best. And His saying, Indeed, He was Forbearing and Forgiving, meaning that He does not hasten to punish those who disobey Him, but rather He gives them respite and gives them time. If they persist in their disbelief and stubbornness, He will seize them with the grasp of the Mighty, the Powerful, as it came in the two Sahihs, Indeed, God gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, And thus does your Lord seize when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoers. And God the Almighty said, And how many a town have I granted respite while they were wrongdoers? And He said, How many a town have We destroyed while they were wrongdoers? And the two verses. And whoever abandons what he is in of disbelief or disobedience, and returns to God, He will repent to Him and He will accept his repentance, as God the Almighty said, And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God and He said here, Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving, as He said at the end of Fatir, “Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist. And if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving.” Until he said. And if God were to punish people to the end of the Surah.
17:45: God the Almighty says to His Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him): And when you recite the Qur'an, O Muhammad, to these polytheists, We will place between you and them a hidden veil. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: It is the coverings over their hearts, as God the Almighty said: And they say, ‘Our hearts are within coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a veil.’ That is, a barrier preventing anything of what you say from reaching us. His statement a hidden veil means a cover, like auspicious and ominous, meaning auspicious and ominous, because it is from their auspiciousness and ominousness. It was said: hidden from the eyes so that you do not see it, and yet it is a veil between them and guidance. Ibn Jarir may God have mercy on him tended to prefer this. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili said: Abu Musa al-Harawi Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Kathir, on the authority of Yazid ibn Tadrus, on the authority of Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, may God be pleased with her, who said: “When the verse ‘Perish the hands of Abu Lahab’ was revealed, the one-eyed Umm Jamil came, wailing and holding a stick in her hand, saying: ‘We have come as a blameworthy person – or we have refused.’ Abu Musa said: ‘The doubt is on my part, and his religion is weak, and his command is disobeyed.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting with Abu Bakr beside him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: ‘She has come and I am afraid that she will see you.’ He said: ‘She will not see me.’ He recited a Qur’an that he sought protection from her: ‘And when you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible veil.’ So she came and stood over Abu Bakr, but she did not see the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: ‘O Abu Bakr, I have heard that your companion has satirized me.’ Abu Bakr said: ‘No, by the Lord of this House, he has not satirized you.’ She left, saying: Quraish knew that I was the daughter of their master. And His statement: “And We have placed over their hearts coverings” which is the plural of kinan which covers the heart lest they understand it meaning so that they do not understand the Qur’an and in their ears deafness which is the heaviness that prevents them from hearing the Qur’an in a way that benefits them and guides them. And His statement, the Most High: And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur’an meaning when you make God One in your recitation and say there is no god but God, they turn back meaning they turn their backs in aversion and nafar is the plural of nafar and qa’ud is the plural of qa’id. It is permissible for it to be a verbal noun other than the verb, and God knows best. As God Almighty said: And when God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter are filled with disgust 17:1. Qatada said about His statement: And when your Lord is mentioned in the Qur’an 17:1, that when the Muslims said, There is no god but God, the polytheists denied it. It became too great for them and Satan and his soldiers found it difficult. But God refused except to carry it out, raise it up, support it, and make it prevail over those who opposed it. It is a word that whoever disputes with it will succeed, and whoever fights with it will be victorious. It is only known to the people of this expedition from the Muslims, which a rider can cover in a few nights, and time passes among groups of people who do not know it or acknowledge it. Another saying about the verse Ibn Jarir narrated: Al-Husayn bin Muhammad Al-Dhar’i’ told me, Ruh bin Al-Musayyab Abu Raja Al-Kalbi told us, and Amr bin Malik told us on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur’an, they turn their backs in aversion, they are the devils, and this is very strange in its interpretation, otherwise the devils, when the Qur’an is recited or the call to prayer is made or God is mentioned, they turn away.

17:47: God Almighty informs His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what the leaders of Quraysh were whispering when they came to listen to his recitation, may God bless him and grant him peace, secretly from their people, about what they said, that he was a man bewitched by magic, as is well-known, or by magic, which is the lung, meaning that if you follow Muhammad, you will follow nothing but a human being who eats, as the poet said: If you ask us what we are, then we are birds from this enchanted people The rajaz poet said: We are enchanted by food and drink That is, he nourishes. Ibn Jarir approved this statement, but it is questionable because they meant here that he was bewitched and had a vision that came to him with what they heard of the speech that he recited. Some of them said: a poet. Some of them said: a soothsayer. Some of them said: He is crazy and some of them said: He is a magician. That is why God Almighty said: See how they have put forth for you examples, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way. That is, they are not guided to the truth and cannot find a way out of it. Muhammad bin Ishaq said in the biography: Muhammad bin Muslim bin Shihab al-Zuhri told me that he was told that Abu Sufyan bin Harb, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, and al-Akhns bin Shuraiq bin Amr bin Wahb al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhrah, went out one night to listen to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was praying at night in his house. Each one of them took a seat to listen in, and each one did not know where the other was. They spent the night listening to him until dawn came and they dispersed. When the road brought them together, they blamed each other, and some of them said to each other: Do not return, for if one of your fools saw you, you would cause something to affect his mind. Then they left until the second night, each man returned to his seat and they spent the night listening to him until dawn came and they dispersed and the road brought them together. Some of them said to each other the same as the first one had said. Once, then they departed until the third night, each man took his seat and spent the night listening to him, until dawn came and they dispersed and the road brought them together, and some of them said to each other, We will not leave until we promise not to return, so they promised to do that and then dispersed. When morning came, Al-Akhnas bin Shuraik took his stick and went out until he came to Abu Sufyan bin Harb in his house and said: Tell me, O Abu Hanzala, what do you think of what you heard from Muhammad? He said: O Abu Tha’laba, by God, I have heard things that I know and I know what is meant by them, and I have heard things whose meaning I do not know or what is meant by them. Al-Akhnas said: And I, by Him by whom I swore. He said: Then he went out from him until he came to Abu Jahl and entered his house and said: O Abu Al-Hakam, what do you think of what you heard from Muhammad? He said: What did you hear? He said: We and Banu Abd Manaf disputed over honor: They fed and we fed, they carried and we carried, they gave and we gave, until when we knelt on our knees and were like two racehorses, they said: Among us is a prophet to whom revelation comes from the heavens, so when will we attain this? By God, we will never believe in him or trust him. He said: Then Al-Akhns got up from him and left him.

17:49: God Almighty says, informing about the infidels who reject the occurrence of the Resurrection and who say a question of denial about it, When we are bones and dust, meaning dust, as Mujahid said. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: dust, Shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation? meaning on the Day of Resurrection after we have decayed and become nothingness and are not remembered, as He informed about them in another place, They say, ‘Shall we indeed be returned to the grave? When we are decayed bones?’ They say, ‘That then is a losing return.’ And the Almighty said: And he has set forth for us an example and has forgotten his own creation 2:100. So God Almighty commanded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer them, saying: Say, ‘Be you stones or iron’ since they are more impenetrable than bones and dust, or some creation of that which is great in your breasts. Ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: I asked Ibn Abbas about that, and he said: It is death. Atiyah narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said in the interpretation of this verse: If you were dead, I would have brought you back to life. This is what Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Salih, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and others said. The meaning of that is that if you were to assume that you were to reach death, which is the opposite of life, God would bring you back to life if He willed, for nothing is impenetrable to Him if He wills it. Ibn Jarir mentioned here a hadith: “Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection as if it were a white ram, and it will be stopped between Paradise and Hell. Then it will be said: O people of Paradise, do you recognize this? They will say: Yes. Then it will be said: O people of Hell, do you recognize this? They will say: Yes. Then it will be slaughtered between Paradise and Hell. Then it will be said: O people of Paradise, eternity without death, and O people of Hell, eternity without death.” Mujahid said: Or a creation of what is great in your hearts, meaning the sky, the earth, and the mountains. In another narration: Whatever you wish, be, for God will bring you back after your death. It was mentioned in the interpretation narrated from Imam Malik from al-Zuhri in his saying: Or a creation of what is great in your hearts, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Malik said: And they say it is death. And the Almighty’s saying: And they will say, ‘Who will restore us?’ meaning, who will restore us if we were stones or iron or some other strong creation? Say, ‘He who created you the first time.’ meaning, He who created you when you were nothing worth mentioning and then you became human beings spreading out, for He is able to restore you even if you become in any state. And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. The verse. And the Almighty’s saying: They shake their heads at you. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: They move them in mockery. And what they said is what the Arabs know from their languages, because inghaadh means moving from the bottom to the top or from the top to the bottom. And from this, the gazelle, which is the young ostrich, is called naghdh, because when it walks, it hurries in its gait and moves its head. And it is said: Naqafat Sanah means that it moved and rose from its place. And the rajaz poet said: And she lowered her teeth And His statement: "And they say, 'When will it be?'" is an indication of their exclusion of that happening, as the Almighty said: "And they say, 'When will this promise be, if you should be truthful?'" And the Almighty said: "Those who do not believe in it hasten it." And His statement: "Say, 'Perhaps it is near.'" That is, beware of that, for it is near and will inevitably come to you, for everything that is coming will come. And His statement, the Almighty: "The Day He will call you," that is, the Lord, the Blessed and Exalted: "When He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will emerge," that is, when He commands you to emerge from it, for He will not disobey or prevent, but as the Almighty said: "And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, 'Be,' and it is." And His statement: "It is but a single cry * And at once they are awake," that is, it is only a single command to rebuke, and at once the people have emerged from the interior of the earth to its exterior, as the Almighty said: "The Day He will call you, and you will respond with His praise," that is, you will all stand up in response to His command and obedience to His will. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So you respond with His praise, meaning with His command. Ibn Jurayj said the same. Qatada said with His knowledge and obedience. Some of them said, On the Day He calls you and you respond with His praise, meaning, to Him be praise in every situation. It was mentioned in the hadith, “There is no loneliness in the graves of the people of ‘There is no god but God.’ It is as if I see the people of ‘There is no god but God’ rising from their graves, shaking the dirt off their heads, saying, ‘There is no god but God.’” In another narration, they say, Praise be to God who has removed sorrow from us. This will come in Surah Fatir. And the Almighty said: And you think meaning on the Day you rise from your graves that you had tarried meaning in this worldly abode except a little, and like His Almighty’s saying: On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had not tarried except an afternoon or a morning thereof, and the Almighty said: “On the Day the Trumpet will be blown and We will gather the criminals that Day blue-eyed. They will whisper to one another, “You tarried only ten days.” We are most knowing of what they say when the best of them in way will say, You tarried only a day. And the Almighty said: “And on the Day the Hour will appear, the criminals will swear that they had not tarried except an hour. Thus were they deluded.” And the Almighty said: “He will say, ‘How many years did you remain on the earth?’ They will say, ‘We tarried a day or part of a day. So ask the counters.’ He will say, ‘You tarried only a little, if you only knew.’”

They will whisper to one another, “You tarried only ten days.” We are most knowing of what they say when the best of them in way will say, You tarried only a day. And the Almighty said: “And on the Day the Hour will appear, the criminals will swear that they had not tarried except an hour. Thus were they deluded.” And the Almighty said: “He will say, ‘How many years did you remain on the earth?’ They will say, ‘We tarried a day or part of a day. So ask the counters.’ He will say, ‘You tarried only a little, if you only knew.’”
17:51: God Almighty says, informing about the infidels who reject the occurrence of the Resurrection and who say a question of denial about it, When we are bones and dust, meaning dust, as Mujahid said. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: dust, Shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation? meaning on the Day of Resurrection after we have decayed and become nothingness and are not remembered, as He informed about them in another place, They say, ‘Shall we indeed be returned to the grave? When we are decayed bones?’ They say, ‘That then is a losing return.’ And the Almighty said: And he has set forth for us an example and has forgotten his own creation 2:100. So God Almighty commanded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer them, saying: Say, ‘Be you stones or iron’ since they are more impenetrable than bones and dust, or some creation of that which is great in your breasts. Ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: I asked Ibn Abbas about that, and he said: It is death. Atiyah narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said in the interpretation of this verse: If you were dead, I would have brought you back to life. This is what Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Salih, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and others said. The meaning of that is that if you were to assume that you were to reach death, which is the opposite of life, God would bring you back to life if He willed, for nothing is impenetrable to Him if He wills it. Ibn Jarir mentioned here a hadith: “Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection as if it were a white ram, and it will be stopped between Paradise and Hell. Then it will be said: O people of Paradise, do you recognize this? They will say: Yes. Then it will be said: O people of Hell, do you recognize this? They will say: Yes. Then it will be slaughtered between Paradise and Hell. Then it will be said: O people of Paradise, eternity without death, and O people of Hell, eternity without death.” Mujahid said: Or a creation of what is great in your hearts, meaning the sky, the earth, and the mountains. In another narration: Whatever you wish, be, for God will bring you back after your death. It was mentioned in the interpretation narrated from Imam Malik from al-Zuhri in his saying: Or a creation of what is great in your hearts, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Malik said: And they say it is death. And the Almighty’s saying: And they will say, ‘Who will restore us?’ meaning, who will restore us if we were stones or iron or some other strong creation? Say, ‘He who created you the first time.’ meaning, He who created you when you were nothing worth mentioning and then you became human beings spreading out, for He is able to restore you even if you become in any state. And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. The verse. And the Almighty’s saying: They shake their heads at you. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: They move them in mockery. And what they said is what the Arabs know from their languages, because inghaadh means moving from the bottom to the top or from the top to the bottom. And from this, the gazelle, which is the young ostrich, is called naghdh, because when it walks, it hurries in its gait and moves its head. And it is said: Naqafat Sanah means that it moved and rose from its place. And the rajaz poet said: And she lowered her teeth And His statement: And they say, 'When will it be?' is an indication of their exclusion of that happening, as the Almighty said: And they say, 'When will this promise be, if you should be truthful?' And the Almighty said: Those who do not believe in it hasten it. And His statement: Say, 'Perhaps it is near.' That is, beware of that, for it is near and will inevitably come to you, for everything that is coming will come. And His statement, the Almighty: The Day He will call you, that is, the Lord, the Blessed and Exalted: When He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will emerge, that is, when He commands you to emerge from it, for He will not disobey or prevent, but as the Almighty said: And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye, "Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, 'Be,' and it is." And His statement: "It is but a single cry * And at once they are awake," that is, it is only a single command to rebuke, and at once the people have emerged from the interior of the earth to its exterior, as the Almighty said: "The Day He will call you, and you will respond with His praise," that is, you will all stand up in response to His command and obedience to His will. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So you respond with His praise, meaning with His command. Ibn Jurayj said the same. Qatada said with His knowledge and obedience. Some of them said, On the Day He calls you and you respond with His praise, meaning, to Him be praise in every situation. It was mentioned in the hadith, “There is no loneliness in the graves of the people of ‘There is no god but God.’ It is as if I see the people of ‘There is no god but God’ rising from their graves, shaking the dirt off their heads, saying, ‘There is no god but God.’” In another narration, they say, Praise be to God who has removed sorrow from us. This will come in Surah Fatir. And the Almighty said: And you think meaning on the Day you rise from your graves that you had tarried meaning in this worldly abode except a little, and like His Almighty’s saying: On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had not tarried except an afternoon or a morning thereof, and the Almighty said: “On the Day the Trumpet will be blown and We will gather the criminals that Day blue-eyed. They will whisper to one another, “You tarried only ten days.” We are most knowing of what they say when the best of them in way will say, You tarried only a day. And the Almighty said: “And on the Day the Hour will appear, the criminals will swear that they had not tarried except an hour. Thus were they deluded.” And the Almighty said: “He will say, ‘How many years did you remain on the earth?’ They will say, ‘We tarried a day or part of a day. So ask the counters.’ He will say, ‘You tarried only a little, if you only knew.’”

17:53: The Blessed and Exalted commands His servant and Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to command the believing servants of God to speak the best words and kindest words when addressing and conversing with them. If they do not do that, Satan will cause trouble between them, and will turn speech into action, and will cause evil, disputes, and fighting. He has been an enemy to Adam and his descendants since he refused to prostrate to Adam, and his enmity is clear and evident. For this reason, He forbade a man from pointing at his Muslim brother with a sharp object, because Satan will pull it into his hand, meaning he may strike him with it. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘None of you should point a weapon at his brother, for you do not know, perhaps Satan may tempt him into his hand and he may fall into a pit of Hellfire.’” Both of them narrated it from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad told us, Ali ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: A man from Banu Sulait told me: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was among the lowest of people, and I heard him say: ‘A Muslim is a brother to a Muslim. He does not wrong him nor does piety forsake him. Here, piety is.’” Hammad said: He pointed with his hand to his chest: “And no two men love each other for the sake of God and then separate them except that an incident will occur between one of them, the initiator of the incident is evil, the initiator of the incident is evil, and the initiator of the incident is evil.”
17:54: God Almighty says: Your Lord knows you best, O people, meaning He knows best who among you deserves guidance and who does not. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you, by granting you success in obeying Him and turning to Him. “Or if He wills, He will punish you. And We have not sent you over them as a guardian,” meaning We have only sent you as a warner, so whoever obeys you will enter Paradise, and whoever disobeys you will enter Hell. And His saying, And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth, meaning their ranks in obedience and disobedience, And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others, and as God Almighty said, “These are the messengers. We preferred some of them over others. Among them were those to whom God spoke, and He raised some of them in degree.” This does not contradict what was established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Do not make distinctions between the prophets, for what is meant by that is preference based on mere desire and partisanship, not on the basis of evidence. So if evidence indicates something, it must be followed. There is no dispute that the messengers are better than the rest of the prophets, and that those of resolve among them are the best of them, and they are the five mentioned explicitly in two verses of the Qur’an in Surat al-Ahzab, And when We took a covenant from the prophets and from you and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary, and in Ash-Shura, His saying, “He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus - that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein.” There is no dispute that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the best of them, then after him Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, peace be upon them. Peace be upon the famous one, and we have explained it with its evidence in other places, and God is the Grantor of success. And the Almighty’s saying: And We gave David the Psalms is a reminder of his virtue and honor. Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq bin Nasr told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, who said: The Qur’an was made easy for David, so he would order his mount to be saddled, and he would recite it before he finished, meaning the Qur’an.

17:56: God Almighty says: Say O Muhammad to these polytheists who worshipped other than God Call upon those whom you claim besides Him of idols and rivals, so turn to them for they do not possess the power to remove harm from you that is, completely nor to transfer it that is, to transfer it to someone other than you, and the meaning is that the One who has the power to do that is God alone, with no partner, to Whom belongs creation and command. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Say, Call upon those whom you claim the verse, he said: The polytheists used to say we worship the angels, the Messiah, and Ezra, and they are the ones who call upon meaning in the angels, the Messiah, and Ezra. And the Almighty’s saying: Those are the ones who call upon the verse, Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Sulayman bin Mihran Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding his saying: Those are the ones who call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord, he said: People from the jinn used to worship and then converted to Islam. And in another narration: He said: People from among mankind used to worship people from the jinn, so the jinn converted to Islam and these people adhered to their religion. And Qatada said on the authority of Ma’bad bin Abdullah Al-Zamani on the authority of Abdullah bin Utbah bin Mas’ud on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding his saying: Those are the ones who call upon the verse, he said: It was revealed about a group of Arabs who used to worship a group of jinn, so the jinn converted to Islam and the humans who used to worship them did not realize their conversion, so this verse was revealed. And in another narration on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, they used to worship a group of angels called the jinn, so he mentioned it. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Those are they who call upon, seeking means of approach to their Lord, which of them is nearest, he said: Jesus, his mother and Ezra. Mughirah said on the authority of Ibrahim: Ibn Abbas used to say regarding this verse: They are Jesus, Ezra, the sun and the moon. Mujahid said: Jesus, Ezra and the angels. Ibn Jarir chose the statement of Ibn Masoud for his statement, seek means of approach to their Lord, and this does not refer to the past, so it does not include Jesus, Ezra and the angels. He said: The means is the nearness, as Qatada said, and that is why he said: Which of them is nearest. And the statement of God the Almighty: And they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment, worship is not complete except with fear and hope, so with fear one refrains from prohibitions, and with hope one increases acts of obedience. And the statement of God the Almighty: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to be feared, meaning one should beware of it and fear its occurrence and happening, may God protect us from it.
