17:58: This is report from God Almighty that He has decreed and decided what He has in the Preserved Tablet: that there is no village but that He will destroy it by annihilating all its people or punishing them with a severe punishment either by killing or by testing them with whatever He wills, and that will only be because of their sins and transgressions, as God Almighty said about past nations: And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves and God Almighty said: So it tasted the evil consequences of its deed, and the outcome of its deed was loss and He said: And how many a village was insolent toward the command of its Lord and His messengers and the verses.
17:59: Sanid said on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The polytheists said: O Muhammad, you claim that there were prophets before you, among them was one to whom the wind was subjected, and among them was one who brought the dead back to life. If you want us to believe in you and believe you, then ask your Lord to make Safa gold for us. So God revealed to him: I have heard what they said, so if you wish us to do what they said, but if they do not believe, the punishment will come down, for there is no debate after the revelation of the verse. If you wish us to have some patience with your people, then have some patience with them. He said: O Lord, take their time. Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, and others said the same. Imam Ahmad narrated: Uthman ibn Muhammad told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Iyas, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The people of Mecca asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to turn Safa into gold for them, and to move the mountains away from them so that they could farm. He was told: If you wish, we can take our time with them, or if you wish that what they asked for will come to them, then if they disbelieve, they will perish, as the nations before them were perished. He said: No, rather take their time with them. Then God Almighty revealed: And nothing prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them. An-Nasa’i and Ibn Jarir narrated it with this. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail, on the authority of Imran ibn Hakim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Quraysh said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Pray to your Lord to turn Safa into gold for us and we will believe in you. He said: And will you do that? They said: Yes. He said: So he prayed, and Gabriel came to him and said: Your Lord sends you his greetings and says to you: If you wish, I will turn Safa into gold for them. Whoever disbelieves among them after that, I will punish him with a punishment such as I have not punished anyone in the worlds, and if you wish, I will open for them the gates of repentance and mercy. He said: Rather, the gate of repentance and mercy. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said in his Musnad: Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ali al-Ansari told us, Khalaf bin Tamim al-Masisi told us, on the authority of Abdul-Jabbar bin Umar al-Ayli, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ata bin Ibrahim, on the authority of his grandmother Umm Ata, the servant of al-Zubayr bin al-Awwam, who said: “I heard al-Zubayr say when the verse ‘And warn your nearest relatives’ was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, shouted at Abu Qubays, ‘O family of Abd Manaf, I am a warner.’ So the Quraysh came to him and he warned them and warned them, but they said: ‘You claim that you are a prophet to whom revelation is sent, while Solomon subjected the wind and the mountains, and Moses subjected the sea to him, and Jesus used to revive the dead. So ask God to remove these mountains from us and cause rivers to gush forth from the earth for us, so that we may use them as plows and plant and eat. Otherwise, ask God to revive our dead for us so that we may speak to them and they may speak to us. Otherwise, ask God to turn this rock beneath you into gold so that we may carve from it and it will make us independent of the winter and summer journeys, for you claim that you are…’” As for their form. And he said: While we were around him, the revelation came down to him. When it was over, he said: By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, He has given me what you asked for, and if I had wished it would have been, but He gave me the choice between you entering the Gate of Mercy so that your believer would believe, or leaving you to whatever you chose for yourselves so that you would stray from the Gate of Mercy, and none of you would believe. So I chose the Gate of Mercy so that your believer would believe, and He informed me that if He gave you that and then you disbelieved, He would punish you with a punishment by which He has not punished anyone in the worlds. And the verse was revealed: And nothing prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them. And he recited three verses, and the verse was revealed: And if there had been a Qur’an by which mountains were moved, or the earth was split asunder, or the dead were made to speak… And for this reason the Almighty said: And what prevented Us from sending the signs meaning that We send the signs and bring them as your people asked of You, for it is easy and simple for Us, except that the first ones denied them after they asked for them, and Our practice with them and their likes is that We do not delay if they deny them after their revelation, as the Almighty said in al-Ma’idah 5:God said, ‘Indeed, I will send it down upon you, but whoever disbelieves after that among you - then I will punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone in the worlds.’ And the Almighty said about Thamud when they asked for a sign - a she-camel coming out of a rock they had identified, so Salih, peace be upon him, called upon his Lord, and He brought out for them from it a she-camel as they had asked Him. But when they wronged it - meaning they disbelieved in the One who created it and denied His Messenger and hamstrung it - He said, “Enjoy yourselves in your home for three days. That is a promise not to be denied.” That is why God Almighty said: And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. That is, indicating the Oneness of the One who created her and the truthfulness of His Messenger whose prayer was answered regarding her. But they wronged her. That is, they disbelieved in her, prevented them from drinking from her, and killed her. So God annihilated them all, took revenge on them, and seized them with the grip of the Mighty, the Powerful. And the Almighty said: And We do not send the signs except as a warning. Qatada said: God Almighty frightens people with whatever signs He wills, so that they may take heed, remember, and return. It was mentioned to us that Kufa shook during the time of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, so he said: O people, your Lord seeks your repentance, so repent to Him. And it was also narrated that Medina was shaken several times during the time of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, so Omar said: You have innovated, by God, if it happens again, I will do it and I will do it. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the agreed upon hadith: “The sun and the moon are two signs from the signs of God, and they do not eclipse for the death or life of anyone, but God Almighty frightens His servants with them, so if you see that, then rush to remember Him, supplicate to Him, and seek His forgiveness.” Then he said: O nation of Muhammad, by God, no one is more jealous than God when His servant or his female servant commits adultery. O nation of Muhammad, by God, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much.”
17:60: God the Almighty says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, urging him to convey His message, informing him that He has protected him from the people, for He is the One who has power over them and they are in His grip and under His subjugation and dominance. Mujahid, Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others said regarding His statement: And when We said to you, ‘Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people’ meaning He has protected you from them. And His statement: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people the verse, Al-Bukhari said: Ali ibn Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people he said: It is a vision that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw on the night of his Isra’, and the accursed tree in the Qur’an is the tree of Zaqqum, and Ahmad, Abd Al-Razzaq and others narrated it in the same way on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. And Al-Awfi narrated it in the same way on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Thus, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Hasan, Masruq, Ibrahim, Qatadah, Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid, and others interpreted it as the Night of Isra’, and the hadiths of Isra’ have been presented in full at the beginning of the Surah, praise and thanks be to God. It was mentioned that some people turned back from their religion after they had been on the truth, because their hearts and minds could not bear it, so they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge, and God made that a steadfastness and certainty for others, and for this reason He said, except a trial, meaning a test and examination. As for the cursed tree, it is the tree of Zaqqum, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told them that he saw Paradise and Hell, and he saw the tree of Zaqqum, but they denied that until Abu Jahl, may God’s curses be upon him, said: Bring us dates and butter, and he began to eat from this with this, and he said: Eat from it, for we do not know Zaqqum other than this. This was narrated by Ibn Abbas, Masruq, Abu Malik, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and others, and everyone who said that it was the Night of Isra’ interpreted it in the same way as the tree of Zaqqum. It was said: What is meant by the cursed tree is the Umayyads, and this is strange and weak. Ibn Jarir said: I was told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Zabalah, who told us: Abdul-Muhaimin ibn Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sa`d told us, who told me, on the authority of my father, who told me, on the authority of my grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the sons of so-and-so jumping on his pulpit like monkeys, and that upset him, so he could not stop laughing until he died. He said: And God revealed about that, And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, the verse. This chain of transmission is very weak, because Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Zabalah is rejected, and his sheikh is also completely weak. For this reason, Ibn Jarir chose that what was meant by that was the Night of the Isra’, and that the cursed tree was the tree of Zaqqum. He said: Because of the consensus of the hujjat of the people of interpretation on that, i.e. in the vision and the tree, and His saying, And We frighten them, i.e. the disbelievers with threats, torment, and punishment, But it only increases them in great transgression, i.e., persistence in what they are in of disbelief and misguidance, and that is because God has abandoned them.
17:61: The Blessed and Exalted mentions the enmity of Iblis, may God curse him, and his offspring, and that it is an ancient enmity since the creation of Adam, for He, the Almighty, commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, and they all prostrated except Iblis, who was arrogant and refused to prostrate to him out of pride and contempt for him. He said, ‘Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?’ As He said in the other verse, “I am better than him. You created me from fire, and created him from clay.” He also said, Have you seen him say to the Lord with boldness and disbelief, while the Lord is patient and looks on? “He said, ‘Have you seen this one whom You have honored above me?’” The verse, Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He says, ‘I will take control of his offspring, except for a few.’ Mujahid said, I will contain them. Ibn Zayd said, I will mislead them. All of these are close in meaning, and the meaning is, Have you seen this one whom You have honored and glorified above me? If You give me respite, I will mislead his offspring, except for a few of them.
17:62: The Blessed and Exalted mentions the enmity of Iblis, may God curse him, and his offspring, and that it is an ancient enmity since the creation of Adam, for He, the Almighty, commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, and they all prostrated except Iblis, who was arrogant and refused to prostrate to him out of pride and contempt for him. He said, ‘Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?’ As He said in the other verse, “I am better than him. You created me from fire, and created him from clay.” He also said, Have you seen him say to the Lord with boldness and disbelief, while the Lord is patient and looks on? “He said, ‘Have you seen this one whom You have honored above me?’” The verse, Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He says, ‘I will take control of his offspring, except for a few.’ Mujahid said, I will contain them. Ibn Zayd said, I will mislead them. All of these are close in meaning, and the meaning is, Have you seen this one whom You have honored and glorified above me? If You give me respite, I will mislead his offspring, except for a few of them.
17:63: When Iblis asked for a reprieve, God said to him, Go, for I have given you a reprieve, as He said in the other verse. He said, For indeed, you are among those granted reprieve * Until the Day of the Appointed Time. Then He threatened him and those who followed him from the descendants of Adam with Hell. He said, 'Go, for whoever follows you among them, indeed, Hell is your recompense,' meaning for your deeds. A full recompense. Mujahid said, A full recompense. Qatadah said, A full recompense for you, with no decrease from it. And the Almighty’s saying: And incite with your voice whomever you can among them It was said that it is singing. Mujahid said: With amusement and singing meaning that he made them belittle that. Ibn Abbas said regarding his saying: And incite with your voice whomever you can among them He said: Every caller who calls to disobeying God the Almighty. Qatada said: Ibn Jarir chose it. And the Almighty’s saying: And attack them with your cavalry and infantry He says: And attack them with your soldiers, their cavalry and infantry, for man is the plural of rajil just as the rakab is the plural of rakib and sahab is the plural of sahabi and its meaning is to control them with whatever you are able to do. This is a matter of predestination like the Almighty’s saying: Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with incitement That is, they incite them to disobedience and drive them to it. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said regarding his saying: And incite with your cavalry and infantry He said: Every rider and pedestrian in disobedience to God. Qatada said: He has horses and men from the jinn and mankind, and they are the ones who obey him. The Arabs say: Ajlab so-and-so against so-and-so if he shouted at him. And from this he forbade in a race from Al-Jalb and Al-Janb, from which the word jalbah is derived, which means raising voices. The Almighty said: And share with them in wealth and children. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: It is what he commanded them to do of spending wealth in disobeying God. Ata’ said: It is usury. Al-Hasan said: It is collecting it from filth and spending it in what is forbidden. Qatada said the same. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, as for his sharing with them in their wealth, it is what they forbade from their livestock, meaning from the Baha’ir and the Sawaa’ib and the like. Ad-Dahhak and Qatada said the same. Ibn Jarir said: It is better to say that the verse includes all of that. His statement: And children, Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak, meaning the children of fornication. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, it is what they killed from their children foolishly without knowledge. Qatada and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: By God, he shared with them in wealth and children, they became Magians, Jews, Christians and dyed in a way other than the dye of Islam, and divided their wealth as a portion for the devil. Qatada said the same. Abu Salih said on the authority of Ibn Abbas is their naming of their children Abd al-Harith, Abd al-Shams, and Abd so-and-so. Ibn Jarir said: The most correct of the sayings is to say that every child born to a female who disobeys God by naming him with something that God dislikes, or by introducing him to a religion other than the one that God has approved, or by committing adultery with his mother, or by killing him, or other matters in which God is disobeyed by doing it or in it, then he has entered into the partnership of Satan in it from the one who gave birth to that child to him or from him, because God did not specify in His saying and share with them in wealth and children the meaning of partnership in it in one meaning without meaning. So everything in which God was disobeyed or in which Satan was obeyed or in which he or she is obeyed is partnership. This that he said is valid, and each of the early Muslims, may God have mercy on them, explained some of the partnership. It was proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Iyad ibn Hammad that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God the Almighty says: I created My servants as monotheists, then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion and forbade them what I had permitted for them.” And in the two Sahihs, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If one of them wanted to have intercourse with his wife, he would say: In the name of God, O God, keep us away from it.” Satan and keep Satan away from what You have provided for us, for if a child is decreed between them in that, Satan will never harm him.” And the Almighty said: He promised them - and Satan promises them nothing but delusion. Just as the Almighty informed us about Satan that he will say when the truth becomes clear on the Day when He will judge with truth: Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And the Almighty said: Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them. This is a statement of His Almighty’s support for His believing servants, His preservation of them, and His guarding them from the accursed Satan. For this reason, the Almighty said: And sufficient is your Lord as a Disposer of affairs. That is, a protector, supporter, and helper. Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi’ah narrated to us, on the authority of Musa ibn Wardan, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, the believer restrains his devils as one of you restrains his camel on a journey. He restrains means he takes hold of its forelock and subdues it.

17:66: And the Almighty tells of His kindness to His creation in His subjecting the ships in the sea to His servants and His facilitating the interests of His servants in seeking His grace in trade from one region to another. For this reason He said: Indeed, He was to you Merciful, meaning that He only did this to you out of His grace and mercy upon you.
17:67: The Blessed and Exalted tells us that when people are afflicted with harm, they call upon Him, turning to Him and sincerely devoting their religion to Him. For this reason, the Almighty said: And when harm touches you at sea, lost are those you call upon except Him. That is, everything you worship other than God Almighty is gone from your hearts, as happened with Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl when he fled from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he conquered Mecca. He went fleeing and boarded the sea to enter Abyssinia, and a violent wind came upon them. The people said to each other, Nothing will benefit you except that you call upon God alone. Ikrimah said to himself, “By God, if nothing is of any use at sea other than Him, then nothing is of any use on land other than Him. O God, I have a covenant with You that if You take me out of it, I will go and place my hand in the hand of Muhammad, and I will find him to be compassionate and merciful.” So they came out of the sea and he returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he converted to Islam, and his conversion was good, may God be pleased with him and satisfy him. And the Almighty’s saying, But when He delivered you to the land, you turned away, meaning you forgot what you knew of His Oneness and turned away from calling upon Him alone, with no partner for Him. And man is ungrateful, meaning that this is his nature, he forgets blessings and denies them, except for those whom God protects.
17:68: God Almighty says: Did you think that by going out to the land you would be safe from His vengeance and punishment, that He would not cause a part of the land to swallow you up, or that He would send upon you a hailstorm, which is rain that contains stones? This was said by Mujahid and more than one person, just as God Almighty said: “Indeed, We sent upon them a hailstorm, except for the family of Lot. We saved them at dawn, a favor from Us.” And He said in another verse: And We rained upon them stones of baked clay. And He said: “Do you feel secure from Him who is in the heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you up, and behold, it is swaying? Or do you feel secure from Him who is in the heaven that He will not send upon you a hailstorm? Then you will know how My warner is.” And His statement: Then you will not find for yourselves a protector, meaning a supporter who will repel that from you and save you from it.
17:69: God the Most High says, Or do you feel secure O you who turned away from Us after you acknowledged Our Oneness at sea and went out to land, that He will return you to the sea a second time, and send upon you a violent wind meaning that it will violently break the masts and sink the ships. Ibn Abbas and others said: The violent wind is the wind of the seas that breaks the ships and sinks them. His statement, and will drown you because of your disbelief means because of your disbelief and turning away from God the Most High. His statement, Then you will not find for yourselves against Us any supporter thereof Ibn Abbas said a supporter. Mujahid said a supporter, a rebel, meaning one who will take revenge for you after you. Qatada said: We do not fear anyone who will follow us with any of that.
17:70: And the Almighty informs us about His honoring and glorifying the children of Adam in His creation of them in the best and most perfect forms, as He says, Indeed, We created man in the best stature, meaning he walks standing upright on his feet and eats with his hands, while other animals walk on four legs and eat with their mouths. He gave him hearing, sight, and a heart by which he understands all of that and benefits from it and differentiates between things and knows their benefits, properties, and harms in religious and worldly matters. And We carried them on land, meaning on beasts of burden, such as cattle, horses, and mules, and also at sea on large and small ships. And We provided them with good things, meaning crops, fruits, meats, and milk of all kinds of desirable and delicious tastes and colors, beautiful sights, and fine clothing of all kinds, with their different types, colors, and shapes, which they make for themselves and which others bring to them from different regions and areas. And We preferred them over many of those We have created, with a marked preference, meaning of all other animals. And the types of creatures. This noble verse has been used as evidence for the superiority of the human race over the angels. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam who said: The angels said, O our Lord, You have given the children of Adam this world to eat from and enjoy, but You have not given us that, so give us the Hereafter. Then God the Most High said, By My glory and majesty, I will not make the righteous offspring of those I have created with My hands like those to whom I said, ‘Be,’ and they were. This hadith is mursal from this source, and it has been narrated from another source in a connected form. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sadaqah al-Baghdadi told us, Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Khalid al-Masisi told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, Abu Ghassan Muhammad bin Mutraf told us, on the authority of Safwan bin Salim, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The angels said, ‘O our Lord, You have given the children of Adam the world in which they eat, drink, and wear clothing, and we glorify You with praise and do not eat, drink, or play. So just as You have given them the world, give us the Hereafter.’ He said, ‘I will not make the righteous offspring of one whom I have created with My hands like one to whom I said, ‘Be,’ and he was.” Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ayoub al-Razi, who said: Al-Hasan bin Ali bin Khalaf al-Saydalani told us, Sulayman bin Abd al-Rahman told us, Uthman bin Hisn told me, on the authority of Ubaydah bin Alaq, I heard Urwah bin Ruwaym al-Lakhmi tell me, Anas bin Malik told me, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The angels said, ‘O our Lord, You created us and created the children of Adam and made them eat food, drink, wear clothes, marry women, and ride beasts.’ They sleep and rest, and You have not made any of that for us, so make this world for them and the Hereafter for us. So God, the Almighty, said: I will not make one whom I created with My hands and breathed into him of My spirit like one who said to him, Be, and he was. Al-Tabarani said: Abdun bin Ahmad told us, Umar bin Sahl told us, Ubaydullah bin Tamam told us, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Bishr bin Shaghaf, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is nothing more honorable to God on the Day of Resurrection than the son of Adam. It was said: O Messenger of God, not even the angels? He said: Not even the angels. The angels are compelled, like the sun and the moon.” This is a very strange hadith.
17:71: The Blessed and Exalted tells us about the Day of Resurrection that He will hold every nation accountable for their leader, and they differed about that. Mujahid and Qatadah said, For every nation is a messenger, so when their messenger comes, it will be judged between them with justice (al-Anbiya’ 2:10). Some of the Salaf said, "This is the greatest honor for the people of Hadith because their leader is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace." Ibn Zayd said, For their book that was sent down to their Prophet from the legislation, and Ibn Jarir chose it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid that he said, With their books. It is possible that he meant this and that he meant what al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his statement, On the Day when We will call every people with their leader, meaning with their book of deeds. Abu al-Aaliyah, al-Hasan, and al-Dahhak said the same. This statement is the most likely, because of the statement of the Almighty, And everything We have recorded in a clear register, and the Almighty said, And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, (al-Anbiya’ 2:10). It is possible that what is meant by their leader is every people with those whom they follow, so the people of faith followed the prophets, peace be upon them. Peace be upon you, and the people of disbelief followed their imams as He said, And We made them imams calling to the Fire. And in the two Sahihs, So that every nation may follow what it used to worship, and whoever used to worship the tyrants will follow. The hadith. And the Most High said, “And you will see every nation kneeling. Every nation will be called to its book. Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do. This is Our book that speaks against you with the truth. Indeed, We were transcribing what you used to do.” This does not contradict the fact that the Prophet will be brought when God judges between his nation, for he must be a witness over his nation with their deeds, as He, the Most High, said, And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the book will be laid open, and the prophets and witnesses will be brought. And He, the Most High, said, How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these? But what is meant here by the imam is the book of deeds, and that is why the Most High said, “The Day We will call every people with their imam. So whoever is given his book in his right hand - those will read their book.” That is, from his joy and happiness with what is in it of righteous deeds, he will read it and love to read it, as He said: “But as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, ‘Here, read my record. Indeed, I thought that I would meet my account.’ So he will be in a pleasant life, in an elevated garden, with its fruits within reach. Eat and drink in happiness for what you put forth in the past days.” And as for he who is given his record in his left hand, nor will they be wronged as much as a thread, it has already been mentioned that the thread is the long thread in the slit of the pit. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar narrated a hadith in this regard, saying: Muhammad bin Ya`mar and Muhammad bin Uthman bin Karamah told us: Ubaydullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Isra`il, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement of God, the Most High: On the Day when We will call every people with their leader, he said: “One of them will be called and given his book in his right hand, his body will be stretched out for him, his face will be whitened, and a crown of pearls will be placed on his head that will shine. He will go to his companions, and they will see him from afar and say: O God, bring us this and bless us in this. So he will come to them and say: Be of good cheer, for every man among you will have something like this. As for the disbeliever, his face will be blackened and his body will be stretched out for him, and his companions will see him and say: I seek refuge in God from this or from the evil of this. O God, do not bring him to us. So he will come to them and they will say: O God, disgrace him. So he will say: May God distance you, for every man among you will have something like this.” Then Al-Bazzar said: It is not narrated except from this source. And the statement of God, the Most High: And whoever is blind in this verse, Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: Qatada and Ibn Zayd: And whoever is blind in this meaning in this worldly life is blind in the Hereafter meaning that is, to God’s proof, signs and proofs and even more astray in the way meaning even more astray than he was in this world, God forbid that.

17:73: The Almighty tells us about His support for His Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and His confirmation, protection, and safety from the evil of the wicked and the plots of the immoral, and that the Almighty is the one who takes care of his affairs and supports him, and that He does not leave him to any of His creation, but rather He is his guardian, protector, supporter, helper, and victor, and He makes his religion prevail over those who oppose him, disagree with him, and oppose him in the East and West of the earth. May God’s prayers and peace be upon him in abundance until the Day of Judgment.

17:76: It was said: It was revealed about the Jews when they advised the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to live in the Levant, the land of the prophets, and to leave living in Medina. This statement is weak, because this verse is Meccan and the city was settled after that. It was said: It was revealed in Tabuk, but its authenticity is questionable. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Al-Hakim, on the authority of Al-Asamm, on the authority of Ahmad bin Abdul-Jabbar Al-Attardi, on the authority of Yunus bin Bakir, on the authority of Abdul-Hamid bin Bahram, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abdul-Rahman bin Ghanem, that the Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one day and said: O Abu Al-Qasim, if you are truthful that you are a prophet, then head to Ash-Sham, for Ash-Sham is the land of the gathering and the land of the prophets. So he believed what they said, so he invaded Tabuk, intending nothing but Ash-Sham. When he reached Tabuk, God revealed to him verses from Surat Bani Israel after the surah had been concluded: “And indeed, they almost tempted you from the land to expel you from it, and then they would not remain after you except a little. This was the way of those of Our messengers We sent before you, and you will not find in Our way any change.” So God commanded him to return to Medina, and said: In it is your life and your death, and from it you will be resurrected. This chain of transmission is questionable, and it is most likely that this is not correct, because the Prophet did not invade Tabuk because of what the Jews said, but rather he invaded it in compliance with the words of God Almighty: O you who believe, fight those of the disbelievers who are near you and the words of God Almighty: “Fight those who do not believe in God or the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have forbidden and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture - until they pay the jizyah with willing submission while they are subdued.” And he invaded it to exact retribution and take revenge on those of his companions who killed the people of Mu’tah, and God knows best. If this were correct, it would have been based on the hadith narrated by Al-Walid bin Muslim on the authority of Ufayr bin Ma’dan, on the authority of Salim bin Amir, on the authority of Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Qur’an was revealed in three places: Mecca, Medina, and Ash-Sham.” Al-Walid said: He means Jerusalem, and the interpretation of Ash-Sham as Tabuk is better than what Al-Walid said that it is Jerusalem, and God knows best. It was said that it was revealed about the infidels of Quraysh, who intended to expel the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among them, so God threatened them with this verse, and that if they expelled him, they would not have stayed in Mecca after him except for a short time. And that is how it happened, for after his migration from among them, after their harm to him had intensified, it was only a year and a half, until God gathered them and him at Badr without an appointment, and He enabled him to overpower them and gave him power over them and made him triumph over them, so he killed their nobles and took their children captive. For this reason, God Almighty said: This is the way of those We have sent verse, meaning this is our custom with those who disbelieved in Our Messengers and harmed them by the Messenger’s expulsion from among them, the punishment would come to them. And if he, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, were not the Messenger of Mercy, there would have come to them from the punishments in this world that no one could bear. For this reason, God Almighty said: And God would not punish them while you are among them verse.

17:78: The Blessed and Exalted says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanding him to perform the prescribed prayers at their appointed times: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun. It was said at its setting, as Ibn Masoud, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd said. Hisham said on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Its decline is its disappearance. Nafi’ narrated it on the authority of Ibn Umar, and Malik narrated it in his interpretation on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ibn Umar, and Abu Barzah Al-Aslami said it, and it is also a narration on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud and Mujahid, and Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Ja’far Al-Baqir, and Qatadah said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Among the evidence for this is what he narrated on the authority of Ibn Hamid on the authority of Al-Hakam Ibn Bashir: Amr Ibn Qays told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla on the authority of a man on the authority of Jabir Ibn Abdullah who said: “I invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and whoever of his companions wanted to eat with me, then they went out when the sun declined, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and said: Go out, O Abu Bakr, for this is when the sun has declined.” Then he narrated it on the authority of Sahl Ibn Bakkar on the authority of Abu Awanah on the authority of Al-Aswad Ibn Qays, on the authority of Nabih Al-Anzi on the authority of Jabir on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Based on this, this verse includes the times of the five prayers, so from His saying: The decline of the sun until dusk... Night, which is its darkness, and it was said that it is sunset, from which noon, afternoon, sunset, and evening were taken. His saying: And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn means the dawn prayer. The Sunnah has explained the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a continuous chain of transmission of his actions and sayings, with details of these times, as the people of Islam do today, from what they received from their predecessors and generation after generation, as is established in its places, and praise be to God. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Ibrahim on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, and on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this verse: “And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed.” He said: It is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The superiority of the prayer of a group over the prayer of one person is twenty-five degrees, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the dawn prayer. Abu Hurairah said: Recite if you wish, “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed.” Imam Ahmad said: Asbat told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed,” he said: It is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah, all three of them on the authority of Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad on the authority of his father, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic. In a wording in the two Sahihs on the authority of Malik on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad on the authority of Al-A’raj on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Angels take turns among you by night and angels by day, and they gather at the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. Then those who spent the night among you ascend and their Lord asks them - and He is most knowing of you - how did you leave My servants? They say: We came to them while they were praying, and we left them while they were praying.” Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: The two guards gather at the dawn prayer, so some ascend and those stand. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Mujahid, Qatadah and more than one said the same in their interpretation of this verse. As for the hadith that Ibn Jarir narrated here from the hadith of Al-Layth bin Saad, on the authority of Ziyadah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Fadala bin Ubaid, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he mentioned the hadith of the descent, and that God Almighty says: Whoever seeks My forgiveness, I will forgive him. Whoever asks Me, I will give him. Whoever calls upon Me, I will answer him until dawn comes, so that is why He says: “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed,” so God, the angels of the night, and the angels of the day witness it, and Ziyadah is the only one who narrated it, and he has a hadith about this in Sunan Abi Dawud. God the Almighty said: And during part of the night, then pray with it as an additional prayer for you. This is a command for him to perform the night prayer after the obligatory prayer, as was reported in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was asked which prayer is best after the obligatory prayer? He said, The night prayer. For this reason God the Almighty commanded His Messenger to perform the night prayer after the obligatory prayers, because the night prayer is what is done after sleeping. This was said by Alqamah, Al-Aswad, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and others, and it is well-known in the language of the Arabs. Likewise, the hadiths were confirmed on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to perform the night prayer after sleeping, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Aisha and others from the Companions, may God be pleased with them, as is explained in detail in its place. Praise and thanks be to God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: It is what comes after the evening prayer and it is interpreted as what comes after sleep. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of the Almighty’s statement: A voluntary prayer for you. It was said that it means that you are the only one who is obligated to do that, so they made the night prayer obligatory for him and not for the nation. Al-Awfi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is one of the two opinions of the scholars, and one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, and Ibn Jarir chose it. It was said: The night prayer was made a voluntary prayer for him in particular, because his past and future sins have been forgiven, and for others from his nation, only his voluntary prayers expiate the sins that he has committed. Mujahid said it: And it is in Al-Musnad on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Bahili, may God be pleased with him. And His statement: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station, meaning, do what I have commanded you to do so that We may establish you on the Day of Resurrection in a praised station, where all of creation and their Creator, Blessed and Exalted be He, will praise you. Ibn Jarir said: Most of the people of interpretation said: That is the station that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will stand on the Day of Resurrection to intercede for the people so that their Lord may relieve them of the great hardship they will be in on that Day. Mention who said that Ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Silah ibn Zafar, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: The people will be gathered on one plain, the caller will hear them and their sight will penetrate them, barefoot and naked as they were created, standing, no soul will speak except with His permission. He will call out: O Muhammad, and he will say: “At your service and at your pleasure, and good is in your hands and evil is not from you, and the Mahdi is he whom you have guided, and your servant is before you, and from you and to you there is no escape or refuge from you except to you, blessed and exalted are you, glory be to you, Lord of the House.” This is the praised station that God the Almighty mentioned. Then he narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ghundar, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, and Abd al-Razzaq narrated it likewise on the authority of Muammar and al-Thawri, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, and Ibn Abbas said: This praised station is the station of intercession, and Ibn Abi Nujayh said the same on the authority of Mujahid, and al-Hasan al-Basri said the same. Qatada said: He is the first from whom the earth will split open on the Day of Resurrection and the first intercessor. The people of knowledge used to consider him to be the praised station of which God Almighty said: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station. I said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about honors on the Day of Resurrection that no one will share with him, and honors that no one will equal him in. He is the first from whom the earth will split open and he will be sent riding to the place of assembly. He has the banner under which Adam and those after him were under its banner. He has the pool from which there is no one more likely to come to the place of assembly. He has the greatest intercession with God to come to decide the judgment between the creation. This will happen after people ask Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, and each one says: I am not up for it, until they come to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he says: I am up for it, I am up for it, as we will mention in detail in this place, God willing. Among these is that he intercedes for people who have been ordered to Hell, so that they may be returned from it. He is the first of the prophets to judge between his nation, and the first of them to cross the Sirat with his nation. He is the first intercessor in Paradise, as proven in Sahih Muslim. In the hadith of the images, it is stated that all believers will not enter Paradise except through his intercession, and he will be the first to enter it, and his nation will precede all nations, and he will intercede to raise the ranks of people whose deeds cannot reach it, and he is the possessor of the means which is the highest station in Paradise that is only befitting of him, and if God Almighty permits intercession for the sinners, the angels, prophets and believers will intercede, and he will intercede for people whose number is known only to God Almighty, and no one intercedes like him or is equal to him in that, and I have explained that in detail at the end of the Book of Seerah in the chapter on characteristics, and praise and thanks be to God, and now let us mention the hadiths that were reported about the praised station and with God is the helper. Al-Bukhari said: Ismail bin Abaan told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us on the authority of Adam bin Ali, I heard Ibn Umar say: “On the Day of Resurrection, people will become like knees, every nation that follows its prophet will say: O so-and-so, intercede, O so-and-so, intercede, until intercession ends with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that is the day when God will raise him to a praised station.” It was narrated by Hamza bin Abdullah on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me, Shuaib ibn Al-Layth told us, Al-Layth told us on the authority of Ubaidullah ibn Abi Ja`far, that he said: I heard Hamza ibn Abdullah ibn Umar say: I heard Abdullah ibn Umar say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The sun draws near until the sweat reaches half of the ear. While they are like that, they will seek help from Adam, but he will say: ‘I am not the one to do that.’ Then from Moses, and he will say the same. Then from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he will intercede among the creation and walk until he takes hold of the ring of the door of Paradise. On that day, God will raise him to a praiseworthy station.’” And this is how Al-Bukhari narrated it in Zakat on the authority of Yahya ibn Bakir and Alqamah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salih, both on the authority of Al-Layth ibn Sa`d, with the same chain of transmission, and he added: On that day, God will raise him to a praiseworthy station, and all the people of the assembly will praise him. Al-Bukhari said: Ali bin Ayyash told us, Shuaib bin Abi Hamza told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says when he hears the call: O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, grant Muhammad the means and the excellence, and raise him to the praised station which You promised him, my intercession will be permissible for him on the Day of Resurrection.” It was transmitted by him alone, not by Muslim. Hadith of Abi bin Kaab Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir Al-Azdi told us, Zuhair bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel, on the authority of Al-Tufayl bin Abi Kaab, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, I will be the leader of the prophets and their orator and the one who will intercede for them, without boasting. Al-Tirmidhi included it on the authority of Abu Amir Abdul Malik bin Amr Al-Aqdi, and he said: It is good and authentic, and Ibn Majah included it on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel with it. We have already mentioned in the hadith of Abi bin Kaab about reciting the Qur’an in seven letters, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said at the end of it: “So I said: O God, forgive my nation, O God, forgive my nation, and I delayed the third for a day when the creation will yearn for me, even Abraham, peace be upon him.” Hadith of Anas bin Malik Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, Saeed bin Abi Arooba told us, Qatada told us on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The believers will gather on the Day of Resurrection and be inspired by that, and they will say: If only we could intercede with our Lord so that He might relieve us from this place of ours. So they will go to Adam and say: O Adam, you are the father of mankind, God created you with His hand, and His angels prostrated to you, and He taught you the names of everything, so intercede for us with your Lord so that He might relieve us from this place of ours. So Adam will say to them: I am not there for you, and he will mention the sin he committed, and his Lord, the Almighty, will feel ashamed of that, and he will say: But go to Noah, for he was the first Messenger whom God sent to the people of the earth. So they will go to Noah, and he will say: I am not there for you, and he will mention the sin of asking his Lord for something of which he had no knowledge, and his Lord will feel ashamed of that, and he will say: But go to Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful. So they will go to him and he will say: I am not there for you, but go to Moses, a servant to whom God spoke and gave.” The Torah, and they come to Moses, and he says: I am not there with you, and he mentions to them the soul that was killed without a soul, and his Lord is ashamed of that, and says: But go to Jesus, the servant of God and His Messenger and His Word and His Spirit, so they come to Jesus, and he says: I am not there with you, but go to Muhammad, a servant whom God has forgiven his past and future sins, so they come to me - Al-Hasan said this wording - so I stand and walk between two rows of believers - Anas said - until I ask permission to see my Lord, and when I see my Lord, I fall down - or prostrate - to my Lord, and He leaves me as long as God wills that He leaves me - he said - then it is said: Raise Muhammad, say He hears, and intercede and your intercession will be granted, and ask and it will be given to you, so I raise my head and praise Him with praise that He teaches me, then I intercede and He sets a limit for me and I admit them to Paradise, he said: Then I return to Him a second time, and when I see my Lord, I fall down or prostrate to my Lord, and He leaves me as long as God wills that He leaves me, then it is said: Raise Muhammad, say He hears, and ask and it will be given to you Then I will come back a third time and when I see my Lord, I will fall down in prostration to my Lord and He will leave me as long as God wills me to leave. Then it will be said: Raise Muhammad, say and He hears, and ask and He will give you, and intercede and He will intercede. So I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise that He teaches me, then I will intercede and He will set a limit for me and I will enter them into Paradise. Then I will come back a fourth time and say: O Lord, there remains only those whom the Qur’an has detained.” Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then he who says, ‘There is no god but God’ and in his heart there is goodness equal to the weight of a barley seed will come out of the Fire. Then he who says, ‘There is no god but God’ and in his heart there is goodness equal to the weight of a grain of wheat will come out of the Fire. Then he who says, ‘There is no god but God’ and in his heart there is goodness equal to the weight of an atom will come out of the Fire.” They both reported it from the hadith of Sa’id with it. Imam Ahmad narrated it in this way from ‘Affan ibn Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas is tall. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus bin Muhammad narrated to us, Harb bin Maymun Abu Al-Khattab Al-Ansari narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Anas, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated to me, saying: “I am standing, waiting for my nation to cross the bridge, when Jesus, peace be upon him, came to me and said: These prophets have come to you, O Muhammad, asking - or he said: they are gathering to you - and calling upon God to separate all the nations to whatever God wills for the misery they are in. The creation is bridled with sweat. As for the believer, it is like a cold upon him, and as for the disbeliever, death will overtake him. He said: Wait until I return to you. So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went and stood beneath the Throne, and he encountered what no chosen angel or sent prophet has encountered. So God, the Almighty, inspired Gabriel to go to Muhammad and say to him: Raise your head, ask and you will be given, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. So I interceded for my nation, that one person from every ninety-nine should come out. I have not ceased to go back to my Lord, the Almighty, and I do not stand in a place except that I I interceded until God Almighty gave me, including that he said: O Muhammad, include from your nation those of God Almighty’s creation who testified that there is no god but God for one day sincerely and died upon that. Hadith of Buraidah, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Al-Aswad ibn Aamer told us, Abu Israel told us, on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Hasira, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, that he entered upon Muawiyah, and there was a man speaking, so Buraidah said: O Muawiyah, will you permit me to speak? He said: Yes, and he thought that he would say the same as the other one, so Buraidah said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “I hope that I will intercede on the Day of Resurrection as many times as there are trees and mud on the earth.” He said: So you hope for it, O Muawiyah, but Ali, may God be pleased with him, does not hope for it. Hadith of Ibn Masoud - Imam Ahmad said: Arim bin Al-Fadl narrated to us, Saeed bin Al-Fadl narrated to us, Saeed bin Zaid narrated to us, Ali bin Al-Hakam Al-Banani narrated to us, on the authority of Uthman, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah and Al-Aswad, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: “The two sons of Mulaykah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Our mother honors her husband and is kind to her child. He said: They mentioned the guest, but she was buried alive in the pre-Islamic era. He said: Your mother is in Hellfire. He said: So they turned away, and evil was evident on their faces. He ordered them to be returned, and they returned, and joy was evident on their faces, hoping that something had happened. He said: My mother is with your mother. A hypocrite said: What does this man do for his mother, and we are treading on his heels? A man from the Ansar said: I have never seen a man ask more than him, O Messenger of God. Did your Lord promise you about her or both of them? He said: He thought that it was from something he had heard, so he said: I did not ask my Lord, nor did He give me hope for it. I will stand in the praised station on the Day of Resurrection.” The Ansari said: O Messenger of God, what is that praiseworthy station? He said: That is when you are brought barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, and the first to be clothed will be Abraham, peace be upon him, and he will say: Clothe my friend. Then he will be brought two white robes and he will put them on him, then he will make him sit facing the Throne, then my clothing will be brought and I will put it on him, and I will stand on his right in a position that no one will stand on, and the first and the last will envy me for it. He said: And an opening will be made for them from Al-Kawthar to the Pool. The hypocrite said: Water has never flowed except in a state or in a place of dirt. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its state is musk and its dirt is pearls. The hypocrite said: I have not heard of anything like today, for rarely does water flow in a state or in a place of dirt except that it has vegetation. The Ansari said: O Messenger of God, does it have vegetation? He said: Yes, golden rods. The hypocrite said: I have not heard of anything like today, for rarely does a rod grow except that it has leaves and otherwise it has fruit. The Ansari said: O Messenger of God, does it have fruit? He said: Yes, the colors of pearls, and its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Whoever drinks from it will never thirst again, and whoever is deprived of it will never be satisfied again.” Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Yahya ibn Salamah ibn Kuhail narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-Zura’a, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Then God, the Almighty, will permit intercession, and the Holy Spirit, Gabriel, will rise, then Abraham, the friend of God, will rise, then Jesus or Moses will rise. Abu al-Zura’a said: I do not know which one. He said: Then your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, will rise as a fourth and intercede, and no one will intercede after him more than he interceded. This is the praised station of which God, the Almighty, said: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station. Hadith of Kaab bin Malik, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Abd Rabbah told us, Muhammad bin Harb told us, Al-Zubaidi told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik, on the authority of Kaab bin Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “People will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, and I and my nation will be on a hill, and my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, will clothe me in a green garment, then I will be given permission to say whatever God wills me to say, and that will be the praised station.” Hadith of Abu Darda, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Yazid ibn Abi Habib told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I will be the first to be permitted to prostrate on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to be permitted to raise my head. I will look at what is in front of me and recognize my nation from among the nations, and behind me the same, and to my right the same, and to my left the same. A man said: O Messenger of God, how will you recognize your nation from among the nations between Noah and your nation? He said: They are radiant and have white foreheads from the traces of ablution, and no one is like that except them. I will recognize them because they will be given their books in their right hands, and I will recognize them because their offspring will run before them.” Hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, Abu Hayyan told us, Abu Zur’ah bin Amr bin Jarir told us on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought meat, and the arm was raised to him, and he liked it, so he took a bite of it, then he said: I am the master of people on the Day of Resurrection, and do you know why that is? God will gather the first and the last on one plain, and they will hear the caller, and their sight will penetrate, and the sun will draw near, and there will be an anger and distress that they will not be able to bear, and some of the people will say to others: Do you not see what you are in, and what has befallen you, will you not look for someone who will intercede for you with your Lord? Some of the people will say to others: Go to Adam, so they will go to Adam, peace be upon him, and say: O Adam, you are the father of mankind, God created you with His hand and breathed into you from His spirit, and commanded the angels to prostrate to you, so intercede for us with your Lord, do you not see what we are in, do you not see what has befallen us? Adam will say: My Lord has become angry today with an anger that has not been known to me.” He was angry like him before and will never be angry like him again. He forbade me from the tree and I disobeyed. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Noah. So they go to Noah and say: O Noah, you are the first of the messengers to the people of the earth, and God has named you a grateful servant. Intercede for us with your Lord. Don’t you see what we are in? Don’t you see what has befallen us? Noah says: My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry like it again. I had a supplication that I supplicated against my al-Nas 114:Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Abraham. So they go to Abraham and say: O Abraham, you are the prophet of God and His friend from the people of the earth. Intercede for us with your Lord. Don’t you see what we are in? Don’t you see what has befallen us? He will say: My Lord has become angry today with an anger the likes of which He has never become angry before, and will never become angry again. Then he will mention his lies: Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Moses. So they will go to Moses, peace be upon him, and say: O Moses, you are the Messenger of God, God chose you with His messages and His speech to the people. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? So Moses will say to them: My Lord has become angry with an anger the likes of which He has never become angry before, and will never become angry again. I have killed a soul I was not commanded to kill. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Jesus. So they will go to Jesus and say: O Jesus, you are the Messenger of God and His Word which He cast into Mary and a spirit from Him, and you spoke to the people in the cradle as a child. So intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? Jesus will say to them: My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of which He has never been after. He has not mentioned a sin. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So they will come to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: O Muhammad, you are the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets, and God has forgiven you your past and future sins. So intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? Then I stand up and come under the Throne, and fall prostrating to my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime. Then God opens up to me and inspires me with His praise and good commendation of Him, as He has not opened up to anyone before me. Then it is said: O Muhammad, raise your head and ask and it will be given to you, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. So I raise my head and say: My nation, O Lord, my nation, O Lord. Then it is said: O Muhammad, let in from your nation those who will not be held accountable through the right door of the gates of Paradise, and they will be partners with the people in what is other than that of the gates. Then he said: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, the distance between the two leaflets of Paradise is like the distance between Mecca and Hajar, or like the distance between Mecca and Busra. Narrated by both of them in the Sahihs. Muslim may God have mercy on him said: Al-Hakam bin Musa told us, Aql bin Ziyad told us on the authority of Al-Awza’i, Abu Ammar told me, Abdullah bin Farukh told me, Abu Hurairah told me: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and the first from whom the grave will split on the Day of Resurrection, and the first intercessor and the first whose intercession will be accepted.’” Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Waki’ told us on the authority of Dawud bin Yazid Al-Za’afari on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.’ He was asked about it and he said: ‘It is intercession.’” Narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Waki’ and Muhammad bin Ubaid on the authority of Dawud on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) regarding the words of God the Almighty: ‘Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.’ He said: ‘It is the station in which I will intercede for my nation.’” Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will spread out the earth like a leather cover until there will be nothing for a human being except the space for his feet. ’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Then I will be the first to be called, and Gabriel will be on the right of the Most Gracious, Blessed and Exalted, and by God, he had never seen him before. ’ So I will say: ‘O Lord, this one informed me that You sent him to me. ’ God Almighty will say: ‘He has spoken the truth. ’ Then I will intercede and say: ‘O Lord, Your servants worshipped You at the ends of the earth. ’ He said: ‘Then it is the Praised Station. ’” This is a mursal hadith.
17:79: The Blessed and Exalted says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanding him to perform the prescribed prayers at their appointed times: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun. It was said at its setting, as Ibn Masoud, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd said. Hisham said on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Its decline is its disappearance. Nafi’ narrated it on the authority of Ibn Umar, and Malik narrated it in his interpretation on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ibn Umar, and Abu Barzah Al-Aslami said it, and it is also a narration on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud and Mujahid, and Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Ja’far Al-Baqir, and Qatadah said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Among the evidence for this is what he narrated on the authority of Ibn Hamid on the authority of Al-Hakam Ibn Bashir: Amr Ibn Qays told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla on the authority of a man on the authority of Jabir Ibn Abdullah who said: “I invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and whoever of his companions wanted to eat with me, then they went out when the sun declined, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and said: Go out, O Abu Bakr, for this is when the sun has declined.” Then he narrated it on the authority of Sahl Ibn Bakkar on the authority of Abu Awanah on the authority of Al-Aswad Ibn Qays, on the authority of Nabih Al-Anzi on the authority of Jabir on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Based on this, this verse includes the times of the five prayers, so from His saying: The decline of the sun until dusk... Night, which is its darkness, and it was said that it is sunset, from which noon, afternoon, sunset, and evening were taken. His saying: And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn means the dawn prayer. The Sunnah has explained the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a continuous chain of transmission of his actions and sayings, with details of these times, as the people of Islam do today, from what they received from their predecessors and generation after generation, as is established in its places, and praise be to God. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Ibrahim on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, and on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this verse: “And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed.” He said: It is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The superiority of the prayer of a group over the prayer of one person is twenty-five degrees, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the dawn prayer. Abu Hurairah said: Recite if you wish, “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed.” Imam Ahmad said: Asbat told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed,” he said: It is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah, all three of them on the authority of Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad on the authority of his father, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic. In a wording in the two Sahihs on the authority of Malik on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad on the authority of Al-A’raj on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Angels take turns among you by night and angels by day, and they gather at the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. Then those who spent the night among you ascend and their Lord asks them - and He is most knowing of you - how did you leave My servants? They say: We came to them while they were praying, and we left them while they were praying.” Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: The two guards gather at the dawn prayer, so some ascend and those stand. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Mujahid, Qatadah and more than one said the same in their interpretation of this verse. As for the hadith that Ibn Jarir narrated here from the hadith of Al-Layth bin Saad, on the authority of Ziyadah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Fadala bin Ubaid, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he mentioned the hadith of the descent, and that God Almighty says: Whoever seeks My forgiveness, I will forgive him. Whoever asks Me, I will give him. Whoever calls upon Me, I will answer him until dawn comes, so that is why He says: “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed,” so God, the angels of the night, and the angels of the day witness it, and Ziyadah is the only one who narrated it, and he has a hadith about this in Sunan Abi Dawud. God the Almighty said: And during part of the night, then pray with it as an additional prayer for you. This is a command for him to perform the night prayer after the obligatory prayer, as was reported in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was asked which prayer is best after the obligatory prayer? He said, The night prayer. For this reason God the Almighty commanded His Messenger to perform the night prayer after the obligatory prayers, because the night prayer is what is done after sleeping. This was said by Alqamah, Al-Aswad, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and others, and it is well-known in the language of the Arabs. Likewise, the hadiths were confirmed on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to perform the night prayer after sleeping, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Aisha and others from the Companions, may God be pleased with them, as is explained in detail in its place. Praise and thanks be to God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: It is what comes after the evening prayer and it is interpreted as what comes after sleep. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of the Almighty’s statement: A voluntary prayer for you. It was said that it means that you are the only one who is obligated to do that, so they made the night prayer obligatory for him and not for the nation. Al-Awfi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is one of the two opinions of the scholars, and one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, and Ibn Jarir chose it. It was said: The night prayer was made a voluntary prayer for him in particular, because his past and future sins have been forgiven, and for others from his nation, only his voluntary prayers expiate the sins that he has committed. Mujahid said it: And it is in Al-Musnad on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Bahili, may God be pleased with him. And His statement: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station, meaning, do what I have commanded you to do so that We may establish you on the Day of Resurrection in a praised station, where all of creation and their Creator, Blessed and Exalted be He, will praise you. Ibn Jarir said: Most of the people of interpretation said: That is the station that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will stand on the Day of Resurrection to intercede for the people so that their Lord may relieve them of the great hardship they will be in on that Day. Mention who said that Ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Silah ibn Zafar, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: The people will be gathered on one plain, the caller will hear them and their sight will penetrate them, barefoot and naked as they were created, standing, no soul will speak except with His permission. He will call out: O Muhammad, and he will say: “At your service and at your pleasure, and good is in your hands and evil is not from you, and the Mahdi is he whom you have guided, and your servant is before you, and from you and to you there is no escape or refuge from you except to you, blessed and exalted are you, glory be to you, Lord of the House.” This is the praised station that God the Almighty mentioned. Then he narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ghundar, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, and Abd al-Razzaq narrated it likewise on the authority of Muammar and al-Thawri, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, and Ibn Abbas said: This praised station is the station of intercession, and Ibn Abi Nujayh said the same on the authority of Mujahid, and al-Hasan al-Basri said the same. Qatada said: He is the first from whom the earth will split open on the Day of Resurrection and the first intercessor. The people of knowledge used to consider him to be the praised station of which God Almighty said: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station. I said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about honors on the Day of Resurrection that no one will share with him, and honors that no one will equal him in. He is the first from whom the earth will split open and he will be sent riding to the place of assembly. He has the banner under which Adam and those after him were under its banner. He has the pool from which there is no one more likely to come to the place of assembly. He has the greatest intercession with God to come to decide the judgment between the creation.
