This will happen after people ask Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, and each one says: I am not up for it, until they come to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he says: I am up for it, I am up for it, as we will mention in detail in this place, God willing. Among these is that he intercedes for people who have been ordered to Hell, so that they may be returned from it. He is the first of the prophets to judge between his nation, and the first of them to cross the Sirat with his nation. He is the first intercessor in Paradise, as proven in Sahih Muslim. In the hadith of the images, it is stated that all believers will not enter Paradise except through his intercession, and he will be the first to enter it, and his nation will precede all nations, and he will intercede to raise the ranks of people whose deeds cannot reach it, and he is the possessor of the means which is the highest station in Paradise that is only befitting of him, and if God Almighty permits intercession for the sinners, the angels, prophets and believers will intercede, and he will intercede for people whose number is known only to God Almighty, and no one intercedes like him or is equal to him in that, and I have explained that in detail at the end of the Book of Seerah in the chapter on characteristics, and praise and thanks be to God, and now let us mention the hadiths that were reported about the praised station and with God is the helper. Al-Bukhari said: Ismail bin Abaan told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us on the authority of Adam bin Ali, I heard Ibn Umar say: “On the Day of Resurrection, people will become like knees, every nation that follows its prophet will say: O so-and-so, intercede, O so-and-so, intercede, until intercession ends with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that is the day when God will raise him to a praised station.” It was narrated by Hamza bin Abdullah on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me, Shuaib ibn Al-Layth told us, Al-Layth told us on the authority of Ubaidullah ibn Abi Ja`far, that he said: I heard Hamza ibn Abdullah ibn Umar say: I heard Abdullah ibn Umar say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The sun draws near until the sweat reaches half of the ear. While they are like that, they will seek help from Adam, but he will say: ‘I am not the one to do that.’ Then from Moses, and he will say the same. Then from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he will intercede among the creation and walk until he takes hold of the ring of the door of Paradise. On that day, God will raise him to a praiseworthy station.’” And this is how Al-Bukhari narrated it in Zakat on the authority of Yahya ibn Bakir and Alqamah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salih, both on the authority of Al-Layth ibn Sa`d, with the same chain of transmission, and he added: On that day, God will raise him to a praiseworthy station, and all the people of the assembly will praise him. Al-Bukhari said: Ali bin Ayyash told us, Shuaib bin Abi Hamza told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says when he hears the call: O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, grant Muhammad the means and the excellence, and raise him to the praised station which You promised him, my intercession will be permissible for him on the Day of Resurrection.” It was transmitted by him alone, not by Muslim. Hadith of Abi bin Kaab Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir Al-Azdi told us, Zuhair bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel, on the authority of Al-Tufayl bin Abi Kaab, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, I will be the leader of the prophets and their orator and the one who will intercede for them, without boasting. Al-Tirmidhi included it on the authority of Abu Amir Abdul Malik bin Amr Al-Aqdi, and he said: It is good and authentic, and Ibn Majah included it on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel with it. We have already mentioned in the hadith of Abi bin Kaab about reciting the Qur’an in seven letters, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said at the end of it: “So I said: O God, forgive my nation, O God, forgive my nation, and I delayed the third for a day when the creation will yearn for me, even Abraham, peace be upon him.” Hadith of Anas bin Malik Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, Saeed bin Abi Arooba told us, Qatada told us on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The believers will gather on the Day of Resurrection and be inspired by that, and they will say: If only we could intercede with our Lord so that He might relieve us from this place of ours. So they will go to Adam and say: O Adam, you are the father of mankind, God created you with His hand, and His angels prostrated to you, and He taught you the names of everything, so intercede for us with your Lord so that He might relieve us from this place of ours. So Adam will say to them: I am not there for you, and he will mention the sin he committed, and his Lord, the Almighty, will feel ashamed of that, and he will say: But go to Noah, for he was the first Messenger whom God sent to the people of the earth. So they will go to Noah, and he will say: I am not there for you, and he will mention the sin of asking his Lord for something of which he had no knowledge, and his Lord will feel ashamed of that, and he will say: But go to Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful. So they will go to him and he will say: I am not there for you, but go to Moses, a servant to whom God spoke and gave.” The Torah, and they come to Moses, and he says: I am not there with you, and he mentions to them the soul that was killed without a soul, and his Lord is ashamed of that, and says: But go to Jesus, the servant of God and His Messenger and His Word and His Spirit, so they come to Jesus, and he says: I am not there with you, but go to Muhammad, a servant whom God has forgiven his past and future sins, so they come to me - Al-Hasan said this wording - so I stand and walk between two rows of believers - Anas said - until I ask permission to see my Lord, and when I see my Lord, I fall down - or prostrate - to my Lord, and He leaves me as long as God wills that He leaves me - he said - then it is said: Raise Muhammad, say He hears, and intercede and your intercession will be granted, and ask and it will be given to you, so I raise my head and praise Him with praise that He teaches me, then I intercede and He sets a limit for me and I admit them to Paradise, he said: Then I return to Him a second time, and when I see my Lord, I fall down or prostrate to my Lord, and He leaves me as long as God wills that He leaves me, then it is said: Raise Muhammad, say He hears, and ask and it will be given to you Then I will come back a third time and when I see my Lord, I will fall down in prostration to my Lord and He will leave me as long as God wills me to leave. Then it will be said: Raise Muhammad, say and He hears, and ask and He will give you, and intercede and He will intercede. So I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise that He teaches me, then I will intercede and He will set a limit for me and I will enter them into Paradise. Then I will come back a fourth time and say: O Lord, there remains only those whom the Qur’an has detained.” Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then he who says, ‘There is no god but God’ and in his heart there is goodness equal to the weight of a barley seed will come out of the Fire. Then he who says, ‘There is no god but God’ and in his heart there is goodness equal to the weight of a grain of wheat will come out of the Fire. Then he who says, ‘There is no god but God’ and in his heart there is goodness equal to the weight of an atom will come out of the Fire.” They both reported it from the hadith of Sa’id with it. Imam Ahmad narrated it in this way from ‘Affan ibn Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas is tall. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus bin Muhammad narrated to us, Harb bin Maymun Abu Al-Khattab Al-Ansari narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Anas, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated to me, saying: “I am standing, waiting for my nation to cross the bridge, when Jesus, peace be upon him, came to me and said: These prophets have come to you, O Muhammad, asking - or he said: they are gathering to you - and calling upon God to separate all the nations to whatever God wills for the misery they are in. The creation is bridled with sweat. As for the believer, it is like a cold upon him, and as for the disbeliever, death will overtake him. He said: Wait until I return to you. So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went and stood beneath the Throne, and he encountered what no chosen angel or sent prophet has encountered. So God, the Almighty, inspired Gabriel to go to Muhammad and say to him: Raise your head, ask and you will be given, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. So I interceded for my nation, that one person from every ninety-nine should come out. I have not ceased to go back to my Lord, the Almighty, and I do not stand in a place except that I I interceded until God Almighty gave me, including that he said: O Muhammad, include from your nation those of God Almighty’s creation who testified that there is no god but God for one day sincerely and died upon that. Hadith of Buraidah, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Al-Aswad ibn Aamer told us, Abu Israel told us, on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Hasira, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, that he entered upon Muawiyah, and there was a man speaking, so Buraidah said: O Muawiyah, will you permit me to speak? He said: Yes, and he thought that he would say the same as the other one, so Buraidah said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “I hope that I will intercede on the Day of Resurrection as many times as there are trees and mud on the earth.” He said: So you hope for it, O Muawiyah, but Ali, may God be pleased with him, does not hope for it. Hadith of Ibn Masoud - Imam Ahmad said: Arim bin Al-Fadl narrated to us, Saeed bin Al-Fadl narrated to us, Saeed bin Zaid narrated to us, Ali bin Al-Hakam Al-Banani narrated to us, on the authority of Uthman, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah and Al-Aswad, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: “The two sons of Mulaykah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Our mother honors her husband and is kind to her child. He said: They mentioned the guest, but she was buried alive in the pre-Islamic era. He said: Your mother is in Hellfire. He said: So they turned away, and evil was evident on their faces. He ordered them to be returned, and they returned, and joy was evident on their faces, hoping that something had happened. He said: My mother is with your mother. A hypocrite said: What does this man do for his mother, and we are treading on his heels? A man from the Ansar said: I have never seen a man ask more than him, O Messenger of God. Did your Lord promise you about her or both of them? He said: He thought that it was from something he had heard, so he said: I did not ask my Lord, nor did He give me hope for it. I will stand in the praised station on the Day of Resurrection.” The Ansari said: O Messenger of God, what is that praiseworthy station? He said: That is when you are brought barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, and the first to be clothed will be Abraham, peace be upon him, and he will say: Clothe my friend. Then he will be brought two white robes and he will put them on him, then he will make him sit facing the Throne, then my clothing will be brought and I will put it on him, and I will stand on his right in a position that no one will stand on, and the first and the last will envy me for it. He said: And an opening will be made for them from Al-Kawthar to the Pool. The hypocrite said: Water has never flowed except in a state or in a place of dirt. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its state is musk and its dirt is pearls. The hypocrite said: I have not heard of anything like today, for rarely does water flow in a state or in a place of dirt except that it has vegetation. The Ansari said: O Messenger of God, does it have vegetation? He said: Yes, golden rods. The hypocrite said: I have not heard of anything like today, for rarely does a rod grow except that it has leaves and otherwise it has fruit. The Ansari said: O Messenger of God, does it have fruit? He said: Yes, the colors of pearls, and its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Whoever drinks from it will never thirst again, and whoever is deprived of it will never be satisfied again.” Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Yahya ibn Salamah ibn Kuhail narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-Zura’a, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Then God, the Almighty, will permit intercession, and the Holy Spirit, Gabriel, will rise, then Abraham, the friend of God, will rise, then Jesus or Moses will rise. Abu al-Zura’a said: I do not know which one. He said: Then your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, will rise as a fourth and intercede, and no one will intercede after him more than he interceded. This is the praised station of which God, the Almighty, said: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station. Hadith of Kaab bin Malik, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Abd Rabbah told us, Muhammad bin Harb told us, Al-Zubaidi told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik, on the authority of Kaab bin Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “People will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, and I and my nation will be on a hill, and my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, will clothe me in a green garment, then I will be given permission to say whatever God wills me to say, and that will be the praised station.” Hadith of Abu Darda, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Yazid ibn Abi Habib told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I will be the first to be permitted to prostrate on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to be permitted to raise my head. I will look at what is in front of me and recognize my nation from among the nations, and behind me the same, and to my right the same, and to my left the same. A man said: O Messenger of God, how will you recognize your nation from among the nations between Noah and your nation? He said: They are radiant and have white foreheads from the traces of ablution, and no one is like that except them. I will recognize them because they will be given their books in their right hands, and I will recognize them because their offspring will run before them.” Hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, Abu Hayyan told us, Abu Zur’ah bin Amr bin Jarir told us on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought meat, and the arm was raised to him, and he liked it, so he took a bite of it, then he said: I am the master of people on the Day of Resurrection, and do you know why that is? God will gather the first and the last on one plain, and they will hear the caller, and their sight will penetrate, and the sun will draw near, and there will be an anger and distress that they will not be able to bear, and some of the people will say to others: Do you not see what you are in, and what has befallen you, will you not look for someone who will intercede for you with your Lord? Some of the people will say to others: Go to Adam, so they will go to Adam, peace be upon him, and say: O Adam, you are the father of mankind, God created you with His hand and breathed into you from His spirit, and commanded the angels to prostrate to you, so intercede for us with your Lord, do you not see what we are in, do you not see what has befallen us? Adam will say: My Lord has become angry today with an anger that has not been known to me.” He was angry like him before and will never be angry like him again. He forbade me from the tree and I disobeyed. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Noah. So they go to Noah and say: O Noah, you are the first of the messengers to the people of the earth, and God has named you a grateful servant. Intercede for us with your Lord. Don’t you see what we are in? Don’t you see what has befallen us? Noah says: My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry like it again. I had a supplication that I supplicated against my al-Nas 114:Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Abraham. So they go to Abraham and say: O Abraham, you are the prophet of God and His friend from the people of the earth. Intercede for us with your Lord. Don’t you see what we are in? Don’t you see what has befallen us? He will say: My Lord has become angry today with an anger the likes of which He has never become angry before, and will never become angry again. Then he will mention his lies: Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Moses. So they will go to Moses, peace be upon him, and say: O Moses, you are the Messenger of God, God chose you with His messages and His speech to the people. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? So Moses will say to them: My Lord has become angry with an anger the likes of which He has never become angry before, and will never become angry again. I have killed a soul I was not commanded to kill. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Jesus. So they will go to Jesus and say: O Jesus, you are the Messenger of God and His Word which He cast into Mary and a spirit from Him, and you spoke to the people in the cradle as a child. So intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? Jesus will say to them: My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of which He has never been after. He has not mentioned a sin. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So they will come to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: O Muhammad, you are the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets, and God has forgiven you your past and future sins. So intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? Then I stand up and come under the Throne, and fall prostrating to my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime. Then God opens up to me and inspires me with His praise and good commendation of Him, as He has not opened up to anyone before me. Then it is said: O Muhammad, raise your head and ask and it will be given to you, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. So I raise my head and say: My nation, O Lord, my nation, O Lord. Then it is said: O Muhammad, let in from your nation those who will not be held accountable through the right door of the gates of Paradise, and they will be partners with the people in what is other than that of the gates. Then he said: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, the distance between the two leaflets of Paradise is like the distance between Mecca and Hajar, or like the distance between Mecca and Busra. Narrated by both of them in the Sahihs. Muslim may God have mercy on him said: Al-Hakam bin Musa told us, Aql bin Ziyad told us on the authority of Al-Awza’i, Abu Ammar told me, Abdullah bin Farukh told me, Abu Hurairah told me: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and the first from whom the grave will split on the Day of Resurrection, and the first intercessor and the first whose intercession will be accepted.’” Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Waki’ told us on the authority of Dawud bin Yazid Al-Za’afari on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.’ He was asked about it and he said: ‘It is intercession.’” Narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Waki’ and Muhammad bin Ubaid on the authority of Dawud on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) regarding the words of God the Almighty: ‘Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.’ He said: ‘It is the station in which I will intercede for my nation.’” Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will spread out the earth like a leather cover until there will be nothing for a human being except the space for his feet. ’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Then I will be the first to be called, and Gabriel will be on the right of the Most Gracious, Blessed and Exalted, and by God, he had never seen him before. ’ So I will say: ‘O Lord, this one informed me that You sent him to me. ’ God Almighty will say: ‘He has spoken the truth. ’ Then I will intercede and say: ‘O Lord, Your servants worshipped You at the ends of the earth. ’ He said: ‘Then it is the Praised Station. ’” This is a mursal hadith.
17:80: Imam Ahmad said: Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Qabus bin Abi Thabyan on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca, then he was commanded to emigrate, so God revealed: And say, ‘My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and let me exit a truthful exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.’ Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said in his interpretation of this verse: When the infidels of Mecca conspired against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill him, expel him, or tie him up, God wanted to fight the people of Mecca, so He commanded him to go out to Medina, so he is the one about whom God Almighty said: And say, ‘My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and let me exit a truthful exit.’ Qatada said: “And say: My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance,” meaning Medina, and let me exit a truthful exit, meaning Mecca. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said the same, and this is the most famous statement. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Let me enter a truthful entrance, meaning death, and let me exit a truthful exit, meaning life after death. Other statements were said, but the first is more correct, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir. And His saying, "And grant me from Yourself a supporting authority." Al-Hasan Al-Basri said in its interpretation: His Lord promised him that He would take away the kingdom of Persia and the glory of Persia and give it to him, and the kingdom of Rome and the glory of Rome and give it to him. Qatada said about it: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew that he would not be able to do this without an authority, so he asked for an authority to support the Book of God, the limits of God, the obligations of God, and the establishment of the religion of God, for the authority is a mercy from God that He has placed among His servants, and were it not for that, some of them would raid others and the strong among them would eat the weak. Mujahid said, "A supporting authority" is a clear argument, and Ibn Jarir chose the saying of Al-Hasan and Qatada, and it is the most likely because with the truth there must be subjugation of those who oppose and oppose it, and for this reason God Almighty says: "Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that people may maintain justice. And We sent down iron" (10:10). In the hadith, God restrains with the ruler what He does not restrain with the Qur’an, meaning that He prevents with the ruler from committing indecencies and sins what many people do not refrain from with the Qur’an and what it contains of certain warnings and severe intimidation, and this is the reality. And His saying: And say, ‘The truth has come, and falsehood has perished’ 2:10, is a threat and warning to the infidels of Quraysh, for the truth has come to them from God, about which there is no doubt and which they cannot accept, and it is what God sent him with of the Qur’an, faith, and beneficial knowledge. And their falsehood has perished, that is, it has vanished and perished, for falsehood has no stability or permanence with the truth. Rather, We cast the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it, and at once it departs. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered Mecca and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols. He began to stab them with a stick in his hand and say: “The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Falsehood is bound to vanish. The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates nor restores.” Al-Bukhari also narrated it in this way in a place other than this, and Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i all narrated it through chains of transmission on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah on his authority. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated it in this way on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on his authority. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Zuhair told us, Shababah told us, Al-Mughirah told us, Abu Al-Zubayr told us on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: We entered Mecca with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols that were worshipped instead of God. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to be thrown down on their faces, and he said: “Falsehood has come and vanished. Falsehood is bound to vanish.”
17:81: Imam Ahmad said: Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Qabus bin Abi Thabyan on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca, then he was commanded to emigrate, so God revealed: And say, ‘My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and let me exit a truthful exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.’ Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said in his interpretation of this verse: When the infidels of Mecca conspired against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill him, expel him, or tie him up, God wanted to fight the people of Mecca, so He commanded him to go out to Medina, so he is the one about whom God Almighty said: And say, ‘My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and let me exit a truthful exit.’ Qatada said: “And say: My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance,” meaning Medina, and let me exit a truthful exit, meaning Mecca. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said the same, and this is the most famous statement. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Let me enter a truthful entrance, meaning death, and let me exit a truthful exit, meaning life after death. Other statements were said, but the first is more correct, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir. And His saying, And grant me from Yourself a supporting authority. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said in its interpretation: His Lord promised him that He would take away the kingdom of Persia and the glory of Persia and give it to him, and the kingdom of Rome and the glory of Rome and give it to him. Qatada said about it: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew that he would not be able to do this without an authority, so he asked for an authority to support the Book of God, the limits of God, the obligations of God, and the establishment of the religion of God, for the authority is a mercy from God that He has placed among His servants, and were it not for that, some of them would raid others and the strong among them would eat the weak. Mujahid said, A supporting authority is a clear argument, and Ibn Jarir chose the saying of Al-Hasan and Qatada, and it is the most likely because with the truth there must be subjugation of those who oppose and oppose it, and for this reason God Almighty says: "Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that people may maintain justice. And We sent down iron" (10:10). In the hadith, God restrains with the ruler what He does not restrain with the Qur’an, meaning that He prevents with the ruler from committing indecencies and sins what many people do not refrain from with the Qur’an and what it contains of certain warnings and severe intimidation, and this is the reality. And His saying: And say, ‘The truth has come, and falsehood has perished’ 2:10, is a threat and warning to the infidels of Quraysh, for the truth has come to them from God, about which there is no doubt and which they cannot accept, and it is what God sent him with of the Qur’an, faith, and beneficial knowledge. And their falsehood has perished, that is, it has vanished and perished, for falsehood has no stability or permanence with the truth. Rather, We cast the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it, and at once it departs. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered Mecca and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols. He began to stab them with a stick in his hand and say: “The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Falsehood is bound to vanish. The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates nor restores.” Al-Bukhari also narrated it in this way in a place other than this, and Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i all narrated it through chains of transmission on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah on his authority. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated it in this way on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on his authority. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Zuhair told us, Shababah told us, Al-Mughirah told us, Abu Al-Zubayr told us on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: We entered Mecca with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols that were worshipped instead of God. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to be thrown down on their faces, and he said: “Falsehood has come and vanished. Falsehood is bound to vanish.”
17:82: The Almighty says, informing about His Book that was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is the Qur’an, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it, sent down by One Who is Wise, Praiseworthy, that it is a cure and a mercy for the believers, meaning it removes from the heart diseases of doubt, hypocrisy, polytheism, deviation and inclination, so the Qur’an heals from all of that, and it is also a mercy in which faith, wisdom, seeking goodness and desiring it are obtained, and this is only for the one who believes in it, believes in it and follows it, for it is a cure and a mercy for him, and as for the unbeliever who wrongs himself with that, then hearing the Qur’an only increases his distance and disbelief, and the affliction is from the unbeliever, not from the Qur’an, as God the Almighty says: “Say, ‘It is, for those who believe, a guide and a cure. But those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.’” And God the Almighty says: “And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’ As for those who believe, it increases them in faith, and they rejoice. * And as for those who are in Their hearts are diseased, so it increased their filth upon their filth, and they died while they were disbelievers. There are many verses on this subject. Qatada said about His statement, “And We send down of the Qur’an that which is healing and mercy for the believers,” that if a believer hears it, he benefits from it, memorizes it, and comprehends it. But it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss, that is, he does not benefit from it, memorize it, or comprehend it. Indeed, God made this Qur’an a healing and mercy for the believers.
17:83: God the Almighty tells us about the deficiency of man as he is, except for those whom God the Almighty protects in both good and bad times. If God bestows upon him wealth, health, victory, provision and support, and he attains what he wants, he turns away from obeying God and worshipping Him and distances himself from Him. Mujahid said: He turned away from Us. I said: This is like the words of God the Almighty: But when We removed his distress from him, he passed on as if he had never called upon Us to deal with a distress that had befallen him and His words: But when He delivered you to land, you turned away and that if evil befalls him, which is calamities, accidents and misfortunes, he is despairing meaning he despairs of returning and obtaining any good after that, like the words of God the Almighty: "And if We let man taste mercy from Us and then take it away from him, he is indeed despairing, ungrateful. * But if We let him taste favor after an adversity has befallen him, he will surely say, "The bad things have departed from me." Indeed, he is exultant and boastful. * Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds. For those is forgiveness and a great reward." God the Almighty said: Say, ‘Each one works according to his nature.’ Ibn Abbas said: According to his own way. Mujahid said: According to his own nature and individuality. Qatada said: According to his intention. Ibn Zayd said: His religion. All of these sayings are close in meaning. This verse - and God knows best - is a threat and warning to the polytheists, like God the Almighty’s saying: And say to those who do not believe, ‘Work according to your position.’ That is why He said: “Say, ‘Each one works according to his nature. But your Lord is most knowing of who is best guided in way.’” That is, than us and you. And He will reward each worker for his work, for nothing is hidden from Him.
17:84: God the Almighty tells us about the deficiency of man as he is, except for those whom God the Almighty protects in both good and bad times. If God bestows upon him wealth, health, victory, provision and support, and he attains what he wants, he turns away from obeying God and worshipping Him and distances himself from Him. Mujahid said: He turned away from Us. I said: This is like the words of God the Almighty: But when We removed his distress from him, he passed on as if he had never called upon Us to deal with a distress that had befallen him and His words: But when He delivered you to land, you turned away and that if evil befalls him, which is calamities, accidents and misfortunes, he is despairing meaning he despairs of returning and obtaining any good after that, like the words of God the Almighty: "And if We let man taste mercy from Us and then take it away from him, he is indeed despairing, ungrateful. * But if We let him taste favor after an adversity has befallen him, he will surely say, "The bad things have departed from me." 17:85: Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee', we were told by Al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: "I was walking with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a field in Madinah, and he was leaning on a palm branch. He passed by some Jews, and some of them said to each other: Ask him about the spirit, and some of them said: Do not ask him. He said: So they asked him about the spirit, and they said: O Muhammad, what is the spirit? He kept leaning on the palm branch. He said: I thought that revelation was being sent to him, and he said: "And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little." He said: So some of them said to each other: We told you not to ask him." And this is how Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Al-A'mash. Al-Bukhari’s wording in his interpretation of this verse is on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: “While I was walking with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a field, and he was leaning on a palm branch, the Jews passed by and some of them said to each other: Ask him about the spirit. He said: What is it that makes you angry about him? And some of them said: Do not let him meet you with something that you dislike. They said: Ask him. So they asked him about the spirit, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, held back and did not answer them anything. I knew that revelation was being sent to him, so I stood still. When the revelation came down, he said: ‘And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord’” the verse. This context indicates, as it appears at first glance, that this verse is Medinan, and that it was revealed when the Jews asked him about it in Medina, even though the entire surah is Meccan. The answer to this may be that it may have been revealed to him in Medina a second time, as it was revealed to him in Mecca before that, or the revelation came to him to answer what they asked him with the verse that was revealed to him before, which is this verse: And they ask you about the spirit. What indicates that this verse was revealed in Mecca is what Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah told us, Yahya bin Zakariya told us on the authority of Dawud on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Quraysh said to the Jews: Give us something to ask this man about, so they said: Ask him about the spirit, so they asked him, and then it was revealed: “And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord. And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.” They said: We have been given much knowledge, we have been given the Torah, and whoever has been given the Torah has been given much good. He said: And God revealed: “Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted.” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The People of the Book asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the spirit, so God revealed the verse, And they ask you about the spirit, and they said: You claim that we have been given only a little knowledge, while we have been given the Torah, which is wisdom, And whoever has been given wisdom has certainly been given much good, he said: So the verse was revealed, And if all the trees on the earth were pens and the sea were pens, and seven more seas were to replenish it, he said: Whatever knowledge you have been given, and God has saved you with it from the Fire, it is abundant and good, but in comparison to God’s knowledge it is little. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, who said: And of knowledge you have been given only a little was revealed in Mecca. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, the Jewish rabbis came to him and said: O Muhammad, have we not heard that you say, ‘And of knowledge you have been given only a little’? Did you mean us or your people? He said: No, I mean it. They said: “You recite, ‘We have been given the Torah, and in it is clarification of everything.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “It is little in the knowledge of God, and God has given you that which, if you act upon it, you will benefit.” And God revealed: “And if all the trees on the earth were pens and the sea, with seven more seas to replenish it, were ink, the Words of God would not be exhausted. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise.” The commentators differed about what is meant by the spirit here, with some sayings one of which is that what is meant are the spirits of the sons of Adam. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And they ask you about the spirit the verse, that the Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Tell us about the spirit and how the spirit in the body is tormented, but the spirit is from God and nothing was revealed to him about it, so he did not tell them anything, so Gabriel came to him and said to him: “Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little.” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them of that, and they said: Who brought you this? He said: Gabriel brought it to me from God, so they said to him: By God, none told you that except our enemy,” so God revealed: “Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - for he has brought it down upon your heart by God’s permission, confirming what was before it.” It was said: What is meant by the spirit here is Gabriel, and Qatada said: Ibn Abbas concealed it, and it was said that what is meant by it here is a great angel as great as all creatures. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And they ask you about the spirit, meaning: The spirit is an angel. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Aras Al-Masry told us, Wahb bin Rawq bin Hubaira told us, Bishr bin Bakr told us, Al-Awza’i told us, Ata’ told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God has an angel. If he were told to swallow the seven heavens and the earths in one bite, he would do so. His glorification is: Glory be to You wherever you are.” This is a strange hadith, rather it is rejected. Abu Ja`far bin Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Ali told me, Abdullah told me, Abu Marwan Yazid bin Samra, the master of Caesarea, told me, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said regarding His statement: And they ask you about the spirit, he said: It is an angel from the angels who has seventy thousand faces, each face has seventy thousand tongues, each tongue has seventy thousand languages. He glorifies God Almighty in all of those languages, and God creates from every glorification an angel who flies with the angels until the Day of Resurrection. This is a strange and amazing trace, and God knows best. Al-Suhayli said: It was narrated on the authority of Ali that he said: He is an angel with one hundred thousand heads, each head has one hundred thousand faces, in each face one hundred thousand mouths, in each mouth one hundred thousand tongues, glorifying God Almighty in different languages. Al-Suhayli said: It was said that what is meant by this is a group of angels in the form of the sons of Adam, and it was said: A group who see the angels but they do not see them, so they are to the angels as the angels are to the sons of Adam. And His saying: “Say: The spirit is from the affair of my Lord” meaning from His affair and from what He has kept to Himself and not you. That is why He said: And you have not been given of knowledge except a little meaning and He has not informed you of His knowledge except a little, for no one encompasses anything of His knowledge except what He, the Blessed and Most High, wills. The meaning is that your knowledge is little compared to the knowledge of God. What you are asking about is the matter of the spirit from what He, the Most High, has kept to Himself and has not informed you of, just as He has not informed you of except a little of His knowledge, the Most High. And it will come, God willing, in the story of Moses and Al-Khidr that Al-Khidr looked at a bird that had landed on the edge of the ship and pecked at the sea, meaning he drank from it with his beak, so he said: O Moses, my knowledge and your knowledge and the knowledge of creation in comparison to the knowledge of God is only as this bird took from this sea, or as he said, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. That is why God Almighty said: And you have not been given of knowledge except a little. Al-Suhayli said: Some people said that He did not answer them about what they asked, because they asked in a way that was obstinate, and it was said that He answered them. Al-Suhayli relied on the fact that what was meant by his saying: “Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord” is from His law, meaning enter into it and you have known that, because there is no way to know this from nature or philosophy, but rather it is attained from the side of the law, and in this path that he took and followed there is consideration, and God knows best. Then Al-Suhayli mentioned the disagreement among scholars as to whether the soul is the self or something else, and he decided that it is a subtle entity like air, flowing in the body as water flows in the veins of a tree, and he decided that the soul that the angel breathes into the fetus is the self on condition that it is connected to the body and acquires praiseworthy or blameworthy qualities because of it, so it is either a tranquil soul or a soul that commands evil, just as water is the life of the tree and then acquires a special name because of its mixing with it, so if it is connected to the grape and squeezed from it, it becomes either a distilled wine or wine, and it is not called water in that case except by way of metaphor, and likewise the soul is not called a soul except in this way, and likewise the soul is not called a soul except in consideration of what it leads to, so the gist of what we say is that the soul is the origin of the soul and its matter, and the soul is composed of it and of its connection to the body, so it is it in one way but not in every way, and this is a good meaning, and God knows best. I said: People have spoken about the nature of the soul and its rulings, and they have classified books on that, and the best of those who spoke about that is Al-Hafiz Ibn Mandah in a book that we heard about the soul.
17:86: God Almighty mentions His great grace and favor upon His servant and noble Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what He revealed to him of the Glorious Qur’an, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it, a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy. Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him said: A red wind will blow upon the people, meaning at the end of time from the direction of Ash-Sham, and there will not remain in a man’s copy of the Qur’an or in his heart a single verse. Then Ibn Mas`ud recited: And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you Al-Baqarah 2:17. Then God the Almighty pointed out the honor of this great Qur’an, and informed us that if all of mankind and the jinn were to gather and agree to produce something like what was revealed to His Messenger, they would not be able to do so, nor would they be able to do so. Even if they cooperated, helped each other, and joined forces, this is something that cannot be done. How can the speech of the created be similar to the speech of the Creator, who has no equal, no likeness, and no peer? Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr or `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, that this verse was revealed about a group of Jews who came to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and said to him: We will bring you something like what you have brought us. So God revealed this verse. There is a problem with this, because this surah is Meccan and its entire context is with the Quraysh, and the Jews only gathered with him. In the city, God knows best. And His saying, And We have certainly presented to the people the verse, meaning, We have shown them the decisive arguments and proofs, and We have clarified the truth to them and explained it and expanded it, and despite this, most people refused except to be ungrateful, meaning, to deny the truth and reject what is right.

17:90: Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, an old man from Egypt who came forty-some years ago told me on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi’ah, Abu Sufyan bin Harb, a man from Banu Abd al-Dar, Abu al-Bukhtari, the brother of Banu Asad, al-Aswad bin al-Muttalib bin Asad, Zam’ah bin al-Aswad, al-Walid bin al-Mughira, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah, Umayyah bin Khalaf, al-‘As bin Wa’il, Nabih and Munabbih, the sons of al-Hajjaj al-Sahmiyyin, gathered, or whoever gathered from them, after sunset at the back of the Kaaba. Some of them said to each other: Send to Muhammad and speak to him and argue with him until they find an excuse for him. So they sent to him that the nobles of your people have gathered to speak to you. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them quickly, thinking that they had changed their mind about him, and they were on them. He was keen on their guidance and was saddened by their trouble until he sat with them. They said: “O Muhammad, we have been sent to you to excuse you. By God, we do not know of any Arab man who has brought upon his people what you have brought upon your people. You have insulted the fathers, denounced the religion, belittled dreams, insulted the gods, and divided the community. There is no ugly thing that I have not done between us and you. If you have only come with this hadith seeking money, we will collect for you from our money until you are the wealthiest among us. If you are only seeking honor among us, we will make you our leader. If you want a kingdom, we will make you our king. If this one who brings you what he brings you is a vision that you see has overcome you - and they used to call the follower of the jinn the visionary - then perhaps that is what we have spent our money seeking medicine until we cure you of it or excuse you.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I do not have what you say. I have not come to you with what I have come to you seeking your money, nor honor among you, nor kingship over you. Rather, God has sent me to you as a messenger and revealed to me a book and commanded me to be for you.” As a bearer of good tidings and a warner, I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you. Blessed is He who, if He wills, can grant you better than that - gardens beneath which rivers flow and can grant you palaces. Rather, they have denied the Hour, and We have prepared for whoever denies the Hour a Blaze.” And the Almighty’s saying: Until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth. The spring is the flowing eye. They asked Him to cause a flowing eye to gush forth for them in the land of the Hijaz here and there, and that is easy for God, the Almighty. If He had willed, He would have done it and answered them on all that they asked and requested of Him, but He knew that they would not be guided, as the Almighty said: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign came to them until they saw the painful punishment. And the Almighty said: And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We had gathered together before them all things before, they would not have believed. The verse. And the Almighty said: Or the sky will fall as you claimed meaning that you promised us that on the Day of Resurrection the sky will split and fall and its edges will hang down, so make that in this world and make it fall in pieces, i.e. in pieces, like His saying: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky verse. And likewise the people of Shu’ayb asked Him and said: Let a piece of the sky fall upon us, if you are of the truthful. So God punished them with the punishment of the Day of the Shadow, for it was the punishment of a great day. As for the Prophet of Mercy and the Prophet of Repentance, who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, he asked for their respite and postponement so that perhaps God would bring forth from their loins someone who would worship Him and not associate anything with Him. And likewise it happened, for among those mentioned were those who converted to Islam after that and their Islam was good, even Abdullah ibn Umayyah who followed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him what he said. He converted to Islam completely and repented to God Almighty. God the Almighty said: Or you have a house of gold. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: It is gold. It is also in the reading of Ibn Masoud: Or you have a house of gold. “Or you ascend into the heaven.” That is, you ascend a ladder while we watch you. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book that we can read. Mujahid said: That is, written in it for each one is a scroll. This is a book from God to so-and-so. It is placed at his head in the morning. God the Almighty said: “Say: Glory be to my Lord. Am I anything but a human messenger?” That is, He is exalted and sanctified that anyone should precede Him in any matter of His authority and kingdom. Rather, He is the Doer of whatever He wills. If He wills, He will answer you in what you asked for, and if He wills, He will not answer you. I am only a messenger to you, conveying to you the messages of my Lord and advising you, and I have done that. Your affair in what you asked is up to God the Almighty. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Ali ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Yahya ibn Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Zajar, on the authority of Ali ibn Yazid, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “My Lord, the Almighty, offered to make the plain of Mecca into gold for me, so I said: No, O Lord, but I will be full one day and hungry one day - or something like that - so when I am hungry I will supplicate to You and remember You, and when I am full I will praise You and thank You.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Az-Zuhd on the authority of Suwaid ibn Nasr on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, and he said: This is a good hadith, and Ali ibn Yazid is considered weak in hadith.
17:93: Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, an old man from Egypt who came forty-some years ago told me on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi’ah, Abu Sufyan bin Harb, a man from Banu Abd al-Dar, Abu al-Bukhtari, the brother of Banu Asad, al-Aswad bin al-Muttalib bin Asad, Zam’ah bin al-Aswad, al-Walid bin al-Mughira, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah, Umayyah bin Khalaf, al-‘As bin Wa’il, Nabih and Munabbih, the sons of al-Hajjaj al-Sahmiyyin, gathered, or whoever gathered from them, after sunset at the back of the Kaaba. Some of them said to each other: Send to Muhammad and speak to him and argue with him until they find an excuse for him. So they sent to him that the nobles of your people have gathered to speak to you. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them quickly, thinking that they had changed their mind about him, and they were on them. He was keen on their guidance and was saddened by their trouble until he sat with them. They said: “O Muhammad, we have been sent to you to excuse you. By God, we do not know of any Arab man who has brought upon his people what you have brought upon your people. You have insulted the fathers, denounced the religion, belittled dreams, insulted the gods, and divided the community. There is no ugly thing that I have not done between us and you. If you have only come with this hadith seeking money, we will collect for you from our money until you are the wealthiest among us. If you are only seeking honor among us, we will make you our leader. If you want a kingdom, we will make you our king. If this one who brings you what he brings you is a vision that you see has overcome you - and they used to call the follower of the jinn the visionary - then perhaps that is what we have spent our money seeking medicine until we cure you of it or excuse you.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I do not have what you say. I have not come to you with what I have come to you seeking your money, nor honor among you, nor kingship over you. Rather, God has sent me to you as a messenger and revealed to me a book and commanded me to be for you.” As a bearer of good tidings and a warner, I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you. If you accept from me what I have brought to you, then it is your portion in this world and the Hereafter, and if you reject it, I will be patient for the sake of God’s command until God judges between me and you.” Or as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in submission. They said: “O Muhammad, if you do not accept what we have offered you, then you have come to know that there is no one among the people who has a narrower land than us, nor less wealth, nor a harsher life than us. So ask your Lord who sent you with what He sent you with, so that He may remove these mountains that have become narrow for us, and expand our land for us and cause rivers to gush forth in it like the rivers of Syria and Iraq, and send to us those of our fathers who have passed away, and let among those He sends to us be Qusayy ibn Kilab, for he was a truthful old man. So we will ask them about what you say, is it true or false? If you do what we ask you and they believe you, then we will believe you and know by that your status with God, and that He sent you as a Messenger as you say.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: This is not what I was sent for. I have come to you from God with what He sent me with. I have conveyed to you what I was sent with. If you accept it, it is your portion in this world and the hereafter. If you reject it, I will be patient for God’s sake until God judges between me and you. They said: If you do not do this for us, then take it for yourself. Ask your Lord to send an angel who will confirm what you say and will return to us on your behalf. Ask Him and He will make for you gardens, treasures, and palaces of gold and silver, and make you independent of what we see you seeking. You stand in the markets and seek a living as we seek it, so that we may know the excellence of your position with your Lord if you are a Messenger as you claim. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: I will not do this. I am not one who asks his Lord for this. I was not sent to you with this, but God sent me as a bearer of good tidings and a warner. If you accept what I have come to you with, it is your portion in this world and the hereafter. If you reject it, I will be patient for God’s sake until God judges between me and you. They said: Then cause the sky to fall as you claim. If your Lord wills, He will do that. We will not believe in you unless you do that. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: That is up to God. If He wills, He will do that to you. They said: O Muhammad, does your Lord not know that we will sit with you and ask you about what we asked you about and request from you what we request, and then He will come to you and teach you what you have brought us back, and inform you of what He will do to us if we do not accept what you have brought us? It has reached us that only a man in Yamamah called Ar-Rahman is teaching you this, and by God, we will never believe in Ar-Rahman. We have excused ourselves to you, O Muhammad. By God, we will not leave you and what you have done to us until we perish or you perish. One of them said: We worship the angels, who are the daughters of God. And their speaker said: We will not believe you until you bring God and the angels before you. When they said that, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rose from them, and with him rose Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah bin Al-Mughira bin Abdullah bin Umar bin Makhzum, who was the son of his paternal aunt Atikah bint Abdul Muttalib. He said: O Muhammad, your people offered you what they offered you, but you did not accept it from them. Then they asked you for themselves things so that they would know your status with God, but you did not do that. Then they asked you to hasten for them what you threaten them with of punishment. By God, I will never believe in you until you take a ladder to the sky, then ascend it while I watch until you reach it and bring with you an open document and with you four angels who will testify that you are as you say. By God, if you did that, you would think that I would not believe you. Then he turned away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned back to his family, sad and sorry for what he had missed out on from what he had hoped for from his people when they called him, and for what he saw of their distancing from him. And this is how Ziyad bin Abdullah Al-Bakkai on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Some of the people of knowledge told me on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned something similar. And this council for which these people had gathered, if God had known that they were asking for that in order to seek guidance, they would have responded to him, but He knew that they were only asking for that out of disbelief and stubbornness towards Him. So it was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you wish, we will give them what they asked for, and if they disbelieve, I will punish them with a punishment that I have not punished anyone in the worlds with, and if you wish, you will open for them the door of repentance and mercy? He said: Rather, the door of repentance and mercy will be opened for them, as was mentioned previously in the hadiths of Ibn Abbas and Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam, when God the Almighty said: “And nothing prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We do not send signs except as a warning.” And God the Almighty said: “And they said, ‘What is this Messenger who eats food and walks in the markets? Why is an angel not sent down to him so that he may be with him as a warner? Or a treasure is thrown down to him, or there is for him a garden from which he may eat?’ And the wrongdoers said, ‘You are not following except a man bewitched.’ Look how they strike for you examples, but they have gone astray and cannot find a way. Blessed is He who, if He wills, can grant you better than that - gardens beneath which rivers flow and can grant you palaces. Rather, they have denied the Hour, and We have prepared for whoever denies the Hour a Blaze.” And the Almighty’s saying: Until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth. The spring is the flowing eye. They asked Him to cause a flowing eye to gush forth for them in the land of the Hijaz here and there, and that is easy for God, the Almighty. If He had willed, He would have done it and answered them on all that they asked and requested of Him, but He knew that they would not be guided, as the Almighty said: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign came to them until they saw the painful punishment. And the Almighty said: And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We had gathered together before them all things before, they would not have believed. The verse. And the Almighty said: Or the sky will fall as you claimed meaning that you promised us that on the Day of Resurrection the sky will split and fall and its edges will hang down, so make that in this world and make it fall in pieces, i.e. in pieces, like His saying: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky verse. And likewise the people of Shu’ayb asked Him and said: Let a piece of the sky fall upon us, if you are of the truthful. So God punished them with the punishment of the Day of the Shadow, for it was the punishment of a great day. As for the Prophet of Mercy and the Prophet of Repentance, who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, he asked for their respite and postponement so that perhaps God would bring forth from their loins someone who would worship Him and not associate anything with Him. And likewise it happened, for among those mentioned were those who converted to Islam after that and their Islam was good, even Abdullah ibn Umayyah who followed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him what he said. He converted to Islam completely and repented to God Almighty. God the Almighty said: Or you have a house of gold. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: It is gold. It is also in the reading of Ibn Masoud: Or you have a house of gold. “Or you ascend into the heaven.” That is, you ascend a ladder while we watch you. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book that we can read. Mujahid said: That is, written in it for each one is a scroll. This is a book from God to so-and-so. It is placed at his head in the morning. God the Almighty said: “Say: Glory be to my Lord. Am I anything but a human messenger?” That is, He is exalted and sanctified that anyone should precede Him in any matter of His authority and kingdom. Rather, He is the Doer of whatever He wills. If He wills, He will answer you in what you asked for, and if He wills, He will not answer you. I am only a messenger to you, conveying to you the messages of my Lord and advising you, and I have done that. Your affair in what you asked is up to God the Almighty. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Ali ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Yahya ibn Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Zajar, on the authority of Ali ibn Yazid, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “My Lord, the Almighty, offered to make the plain of Mecca into gold for me, so I said: No, O Lord, but I will be full one day and hungry one day - or something like that - so when I am hungry I will supplicate to You and remember You, and when I am full I will praise You and thank You.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Az-Zuhd on the authority of Suwaid ibn Nasr on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, and he said: This is a good hadith, and Ali ibn Yazid is considered weak in hadith.
17:94: God Almighty says: And what prevented the people meaning most of them from believing and following the messengers except their astonishment at the sending of human beings as messengers, as God Almighty says: Is it a wonder to the people that We inspired a man from among themselves, ‘Warn the people and give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing with their Lord?’ And God Almighty says: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said, ‘Is it human beings who guide us?’ Pharaoh and his chiefs said, Shall we believe in two men like ourselves, while their people worship us? And the nations said to their messengers, “You are only men like us. You want to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship. So bring us a clear authority.” There are many verses about this. Then the Almighty said, drawing attention to His kindness and mercy towards His servants, that He sends to them a Messenger from their own kind so that they may understand from him, enabling them to address him and converse with him. Had He sent to mankind a Messenger from among the angels, they would not have been able to confront him or learn from him, as the Almighty said, God has conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves. And the Almighty said, There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. And the Almighty said, “Just as We have sent among you a Messenger from among yourselves, reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you that which you did not know. So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.” And for this reason He said here, “Say, ‘If there were angels walking about in peace and security on the earth,’” meaning as you are on it, We would have sent down to them from the sky. A king and a messenger, meaning from their kind. And since you were human beings, We sent among you Our messengers from among you, as kindness and mercy.

And the nations said to their messengers, “You are only men like us. You want to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship. So bring us a clear authority.” There are many verses about this. So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.” And for this reason He said here, “Say, ‘If there were angels walking about in peace and security on the earth,’” meaning as you are on it, We would have sent down to them from the sky. A king and a messenger, meaning from their kind. And since you were human beings, We sent among you Our messengers from among you, as kindness and mercy.
17:96: The Almighty says, guiding His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the argument against his people regarding the truth of what he brought them: He is a witness over me and over you, and He knows what I have brought you. So if I were lying about him, We would not take the most severe revenge on me, as the Almighty says: And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta. And His statement, Indeed, He is ever, of His servants, Knowing and Seeing, means He is All-Knowing of them, who deserves favor, kindness, and guidance, and who deserves misery, misguidance, and deviation. For this reason He said:
17:97: God Almighty says, informing about His control over His creation and the implementation of His rule and that there is no one to follow Him, that whomever He guides, there is none to misguide him, and whomever He misguides, you will find no protectors besides Him, as He said: He whom God guides is the rightly guided, and he whom He misguides, you will find no protector to guide him. And His statement: And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces. Imam Ahmad said, Ibn Numayr told us, Ismail told us on the authority of Nafi’ who said: I heard Anas bin Malik say: “It was said: O Messenger of God, how will people be gathered on their faces? He said: He who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces.” And they included it in the two Sahihs. Imam Ahmad also said: Al-Walid bin Jami’ Al-Qurashi narrated to us, Abu Al-Tayyal Amir bin Wathilah narrated to us, on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Asid, who said: Abu Dharr stood up and said: O Banu Ghifar, speak and do not swear, for the Truthful, the Trusted One narrated to me that people will be gathered in three groups: a group riding, eating and drinking, a group walking and striving, and a group whom the angels will drag on their faces and gather into the Fire. One of them said: We know these two, but what about those who walk and striving? He said: God the Almighty will cast a scourge upon the back until there is no back left, so that if a man has an impressive garden and he gives it to a camel with a saddle, he will not be able to do it. And His saying: blind means they do not see, dumb means they do not speak, deaf means they do not hear, and this will be in one state rather than another as a reward for them, just as they were in this world dumb, blind and deaf to the truth, so they will pass through their place of assembly with that which they need most, their abode meaning their place of return and their destination, Hell, whenever it subsides Ibn Abbas said: it calms down, and Mujahid said: it is extinguished, We will increase them in blazing fire meaning flame, blazing and embers, as He said: So taste, for We will not increase you except in torment.
17:98: God Almighty says: This is what We have rewarded them with of resurrection while blind, dumb and deaf. It is their reward that they deserve, because they denied Our signs meaning Our evidence and proof, and they ruled out the occurrence of resurrection. “And they said, ‘When we are bones and dust’ meaning rotten and decayed, ‘will we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?’ meaning after what we have become of decay, destruction, dispersion and going on earth, will we be returned a second time?” So God, the Almighty, argued with them and alerted them to His ability to do that, as He created the heavens and the earth, so His ability to bring them back is easier than that, as He said: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. And He said: Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth and was not weary in their creation, is able to give life to the dead? At this point, he was confused and said: “Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, and He is the Creator, the Knowing. * His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, “Be,” and it is.” To the end of the surah. And He said here: Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them? That is, on the Day of Resurrection, He will bring their bodies back and create them another creation, just as He began them. And His statement: And has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt means that He has appointed for their return and their resurrection from their graves a set term and a determined period that must come to an end, as God, the Almighty, said: And We do not delay it except for a numbered term. And His statement: But the wrongdoers refused meaning after the proof was established against them except to be ungrateful except to persist in their falsehood and misguidance.
