And His statement: But the wrongdoers refused meaning after the proof was established against them except to be ungrateful except to persist in their falsehood and misguidance.
17:100: The Almighty says to His Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: Say to them, O Muhammad, if you, O people, had the power to dispose of God’s treasures, you would withhold them for fear of spending. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: That is, poverty, for fear that you will waste them even though they will never be empty or exhausted, because this is part of your nature and disposition. That is why He said: And man is ever niggardly. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: That is, miserly and withholding. And God Almighty said: Or do they have a share in the kingdom? Then they would not give the people even a speck. That is, if they had a share in God’s kingdom, they would not give anyone anything, not even the amount of a speck. And God Almighty describes man as he is, except for those whom God has guided and bestowed success upon, for miserliness, impatience, and panic are characteristics of him, as God Almighty said: “Indeed, man was created impatient. When evil touches him, impatient. And when good touches him, withholding [it], except for the praying ones.” There are many parallels to this in the Noble Qur’an, and this indicates his generosity, goodness, and kindness. It was mentioned in the two Sahihs: “The hand of God is full, and no spending by night or day diminishes it. Have you seen what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? What is in His right hand has not diminished.”
17:101: God Almighty tells us that He sent Moses with nine clear signs, which are the conclusive evidence of the truth of his prophethood and his truthfulness in what he told about the one who sent him to Pharaoh. They are the staff, the hand, the years, the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood. These are detailed signs, as Ibn Abbas said. Muhammad bin Kaab said: It is the hand and the staff, and the five in Al-A’raf, Al-Tamsa and Al-Hajar. Ibn Abbas also said, as did Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Sha’bi and Qatadah: It is his hand and staff, the years, the loss of fruits, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood. This statement is clear, obvious, good and strong. Al-Hasan Al-Basri made the years and the loss of fruits one, and he believed that the ninth is the staff swallowing what they fabricated. So they were arrogant and were a criminal people. That is, despite these signs and their witnessing them, they disbelieved in them and denied them, and their souls were certain of them unjustly and arrogantly, and they did not work on them. So likewise, if we had answered those who asked you what they asked, and said, We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, and so on, they would not have responded nor believed unless God willed, as Pharaoh said to Moses when he saw from him what he saw of these signs: Indeed, I think, O Moses, that you are bewitched. It was said: meaning a magician, and God Almighty knows best. These nine verses mentioned by these imams are what is meant here, and they are what is meant in the words of God the Almighty: “And throw down your staff. But when he saw it writhing as if it were a serpent, he turned back in flight and did not look back. O Moses, fear not. Indeed, no messengers fear in My presence, except one who has done wrong and then substituted evil for good. Indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful. And put your hand into the bosom of your garment; it will come out white without disease. These are nine signs to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they were a people of wickedness.” So He mentioned these two verses, the staff and the hand, and explained the remaining verses in Surat Al-A’raf and separated them. And Moses, peace be upon him, was given many other signs, including striking the stone with the staff, and the water coming out of it, and shading them with clouds and sending down manna and quails, and other things that were given to the Children of Israel after they left the land of Egypt. However, He mentioned here the nine signs that Pharaoh and his people from the people of Egypt witnessed, and they were an argument against them, so they opposed them and defied them out of disbelief and denial. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Yazid told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Salamah narrating on the authority of Safwan ibn ‘Assal al-Muradi, may God be pleased with him, who said: A Jew said to his companion: Let us go to this prophet so that we may ask him about this verse: And We gave Moses nine clear signs. He said: Do not call him a prophet, for if he heard you, he would have four eyes. For this reason, He said: So that you may recite it to the people, meaning so that you may convey it to the people and recite it to them, meaning over a period of time, meaning slowly, and We revealed it gradually, meaning little by little.

That is why He said, Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, meaning from the righteous people of the Book who held fast to their book and established it and did not change it or distort it, when it is recited to them, this Qur’an, they fall upon their chins, the plural of chin is the lower part of the face, in prostration, meaning to God Almighty in thanks for what He has bestowed upon them of making them worthy of realizing this Messenger to whom this book was revealed. That is why they say, Glory be to our Lord, meaning in glorification and reverence for His perfect power and that He does not break the promise He promised them on the tongues of the prophets who came before the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. That is why they say, Glory be to our Lord, if the promise of our Lord is true. “And they fall upon their chins weeping,” meaning in submission to God Almighty and in faith and belief in His Book and His Messenger. And He increases them in humility, meaning in faith and submission, as He said: And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness. And His saying: And they fall upon their chins, is a conjunction of one attribute with another attribute, not a conjunction of prostration with prostration, as the poet said: To the venerable king, the son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowded place

17:110: God the Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who deny the attribute of mercy to God the Almighty, who forbid calling Him the Most Gracious, "Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious, whichever you call upon, to Him belong the best names." That is, there is no difference between your calling upon Him by the name of God or by the name of the Most Gracious, for He is the Possessor of the best names, as God the Almighty says: "He is God, other than whom there is no god, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. He is God, other than whom there is no god, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Guardian, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Proud. Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him. He is God, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner. To Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Him." The verse. Makhul narrated that a man from the polytheists heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying in his al-Sajdah 32:"O Most Gracious, O Most Merciful." He said: He claims that he is calling upon one, but he is calling upon two, so God revealed this verse. This is also narrated from Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Jarir narrated them both. And His saying: And do not recite your prayer aloud the verse Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Abu Bishr told us on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was hiding in Mecca, And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice he said: When he prayed with his companions, he would raise his voice with the Qur’an, and when the polytheists heard that, they cursed the Qur’an and cursed the One who revealed it and the One who brought it. He said: So God, the Most High, said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not recite your prayer aloud meaning your recitation so that the polytheists hear and curse the Qur’an, nor in a low voice from your companions, so that they do not hear the Qur’an until they learn it from you, and seek a way between that. They included it in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Bishr Ja’far bin Iyas on his authority, and Ad-Dahhak narrated it likewise on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he added: When he migrated to Medina, that was dropped, so he could do whichever of those things he wanted. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Dawud ibn al-Husayn told me on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited the Qur’an aloud while he was praying, they would disperse from him and refuse to listen to him. When a man wanted to hear some of what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was reciting while he was praying, he would eavesdrop on them out of fear of them. When he saw that they knew that he was listening, he would leave for fear of harming them and would not hear. If he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) lowered his voice, those listening would not hear anything of his recitation. So God revealed: And do not recite your prayer aloud lest they disperse from you. And do not recite it in a low voice lest the one who wanted to hear from those who eavesdrop on them hear, perhaps he might be moved by some of what he heard and benefit from it. And seek a way between that. And this is what Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah said: This verse was revealed about recitation in prayer. Shu’bah said on the authority of al-Ash’ath ibn Abi Sulaym on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Hilal on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. He did not lower his voice to those who could hear him. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Salma bin Alqamah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, who said: I was informed that when Abu Bakr prayed and recited, he lowered his voice, and that Umar raised his voice. It was said to Abu Bakr: Why do you do this? He said: I am communing with my Lord, the Almighty, and He knows my need. It was said: Well done. It was said to Umar: Why do you do this? He said: I drive away Satan and wake up the sleepy. It was said: Well done. When the verse, And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, but seek a way between the two, was revealed, it was said to Abu Bakr: Raise your voice a little, and it was said to Umar: Lower your voice a little. Ash’ath bin Suwar said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was revealed about supplication. And this is how Ath-Thawri and Malik narrated it on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that it was revealed about supplication. And this is what Mujahid, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Abu Ayyad, Makhul, and Urwah bin Az-Zubayr said. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Ibn Ayyash Al-Amiri on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, who said: Whenever a Bedouin from Banu Tamim greeted the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would say: O God, grant us camels and children. He said: Then this verse was revealed: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice. Another statement Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa’ib told us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: This verse was revealed regarding the testimony of faith: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice. Hafs said the same on the authority of Ash’ath ibn Suwar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, something similar. Another saying Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, he said: Do not pray to show off to people and do not abandon it out of fear of people. And Al-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, he said: Do not make it good in public and bad in secret. And this is how Abd Al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Al-Hasan on his authority, and Hisham on the authority of Awf on his authority on his authority, and Saeed on the authority of Qatadah on his authority likewise. Another statement Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding his statement: And seek a way between that, he said: The People of the Book would lower their voices, then one of them would recite the letter aloud, and he would shout it out and they would shout it out behind him, so he forbade him from shouting as these shouted, and from lowering his voice as the people lowered their voices, then the way between that was what Gabriel prescribed for him in prayer. And His statement: “And say: Praise be to God, who has not taken a son,” when the Most High affirmed for Himself the most beautiful names, He cleared Himself of contradictions, saying: “And say: Praise be to God, who has not taken a son and has no partner in dominion,” rather He is God, the One, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. And He has no protector out of humiliation, meaning He is not humiliated, so He does not need to have a protector, minister, or advisor. Rather, He, the Most High, is the Creator of all things alone, with no partner, and He is their Administrator and Determiner alone, with no partner. Mujahid said about His statement: And He has no protector out of humiliation, He did not ally with anyone and did not seek anyone’s support. And glorify Him with utmost glorification, meaning He magnified Him and exalted Him above what the unjust and aggressive people say, with great exaltation. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Abu Sakhr told me on the authority of Al-Qurazi that he used to say about this verse: “And say: Praise be to God, who has not taken a son” 1:13. He said: The Jews and Christians say: God has taken a son, and the Arabs said: At your service, you have no partner except a partner who is yours, you own him and what he owns. The Sabians and Magians said: Were it not for the allies of God, he would have been humiliated. So God revealed this verse: “And say: Praise be to God, who has not taken a son, and has no partner in dominion, and has no protector out of humiliation. And glorify Him with great glorification.” He also said: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatadah, who mentioned to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to teach his family this verse: Praise be to God, who has not taken a son 1:13, the young and the old among his family. I said: It has been reported in a hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called this verse the verse of glory, and in some of the reports it is said that if it is recited in a house at night, it will be afflicted with theft or a calamity, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Bishr bin Sayhan al-Basri told us, Harb bin Maymun told us, Musa bin Ubaidah al-Zubaidi told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka`b al-Qurazi on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “I went out with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his hand was in my hand, or my hand was in his, and he came upon a man who was in poor condition and said: ‘O so-and-so, what has happened to you that I see? ’ He said: ‘Illness and harm, O Messenger of God. ’ He said: ‘Shall I not teach you words that will remove illness and harm from you? ’ He said: ‘I would not be pleased with them if I were to witness Badr or Uhud with you. ’ He said: ‘The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed and said: ‘Do the people of Badr and Uhud attain what the contented poor attain? ’ Abu Hurayrah said: ‘O Messenger of God, teach me. ’ He said: ‘Then say, O Abu Hurayrah, I put my trust in the Ever-Living who does not die. Praise be to God who has not taken a son, and has no partner in the kingdom, and has no protector from humiliation, and glorify Him greatly. ’ He said: ‘Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to me and my condition had improved. ’ He said to me: ‘Mahim. ’ He said: ‘I said: O Messenger of God, I have not ceased to say the words that you taught me. Its chain of transmission is weak, and there is something objectionable in its text. And God knows best. The end of the interpretation of Surat Subhan. Praise and thanks be to God.
